tooling.name: ToolSettings

setters.name: env
setters.doc: Merge additional environment variables for the process.

setters.name: cwd
setters.doc: Set the working directory for the process.

setters.name: noThrow
setters.doc: Do not throw on a non-zero exit; inspect `code` on the output instead.

setters.name: quiet
setters.doc: Suppress live stdout/stderr streaming to the terminal.

setters.name: killAfter
setters.doc:
Kill the tool if it runs longer than `ms` milliseconds, raising a
`CommandTimeoutError`. Fires even under noThrow.

setters.name: maxCapturedBytes
setters.doc:
Cap how much of **each** captured stream the run keeps in memory, in bytes
(default 8 MiB). Once the cap is reached the oldest bytes are dropped,
`CommandOutput.truncated` is set, and `CommandOutput.text` prefixes a
notice. Raise it for a tool whose whole output must be parsed — a coverage
report, a `--json` dump — and lower it to bound a chatty one. Live
streaming to the terminal is never capped.

setters.name: toolPath
setters.doc: Override the binary to run (e.g. an absolute path to the tool).

setters.name: fromNodeModules
setters.doc:
Resolve the binary npx-style: walk up from the working directory looking
for `node_modules/.bin/<tool>`, falling back to `PATH` on a miss. Overrides
both the wrapper default and the ambient `ZUKE_TOOL_RESOLUTION`. Has no
effect once toolPath is set (an explicit path always wins).

setters.name: fromPath
setters.doc: Resolve the binary from `PATH` only, ignoring any `node_modules/.bin`.

setters.name: args
setters.doc: Escape hatch: append raw arguments after all typed options.

tooling.name: DynamicToolSettings
tooling.doc:
Fluent settings for a defineTool tool: build the argv with
DynamicToolSettings.arg/DynamicToolSettings.flag/DynamicToolSettings.option (in call order), plus all the shared chainers
(`cwd`, `env`, `noThrow`, `quiet`, `toolPath`, `args`).

setters.name: arg
setters.doc: Append raw positional/argument tokens.

setters.name: flag
setters.doc: Append a boolean flag, e.g. `flag("verbose")` → `--verbose` (or `-v`).

setters.name: option
setters.doc: Append a flag and its value as two tokens, e.g. `--output dist`.

tooling.name: SubcommandSettings
tooling.doc:
Base for a wrapper over a CLI organised into **subcommand groups** — a command
path built with command plus repeatable `--flag [value]` options built
with flag. The agent and cloud wrappers (`gh`, `gcloud`, `claude`,
`gemini`, `codex`) share this shape; each sets its binary via
ToolSettings.defaultTool and, when needed, a fixed prefix via
leadingTokens or between-command global flags via middleTokens.

The argv is assembled as
`[...leadingTokens(), ...command, ...middleTokens(), ...flags]`, keeping every
token a discrete argv entry so command construction stays injection-free.

setters.name: command
setters.doc: Append command-path tokens — the group, verb, and operands — in order.

setters.name: flag
setters.doc:
Add an arbitrary flag. With a value it renders `--name value`; without one
the bare `--name`. Repeatable.

packages.name: deno
packages.summary: `@zuke/deno` — typed `DenoTasks` wrappers for the `deno` CLI, for use in Zuke build targets.

tasks.name: DenoTasks
tasks.doc: Typed task functions for the `deno` CLI.

tasks.name: run
tasks.doc: Run a script: `deno run`.

tasks.name: test
tasks.doc:
Run tests: `deno test`. Reports the run's counts into the running
target's row of the build summary (`// Tests: 837 · Passed: 837 ·
Failed: 0`), read from deno's own result line — see
DenoTestSettings.

tasks.name: check
tasks.doc: Type-check files: `deno check`.

tasks.name: fmt
tasks.doc: Format files: `deno fmt`.

tasks.name: lint
tasks.doc: Lint files: `deno lint`.

tasks.name: doc
tasks.doc: Generate documentation: `deno doc`.

tasks.name: cache
tasks.doc: Warm the module cache: `deno cache`.

tasks.name: coverage
tasks.doc: Report coverage: `deno coverage`.

tasks.name: install
tasks.doc: Install a script or executable: `deno install`.

tasks.name: publish
tasks.doc: Publish a package to JSR: `deno publish`.

tasks.name: task
tasks.doc: Run a deno.json task: `deno task`.

tasks.name: serve
tasks.doc: Run a server: `deno serve`.

tasks.name: eval
tasks.doc: Evaluate a snippet: `deno eval`.

tasks.name: bench
tasks.doc: Run benchmarks: `deno bench`.

tasks.name: compile
tasks.doc: Build a self-contained executable: `deno compile`.

tasks.name: clean
tasks.doc: Remove the cache directory: `deno clean`.

tasks.name: info
tasks.doc: Report on a module or the caches: `deno info`.

tasks.name: init
tasks.doc: Scaffold a new project: `deno init`.

tasks.name: upgrade
tasks.doc: Upgrade the deno executable: `deno upgrade`.

tasks.name: add
tasks.doc: Add dependencies: `deno add`.

tasks.name: remove
tasks.doc: Remove dependencies: `deno remove`.

tasks.name: uninstall
tasks.doc: Uninstall a dependency or global executable: `deno uninstall`.

tasks.name: outdated
tasks.doc: Report outdated dependencies: `deno outdated`.

tasks.name: why
tasks.doc: Explain why a package is installed: `deno why`.

tasks.name: ci
tasks.doc: Install strictly from the lockfile: `deno ci`.

tasks.name: approveScripts
tasks.doc: Approve npm lifecycle scripts: `deno approve-scripts`.

tasks.name: bumpVersion
tasks.doc: Bump the version in the manifest: `deno bump-version`.

tasks.name: pack
tasks.doc: Build an npm-compatible tarball: `deno pack`.

tasks.name: moduleGraph
tasks.doc:
The module graph rooted at a file, parsed from `deno info --json`.

A reader, not a gate: it returns the graph rather than printing it, so a
build can assert on what its entry point actually pulls in.

tasks.name: cacheInfo
tasks.doc: The toolchain's cache locations, parsed from `deno info --json`.

tasks.name: DenoDeployTasks
tasks.doc: Typed task functions for `deno deploy`.

tasks.name: deploy
tasks.doc: Deploy a directory to an application: `deno deploy`.

tasks.name: create
tasks.doc: Create an application: `deno deploy create`.

tasks.name: envList
tasks.doc: List an application's variables: `deno deploy env list`.

tasks.name: envAdd
tasks.doc: Add a variable: `deno deploy env add`.

tasks.name: envUpdateValue
tasks.doc: Change a variable's value: `deno deploy env update-value`.

tasks.name: envUpdateContexts
tasks.doc: Change the contexts a variable applies in: `deno deploy env update-contexts`.

tasks.name: envDelete
tasks.doc: Delete a variable: `deno deploy env delete`.

tasks.name: envLoad
tasks.doc: Load variables from a `.env` file: `deno deploy env load`.

tasks.name: logs
tasks.doc: Print an application's logs: `deno deploy logs`.

tasks.name: deploymentsList
tasks.doc: List an application's deployments: `deno deploy deployments list`.

tasks.name: appsList
tasks.doc: List an organization's applications: `deno deploy apps list`.

tasks.name: appsGet
tasks.doc: Show an application, with its production URL: `deno deploy apps get`.

tasks.name: orgsList
tasks.doc: List the organizations the token reaches: `deno deploy orgs list`.

tasks.name: whoami

settings.name: DenoSettings
settings.doc: Base for all `deno` subcommand settings: binary is the deno running here.

settings.name: DenoDeployCommandSettings
settings.doc:
Base for all `deno deploy` settings. Each subcommand names its command path
and its own arguments; the shared flags go between them.

setters.name: token
setters.doc:
The Deno Deploy access token. It is passed in the `DENO_DEPLOY_TOKEN`
environment variable rather than on the command line, so it never shows
in a process listing or an error's command line, and it is registered
with the run's redactor. Without it, the CLI reads `DENO_DEPLOY_TOKEN`
from the build's own environment.

setters.name: config
setters.doc: The config file to read and write the org and app from (`--config`).

setters.name: json
setters.doc: Print one JSON object on stdout instead of human-readable output (`--json`).

setters.name: nonInteractive
setters.doc:
Fail instead of prompting, taking every value from flags or the
environment (`--non-interactive`). Use it in CI, where nothing can answer
a prompt.

setters.name: quietOutput
setters.doc: Suppress non-essential output (`--quiet`).

settings.name: DenoDeployOrgSettings
settings.doc: Base for the `deno deploy` commands scoped to an organization.

setters.name: org
setters.doc: The organization (`--org`).

settings.name: DenoDeployAppSettings
settings.doc: Base for the `deno deploy` commands scoped to an application.

setters.name: app
setters.doc: The application (`--app`).

settings.name: DenoDeployUploadSettings
settings.doc:
The flags shared by the commands that upload source from a local directory:
`deno deploy` and `deno deploy create`.

setters.name: root
setters.doc: The directory to upload (defaults to the working directory).

setters.name: ignore
setters.doc: Leave a path out of the upload (`--ignore`); repeatable.

setters.name: allowNodeModules
setters.doc: Include the `node_modules` directory in the upload (`--allow-node-modules`).

setters.name: noWait
setters.doc: Return once uploaded, without waiting for the build (`--no-wait`).

settings.name: DenoDeployCreateSettings
settings.doc: Settings for `deno deploy create`: create an application.

setters.name: dryRun
setters.doc: Validate the flags without creating the application (`--dry-run`).

setters.name: source
setters.doc: Where the source comes from (`--source`).

setters.name: repository
setters.doc: A GitHub source repository: `--owner` and `--repo`.

setters.name: appDirectory
setters.doc: The application's directory inside the source (`--app-directory`).

setters.name: doNotUseDetectedBuildConfig
setters.doc: Ignore the detected build configuration (`--do-not-use-detected-build-config`).

setters.name: frameworkPreset
setters.doc: The framework preset, e.g. `fresh` or `astro` (`--framework-preset`).

setters.name: installCommand
setters.doc: The install command (`--install-command`).

setters.name: buildCommand
setters.doc: The build command (`--build-command`).

setters.name: preDeployCommand
setters.doc: The command run before each deployment (`--pre-deploy-command`).

setters.name: runtimeMode
setters.doc: Whether the application is a server or static files (`--runtime-mode`).

setters.name: entrypoint
setters.doc: A dynamic application's entrypoint (`--entrypoint`).

setters.name: argument
setters.doc: An argument for a dynamic application's entrypoint (`--arguments`); repeatable.

setters.name: workingDirectory
setters.doc: A dynamic application's working directory (`--working-directory`).

setters.name: staticDir
setters.doc: The directory a static application is served from (`--static-dir`).

setters.name: singlePageApp
setters.doc: Serve `index.html` for every path without a file (`--single-page-app`).

setters.name: buildTimeout
setters.doc: The build timeout, e.g. `10m` or `600s` (`--build-timeout`).

setters.name: buildMemoryLimit
setters.doc: The build memory limit in megabytes (`--build-memory-limit`).

setters.name: region
setters.doc: The region to deploy to (`--region`).

settings.name: DenoDeploySettings
settings.doc: Settings for `deno deploy`: upload a directory to an application.

setters.name: prod
setters.doc: Deploy straight to production rather than as a preview (`--prod`).

setters.name: variable
setters.doc: The variable to delete; required.

settings.name: DenoDeployEnvLoadSettings
settings.doc: Settings for `deno deploy env load`: load variables from a `.env` file.

setters.name: file
setters.doc: The `.env` file to load; required.

setters.name: nonSecret
setters.doc: A key in the file to store as a plain value, not a secret (`--non-secrets`); repeatable.

setters.name: replace
setters.doc: Replace variables that already exist (`--replace`).

setters.name: skipExisting
setters.doc: Keep variables that already exist (`--skip-existing`).

setters.name: variable
setters.doc: The variable to update; required.

setters.name: context
setters.doc: A context the variable applies in, e.g. `production`; repeatable.

settings.name: DenoDeployEnvValueSettings
settings.doc:
Settings for `deno deploy env add` and `deno deploy env update-value`.

The value is a positional argument, so one that starts with `-` would be
read as a flag and is refused; load such a value from a file with
`DenoDeployTasks.envLoad` instead.

setters.name: variable
setters.doc: The variable to set; required.

setters.name: value
setters.doc: The variable's value; required, unless set by secretValue.

setters.name: secretValue
setters.doc:
A secret value: masked in the build's logs and errors, and for `add`
stored as a secret (`--secret`).

settings.name: DenoDeployAppsGetSettings
settings.doc: Settings for `deno deploy apps get`: an application, with its URLs.

setters.name: limit
setters.doc: At most this many applications (`--limit`).

setters.name: limit
setters.doc: At most this many deployments (`--limit`).

setters.name: cursor
setters.doc: Continue from a previous `--json` page's cursor (`--cursor`).

setters.name: status
setters.doc: Only deployments with this status (`--status`).

setters.name: start
setters.doc: Logs from this timestamp on, e.g. `2026-01-01T00:00:00Z` (`--start`).

setters.name: end
setters.doc: Logs up to this timestamp; needs start (`--end`).

setters.name: once
setters.doc:
Print the logs available now and exit, instead of following them
(`--once`). Without it the command streams until stopped, so a build
almost always wants this.

settings.name: DenoDeployQuerySettings
settings.doc:
Settings for `deno deploy orgs list` and `deno deploy whoami`, which take
neither an organization nor an application.

settings.name: DenoPermissionSettings
settings.doc: Base for subcommands that accept `--allow-*` permission flags.

setters.name: allowAll
setters.doc: Grant all permissions (`--allow-all`).

setters.name: allow
setters.doc: Grant one permission, optionally scoped to values (`--allow-read=a,b`).

setters.name: frozen
setters.doc:
Error out if the lockfile is out of date instead of silently updating it
(`--frozen`). Use it whenever the module graph must match the committed
`deno.lock` exactly — running an `npm:` tool in CI, say, so its transitive
tree stays pinned to the audited integrity hashes rather than being
resolved afresh. Named `frozen` — not `frozenLockfile` — to mirror the real
Deno CLI flag exactly. This is a deliberate divergence from
`PnpmSettings.frozenLockfile()` in `@zuke/pnpm`, which follows pnpm's own
flag name instead: guideline 7 (mirror the real CLI) takes priority over
cross-package naming symmetry.

settings.name: DenoEvalSettings
settings.doc:
Settings for `deno eval`.

The code is passed as a single argv entry by the shell layer, never
interpolated into a command string, so a value built from build parameters
cannot break out of it.

setters.name: code
setters.doc: The source to evaluate (required).

setters.name: print
setters.doc: Print the expression's result to stdout (`--print`).

setters.name: ext
setters.doc: Treat the source as this content type (`--ext`), rather than TypeScript.

setters.name: config
setters.doc: Use an explicit config file (`--config`).

setters.name: script
setters.doc: The script to run (required).

setters.name: scriptArgs
setters.doc: Arguments passed to the script (after the script path).

setters.name: config
setters.doc: Use an explicit config file (`--config`).

setters.name: noConfig
setters.doc: Discover no configuration file at all (`--no-config`).

setters.name: reload
setters.doc: Reload the module cache (`--reload`), optionally only these specifiers.

setters.name: lock
setters.doc: Use an explicit lockfile (`--lock`).

setters.name: noLock
setters.doc: Ignore the lockfile entirely (`--no-lock`).

setters.name: importMap
setters.doc: Load an import map from a file or URL (`--import-map`).

setters.name: cachedOnly
setters.doc: Resolve only from the cache (`--cached-only`), fetching nothing.

setters.name: noNpm
setters.doc: Do not resolve npm modules (`--no-npm`).

setters.name: noRemote
setters.doc: Do not resolve remote modules (`--no-remote`).

setters.name: nodeModulesDir
setters.doc: Set the node-modules management mode (`--node-modules-dir`).

setters.name: nodeModulesLinker
setters.doc: Set the npm linker mode (`--node-modules-linker`).

setters.name: vendor
setters.doc: Toggle the local vendor folder (`--vendor`).

setters.name: envFile
setters.doc: Load environment variables from a file (`--env-file`).

setters.name: cert
setters.doc: Load a certificate authority from a PEM file (`--cert`).

setters.name: location
setters.doc: Set `globalThis.location` (`--location`).

setters.name: seed
setters.doc: Seed the random number generator (`--seed`).

setters.name: v8Flags
setters.doc: Pass flags through to V8 (`--v8-flags`).

setters.name: conditions
setters.doc: Resolve npm package exports with these conditions (`--conditions`).

setters.name: preload
setters.doc: Execute these modules before the main one (`--preload`).

setters.name: require
setters.doc: Execute these CommonJS modules before the main one (`--require`).

setters.name: noCodeCache
setters.doc: Disable the V8 code cache (`--no-code-cache`).

setters.name: allowScripts
setters.doc: Permit npm lifecycle scripts, optionally only for these packages (`--allow-scripts`).

setters.name: typeCheck
setters.doc: Type-check before running (`--check`), optionally including remote code.

setters.name: noCheck
setters.doc: Skip type-checking (`--no-check`), optionally only for remote code.

setters.name: inspect
setters.doc: Activate the inspector (`--inspect`).

setters.name: inspectBrk
setters.doc: Activate the inspector and break at the start (`--inspect-brk`).

setters.name: inspectWait
setters.doc: Activate the inspector and wait for a debugger (`--inspect-wait`).

setters.name: watch
setters.doc: Restart when a watched file changes (`--watch`).

setters.name: watchHmr
setters.doc:
Watch with hot-module replacement (`--watch-hmr`), which only `deno run`
offers. It implies watching, so it replaces `--watch` rather than joining
it.

setters.name: watchExclude
setters.doc: Exclude paths from the watcher (`--watch-exclude`).

setters.name: noClearScreen
setters.doc: Keep previous output when re-running under `--watch` (`--no-clear-screen`).

settings.name: DenoServeSettings
settings.doc:
Settings for `deno serve`.

A server runs until it is stopped, so a build target that awaits this task
blocks forever. Give it a bound with `.killAfter(ms)` — for a smoke test
that the server starts — or run it from a target the build is not waiting
on.

setters.name: script
setters.doc: The module exporting the server's default handler (required).

setters.name: scriptArgs
setters.doc: Arguments passed to the server module (after the module path).

setters.name: port
setters.doc: The TCP port to serve on (`--port`); `0` picks a free one.

setters.name: host
setters.doc: The TCP address to serve on (`--host`), defaulting to all interfaces.

setters.name: parallel
setters.doc:
Run one server worker per available CPU (`--parallel`), or as many as
`DENO_JOBS` allows.

setters.name: open
setters.doc: Open a browser on the served address (`--open`).

setters.name: watch
setters.doc: Restart the server when a watched file changes (`--watch`).

setters.name: config
setters.doc: Use an explicit config file (`--config`).

setters.name: name
setters.doc: The task name from deno.json (required).

setters.name: taskArgs
setters.doc: Arguments forwarded to the task.

setters.name: recursive
setters.doc: Run the task in every workspace member (`--recursive`).

setters.name: filter
setters.doc:
Select the workspace members to run the task in (`--filter`). It selects
on its own — recursive is not a prerequisite.

setters.name: noPrefix
setters.doc:
Drop the per-member name prefix from output (`--no-prefix`), which a
recursive run adds. Useful when the output is being parsed rather than
read.

setters.name: evalShell
setters.doc:
Treat the task name as a shell command to evaluate (`--eval`) instead of
a task defined in the configuration file.

setters.name: taskCwd
setters.doc:
Run the task from this directory (`--cwd`).

Distinct from the inherited `cwd`, which sets the directory the `deno`
process itself is spawned in: this one moves only the task, leaving
configuration discovery anchored where deno started.

setters.name: config
setters.doc: Use an explicit config file (`--config`).

setters.name: frozen
setters.doc:
Error out if the lockfile is out of date (`--frozen`). See
DenoPermissionSettings.frozen for why the name mirrors the real
Deno flag rather than `PnpmSettings.frozenLockfile()`'s naming.

setters.name: lock
setters.doc: Use an explicit lockfile (`--lock`).

setters.name: noLock
setters.doc: Ignore the lockfile entirely (`--no-lock`).

setters.name: nodeModulesDir
setters.doc: Set the node-modules management mode (`--node-modules-dir`).

setters.name: nodeModulesLinker
setters.doc: Set the npm linker mode (`--node-modules-linker`).

setters.name: envFile
setters.doc: Load environment variables from a file (`--env-file`).

setters.name: paths
setters.doc: Restrict the run to specific benchmark files or directories.

setters.name: filter
setters.doc: Only run benchmarks whose name matches (`--filter`).

setters.name: json
setters.doc:
Report results as JSON (`--json`) rather than the table. Deno marks the
flag unstable, so treat the shape as subject to change between releases.

setters.name: noRun
setters.doc:
Cache the benchmark modules without running them (`--no-run`) — a cheap
way to prove the benchmarks still compile without paying to run them.

setters.name: permitNoFiles
setters.doc:
Succeed when no benchmark files matched (`--permit-no-files`) instead of
failing the target.

setters.name: ignore
setters.doc: Skip files matching these patterns (`--ignore`).

setters.name: config
setters.doc: Use an explicit config file (`--config`).

setters.name: dir
setters.doc: The coverage profile directory to report on.

setters.name: lcov
setters.doc: Emit lcov instead of the table report (`--lcov`).

setters.name: output
setters.doc: Write the report to a file (`--output=`).

setters.name: exclude
setters.doc: Exclude files matching the pattern (`--exclude=`).

setters.name: include
setters.doc: Report only on files matching the pattern (`--include=`).

setters.name: ignore
setters.doc: Skip files matching these patterns (`--ignore=`).

setters.name: html
setters.doc:
Write an HTML report into the profile directory (`--html`).

Mutually exclusive with lcov and with any threshold: given both,
deno emits the lcov and silently produces no HTML, so asking for both is
refused rather than quietly honoured in half.

setters.name: detailed
setters.doc: Report per-line detail alongside the summary table (`--detailed`).

setters.name: linesThreshold
setters.doc:
Fail the gate if line coverage is below `percent`. `deno coverage` has no
fail-under flag, so DenoTasks.coverage enforces this after parsing
the lcov report (and forces `--lcov` so a report exists to parse).

setters.name: branchesThreshold
setters.doc: Fail the gate if branch coverage is below `percent` (see linesThreshold).

setters.name: threshold
setters.doc: Fail the gate if either line or branch coverage is below `percent`.

setters.name: perFileThreshold
setters.doc:
Fail the gate if any single instrumented file's line coverage is below
`percent` — a per-file floor, so an under-tested file can't hide inside a
healthy aggregate (see CoverageThresholds.perFile, which notes the
`deno coverage` limit for files no test loads).

settings.name: DenoTestSettings
settings.doc:
Settings for `deno test`.

A run reports its counts into the running target's row of the build
summary — `// Tests: 837 · Passed: 837 · Failed: 0` — read from the result
line the pretty and dot reporters print (ignored tests count as `Skipped`);
a failed run reports too, so a red row says how many failed. The JUnit and TAP reporters print no such line,
so a run under `.reporter("junit")`/`.reporter("tap")` reports nothing.

setters.name: paths
setters.doc: Restrict the run to specific test files or directories.

setters.name: coverage
setters.doc: Collect coverage into the given profile directory (`--coverage=`).

setters.name: coverageRawDataOnly
setters.doc: Collect raw coverage data without generating a report (`--coverage-raw-data-only`).

setters.name: clean
setters.doc:
Empty the coverage profile directory before running (`--clean`), so a run
reports on its own tests rather than on whatever a previous run left.

The directory need not come from coverage: `DENO_COVERAGE_DIR`
sets it too, which is why this is not tied to that setter.

setters.name: filter
setters.doc: Only run tests whose name matches (`--filter`).

setters.name: parallel
setters.doc: Run test files in parallel (`--parallel`).

setters.name: failFast
setters.doc: Stop after `count` failures (`--fail-fast`), or after the first.

setters.name: doc
setters.doc: Evaluate the code blocks in JSDoc and Markdown as tests (`--doc`).

setters.name: noRun
setters.doc: Cache the test modules without running them (`--no-run`).

setters.name: shuffle
setters.doc:
Randomise test order (`--shuffle`), optionally with a fixed seed so a
failing order can be replayed.

setters.name: traceLeaks
setters.doc:
Trace the ops a test leaks (`--trace-leaks`). It costs run time and is
the only practical way to find which test leaked a pending op — the
flakiest class of failure a suite has.

setters.name: sanitizeOps
setters.doc: Require every async op started in a test to finish in it (`--sanitize-ops`).

setters.name: sanitizeResources
setters.doc: Require every resource opened in a test to be closed in it (`--sanitize-resources`).

setters.name: hideStacktraces
setters.doc: Omit stack traces from failure output (`--hide-stacktraces`).

setters.name: reporter
setters.doc: Select the console reporter (`--reporter`).

setters.name: junitPath
setters.doc:
Also write a JUnit XML report to `path` (`--junit-path`), whatever the
console reporter is — this is the file a CI test-report UI ingests.

setters.name: ext
setters.doc: Treat the inputs as this content type (`--ext`).

setters.name: token
setters.doc:
Authenticate with a token instead of interactive/OIDC auth (`--token`).

Registered with the run's redactor, so every *rendering* of the command
masks it — a dry-run echo, a failure message. That is as far as it goes:
`deno publish` accepts the token only as a flag, so the value still
reaches the child's argv, where `ps` and `/proc/<pid>/cmdline` expose it to
every other user on the host and to every process the build starts.

There is no environment variable to move it to. `DENO_AUTH_TOKENS` is not
one — it authenticates *module fetches*, not publishing.

Prefer passing no token at all. On GitHub Actions `deno publish` uses OIDC,
so the publish is authenticated by the workflow's identity and there is no
credential to expose; this repository's own publish does exactly that.

setters.name: setVersion
setters.doc:
Publish under an overridden version (`--set-version`) instead of the one
in the manifest — how a release job publishes a version it computed
without first committing it.

deno accepts it only when publishing a single package: it is rejected in
a workspace, where the versions have to come from each member's own
manifest. Whether the working directory is a workspace is not visible
while the argv is being built, so this is a note rather than a refusal.

setters.name: noProvenance
setters.doc:
Disable provenance attestation (`--no-provenance`).

Provenance is what lets a consumer verify the published artifact came from
this repository's CI, so turning it off is a deliberate weakening rather
than a default worth reaching for. It stays on unless this is called.

deno produces it by default only on GitHub Actions, so elsewhere there is
nothing to disable. The case it exists for is the trade it makes: the
attestation publicly links the package to the repository, workflow and
commit it was built from, which a package published from a private
repository may not want disclosed. Weigh that against consumers losing
the ability to verify the artifact's origin, and prefer keeping it.

setters.name: path
setters.doc:
The module to report on — a path, or any specifier `deno info` accepts,
including a `file://` URL. Prefer the URL form when the specifier is
built rather than typed: it is the same string on every OS, where a
constructed path is not.

Omit it to report on the caches themselves — `deno info` with no module
prints the cache directories rather than a module graph, which is why
DenoTasks.cacheInfo and DenoTasks.moduleGraph are separate
readers.

setters.name: json
setters.doc: Emit the report as JSON (`--json`).

setters.name: config
setters.doc: Use an explicit config file (`--config`).

setters.name: importMap
setters.doc: Load an import map from a file or URL (`--import-map`).

setters.name: reload
setters.doc: Reload the module cache before reporting (`--reload`).

setters.name: frozen
setters.doc:
Error out if the lockfile is out of date (`--frozen`). See
DenoPermissionSettings.frozen for why the name mirrors the real
Deno flag.

setters.name: noLock
setters.doc: Ignore the lockfile entirely (`--no-lock`).

setters.name: noNpm
setters.doc: Do not resolve npm modules (`--no-npm`).

setters.name: noRemote
setters.doc: Do not resolve remote modules (`--no-remote`).

setters.name: directory
setters.doc: The directory to create, or the package to scaffold from.

setters.name: lib
setters.doc: Scaffold an example library project (`--lib`).

setters.name: serve
setters.doc: Scaffold an example `deno serve` project (`--serve`).

setters.name: empty
setters.doc: Scaffold a minimal project — just `main.ts` and `deno.json` (`--empty`).

setters.name: jsr
setters.doc: Scaffold from a JSR package (`--jsr`).

setters.name: npm
setters.doc: Scaffold from an npm `create-*` package (`--npm`).

setters.name: yes
setters.doc:
Answer the scaffolding prompts affirmatively and grant full permissions
(`--yes`). Required for an unattended run: without it `deno init` can stop
on a prompt no build target is there to answer.

setters.name: version
setters.doc:
The version, channel (`alpha`, `beta`, `rc`, `canary`) or commit hash to
install. Omit it to move to the latest stable release.

setters.name: dryRun
setters.doc: Run every check without replacing the executable (`--dry-run`).

setters.name: force
setters.doc: Replace the executable even when it is already up to date (`--force`).

setters.name: noDelta
setters.doc: Download the full archive instead of a delta update (`--no-delta`).

setters.name: output
setters.doc:
Write the upgraded executable somewhere else (`--output`), leaving the
running one in place. This is what makes `upgrade` usable from a build:
a target can fetch a second Deno without replacing the one executing it.

setters.name: checksum
setters.doc: Verify the downloaded archive against a SHA-256 checksum (`--checksum`).

packages.name: docs
packages.summary: `@zuke/docs` — typed tasks that turn already-generated API documentation into agent-friendly artifacts, so neither humans nor agents have to guess an API.

tasks.name: DocsTasks
tasks.doc: Typed tasks for generating and verifying API documentation.

tasks.name: apiDocs
tasks.doc:
From the supplied per-package docs, generate the index, the full reference,
and (unless disabled) each package README's API block, writing only the
files whose content changed. Returns the paths written.

tasks.name: checkApiDocs
tasks.doc:
Recompute every artifact and return the paths that are out of date on disk
(empty when everything is current). Writes nothing.

tasks.name: checkDocLint
tasks.doc:
Classify `deno doc --lint` output across packages into real defects: every
`missing-jsdoc`, plus every `private-type-ref` whose referenced type is not
an accepted cross-package import (in the report's `crossPackageTypes`).
Fails safe — any other referenced type is treated as a first-party leak.
Pure: the caller runs the linter; this classifies. Empty when clean.

packages.name: npm
packages.summary: `@zuke/npm` — typed `NpmTasks` wrappers for the `npm` CLI, for use in Zuke build targets (including builds that drive Node projects).

tasks.name: NpmTasks
tasks.doc: Typed task functions for the `npm` CLI.

tasks.name: install
tasks.doc: Install dependencies: `npm install`.

tasks.name: ci
tasks.doc: Clean install from the lockfile: `npm ci`.

tasks.name: uninstall
tasks.doc: Remove dependencies: `npm uninstall`.

tasks.name: update
tasks.doc: Update dependencies within their ranges: `npm update`.

tasks.name: dedupe
tasks.doc: Flatten duplicated packages: `npm dedupe`.

tasks.name: prune
tasks.doc: Remove packages nothing depends on: `npm prune`.

tasks.name: rebuild
tasks.doc: Rebuild native packages: `npm rebuild`.

tasks.name: link
tasks.doc: Symlink a package for local development: `npm link`.

tasks.name: run
tasks.doc: Run a package.json script: `npm run`.

tasks.name: test
tasks.doc: Run the project's test script: `npm test`.

tasks.name: exec
tasks.doc: Execute a package binary: `npm exec`.

tasks.name: publish
tasks.doc: Publish the package: `npm publish`.

tasks.name: pack
tasks.doc: Build a tarball without publishing it: `npm pack`.

tasks.name: version
tasks.doc: Bump the package version: `npm version`.

tasks.name: unpublish
tasks.doc: Remove a published version: `npm unpublish`.

tasks.name: deprecate
tasks.doc: Warn installers off a version: `npm deprecate`.

tasks.name: distTag
tasks.doc: Manage dist-tags: `npm dist-tag add|rm|ls`.

tasks.name: view
tasks.doc: Read registry metadata: `npm view`.

tasks.name: ping
tasks.doc: Check the registry is reachable: `npm ping`.

tasks.name: whoami
tasks.doc: Print the authenticated user: `npm whoami`.

tasks.name: whoamiName
tasks.doc:
The authenticated user's name, or `undefined` when this machine is not
logged in — an answer a release target can act on, rather than the
non-zero exit npm reports.

tasks.name: access
tasks.doc: Manage package access: `npm access`.

tasks.name: owner
tasks.doc: Manage package maintainers: `npm owner add|rm|ls`.

tasks.name: token
tasks.doc: Manage registry tokens: `npm token list|create|revoke`.

tasks.name: ls
tasks.doc: List the installed tree: `npm ls`.

tasks.name: outdated
tasks.doc: Report dependencies behind their latest: `npm outdated`.

tasks.name: outdatedEntries
tasks.doc:
The outdated dependencies as parsed NpmOutdatedEntry values. npm
exits non-zero *because* something is outdated, so this reads that as the
answer rather than as a failure; an empty array means everything is
current.

tasks.name: audit
tasks.doc: Audit dependencies for vulnerabilities: `npm audit`.

tasks.name: auditSummary
tasks.doc:
The audit's vulnerability counts by severity, so a target decides for
itself what is worth failing on. npm's non-zero exit is the finding, not
an error.

tasks.name: sbom
tasks.doc: Emit a software bill of materials: `npm sbom`.

tasks.name: init
tasks.doc: Create a package or run an initializer: `npm init`.

tasks.name: pkg
tasks.doc: Read or write package.json fields: `npm pkg get|set|delete|fix`.

tasks.name: pkgGet
tasks.doc:
One `package.json` field as a string, or `undefined` when it is unset or
is not a scalar — how a build reads its own version without parsing the
manifest or guessing where it lives.

tasks.name: config
tasks.doc: Read or write npm configuration: `npm config get|set|delete|list|fix`.

tasks.name: cache
tasks.doc: Maintain the package cache: `npm cache add|clean|ls|verify`.

settings.name: NpmSettings
settings.doc:
Shared base for every `npm` subcommand: the binary, and the flags npm treats
as configuration rather than as a command's own — it accepts these on any
command, which is why they live here instead of being repeated.

setters.name: registry
setters.doc: Use a specific registry (`--registry=<url>`).

setters.name: json
setters.doc:
Emit JSON (`--json`). The value-returning tasks set this themselves; a
caller reaches for it to parse output the wrapper does not yet model.

setters.name: logLevel
setters.doc: How much npm prints (`--loglevel=<level>`).

setters.name: global
setters.doc: Operate on the global install rather than the project (`--global`).

setters.name: prefix
setters.doc: Run as if npm were started in this directory (`--prefix=<path>`).

setters.name: userconfig
setters.doc: Read this user config file rather than `~/.npmrc` (`--userconfig=<path>`).

settings.name: NpmWorkspaceSettings
settings.doc:
Base for the npm commands that accept workspace selection. `--workspace`
names one (repeatable) and `--workspaces` means all of them; npm takes one
or the other, and this refuses the combination rather than passing on a
command whose meaning is ambiguous.

setters.name: workspace
setters.doc: Run in this workspace (`--workspace=<name>`); repeatable.

setters.name: workspaces
setters.doc:
Run in **every** workspace (`--workspaces`). Mutually exclusive with
workspace — setting both is a build error.

setters.name: includeWorkspaceRoot
setters.doc: Include the root project alongside the workspaces (`--include-workspace-root`).

setters.name: fix
setters.doc: Install compatible updates for what it finds (`npm audit fix`).

setters.name: signatures
setters.doc: Verify the registry signatures of what is installed (`npm audit signatures`).

setters.name: auditLevel
setters.doc:
The severity at which the command fails
(`--audit-level=<info|low|moderate|high|critical|none>`).

setters.name: omit
setters.doc: Skip a dependency group (`--omit=<group>`); repeatable.

setters.name: include
setters.doc: Keep a dependency group npm would otherwise omit (`--include=<group>`); repeatable.

setters.name: packageLockOnly
setters.doc: Audit the lockfile without touching `node_modules` (`--package-lock-only`).

setters.name: dryRun
setters.doc: Report what a fix would change without changing it (`--dry-run`).

setters.name: spec
setters.doc: Limit the listing to one package spec (positional).

setters.name: depth
setters.doc: How deep to walk the tree (`--depth=<n>`); `0` lists direct dependencies.

setters.name: all
setters.doc: Show every dependency, not just the top level (`--all`).

setters.name: long
setters.doc: Include extended information (`--long`).

setters.name: parseable
setters.doc: Emit one line per package, tab-separated (`--parseable`).

setters.name: omit
setters.doc: Skip a dependency group (`--omit=<group>`); repeatable.

setters.name: packages
setters.doc: Limit the report to these package specs (positional); repeatable.

setters.name: all
setters.doc: Report transitive dependencies too (`--all`).

setters.name: long
setters.doc: Include the package type and homepage (`--long`).

setters.name: sbomFormat
setters.doc: Which document to emit (`--sbom-format=<cyclonedx|spdx>`), required by npm.

setters.name: sbomType
setters.doc: What the project is (`--sbom-type=<library|application|framework>`).

setters.name: omit
setters.doc: Skip a dependency group (`--omit=<group>`); repeatable.

setters.name: packageLockOnly
setters.doc: Build the document from the lockfile alone (`--package-lock-only`).

settings.name: NpmDependencySettings
settings.doc:
Shared base for the install-shaped commands: the `--omit`/`--include`
dependency-group selectors npm accepts on all of them, plus the package
specs most of them take.

setters.name: packages
setters.doc: Package specs the command operates on (positional); repeatable.

setters.name: omit
setters.doc: Skip a dependency group (`--omit=<group>`); repeatable.

setters.name: include
setters.doc: Keep a dependency group npm would otherwise omit (`--include=<group>`); repeatable.

setters.name: ignoreScripts
setters.doc: Do not run lifecycle scripts (`--ignore-scripts`).

setters.name: foregroundScripts
setters.doc: Show lifecycle-script output as it runs (`--foreground-scripts`).

setters.name: saveDev
setters.doc: Save to devDependencies (`--save-dev`).

setters.name: saveOptional
setters.doc: Save to optionalDependencies (`--save-optional`).

setters.name: savePeer
setters.doc: Save to peerDependencies (`--save-peer`).

setters.name: saveExact
setters.doc: Pin exact versions (`--save-exact`).

setters.name: noSave
setters.doc: Install without recording the dependency (`--no-save`).

setters.name: installStrategy
setters.doc: How npm lays out the tree (`--install-strategy=<strategy>`).

setters.name: noAudit
setters.doc: Skip the audit npm runs after installing (`--no-audit`).

setters.name: noFund
setters.doc: Skip the funding message (`--no-fund`).

setters.name: noAudit
setters.doc: Skip the audit npm runs after installing (`--no-audit`).

setters.name: noFund
setters.doc: Skip the funding message (`--no-fund`).

setters.name: noSave
setters.doc: Remove the package without updating `package.json` (`--no-save`).

setters.name: save
setters.doc: Write the updated ranges back to `package.json` (`--save`).

setters.name: dryRun
setters.doc: Report what would move without changing the tree (`--dry-run`).

setters.name: dryRun
setters.doc: Report what would be removed without removing it (`--dry-run`).

setters.name: noBinLinks
setters.doc: Do not create the `.bin` symlinks (`--no-bin-links`).

setters.name: saveDev
setters.doc: Record the linked package in devDependencies (`--save-dev`).

setters.name: script
setters.doc: The package.json script to run (required).

setters.name: ifPresent
setters.doc: Do not fail when the script is missing (`--if-present`).

setters.name: scriptArgs
setters.doc: Arguments forwarded to the script (after `--`).

setters.name: testArgs
setters.doc: Arguments forwarded to the test script (after `--`).

setters.name: command
setters.doc: The command to execute (required).

setters.name: package
setters.doc: The package providing the command (`--package=`).

setters.name: yes
setters.doc: Skip the install prompt (`--yes`).

setters.name: no
setters.doc:
Refuse to install anything (`--no`), so the command runs only if it is
already present — what a hermetic CI step wants instead of a silent fetch.

setters.name: execArgs
setters.doc: Arguments forwarded to the command (after `--`).

setters.name: tag
setters.doc: Publish under a dist-tag (`--tag=`).

setters.name: access
setters.doc: Set the package access level (`--access=`).

setters.name: dryRun
setters.doc: Report what would be published without uploading (`--dry-run`).

setters.name: otp
setters.doc:
Provide a one-time password.

Carried in `npm_config_otp` rather than on the command line — see
NpmSettings.applyOtp for why.

setters.name: provenance
setters.doc:
Publish with a provenance attestation (`--provenance`), which npm can
generate from a trusted CI run — the supply-chain signal a consumer can
verify against the workflow that built the tarball.

setters.name: packages
setters.doc: Package specs to pack (positional); defaults to the current project.

setters.name: packDestination
setters.doc: Where to write the tarball (`--pack-destination=<dir>`).

setters.name: dryRun
setters.doc: Report what would be packed without writing a tarball (`--dry-run`).

setters.name: bump
setters.doc: The bump: `patch` | `minor` | `major` or an explicit semver (required).

setters.name: message
setters.doc: Commit message; `%s` expands to the new version (`--message`).

setters.name: noGitTagVersion
setters.doc: Do not create a git commit and tag (`--no-git-tag-version`).

setters.name: preid
setters.doc: The prerelease identifier for a `pre*` bump (`--preid=<id>`), e.g. `rc`.

setters.name: allowSameVersion
setters.doc: Accept a bump to the version already set (`--allow-same-version`).

setters.name: spec
setters.doc: The package spec to remove, e.g. `app@1.2.3` (positional).

setters.name: force
setters.doc:
Confirm an unpublish npm would otherwise refuse (`--force`) — removing a
whole package, or a version outside the 72-hour window.

setters.name: dryRun
setters.doc: Report what would be removed without removing it (`--dry-run`).

setters.name: spec
setters.doc: The package spec to deprecate, e.g. `app@<2` (required).

setters.name: message
setters.doc:
The warning installers will see (required). An empty message is how npm
*un*-deprecates a version, so it must be given deliberately rather than
by omission.

setters.name: otp
setters.doc:
Provide a one-time password.

Carried in `npm_config_otp` rather than on the command line — see
NpmSettings.applyOtp for why.

settings.name: NpmDistTagSettings
settings.doc:
Settings for `npm dist-tag`. Pick the subcommand with add,
rm, or ls.

setters.name: add
setters.doc:
Point a tag at a published version (`dist-tag add <pkg@version> [<tag>]`).
The spec must carry the version; a tag cannot point at a range. With no
tag npm uses `latest`, as it does on the command line.

setters.name: rm
setters.doc: Remove a tag (`dist-tag rm <pkg> <tag>`).

setters.name: ls
setters.doc: List a package's tags (`dist-tag ls [<pkg>]`), the default.

setters.name: spec
setters.doc: The package spec to read, e.g. `react@18` (positional).

setters.name: field
setters.doc:
A field of the registry metadata to print, e.g. `version` or
`dist-tags.latest` (positional); repeatable. With none, npm prints the
whole record.

setters.name: listPackages
setters.doc: List the packages a user, scope, or team can reach (`access list packages`).

setters.name: listCollaborators
setters.doc: List a package's collaborators (`access list collaborators`).

setters.name: getStatus
setters.doc: Read whether a package is public or private (`access get status`), the default.

setters.name: setStatus
setters.doc: Set a package public or private (`access set status=<level>`).

setters.name: setMfa
setters.doc: Require two-factor auth for publishing (`access set mfa=<mode>`).

setters.name: grant
setters.doc: Give a team access (`access grant <permission> <scope:team>`).

setters.name: revoke
setters.doc: Take a team's access away (`access revoke <scope:team>`).

setters.name: otp
setters.doc:
Provide a one-time password.

Carried in `npm_config_otp` rather than on the command line — see
NpmSettings.applyOtp for why.

setters.name: add
setters.doc: Add a maintainer (`owner add <user> <pkg>`).

setters.name: rm
setters.doc: Remove a maintainer (`owner rm <user> <pkg>`).

setters.name: ls
setters.doc: List a package's maintainers (`owner ls <pkg>`).

setters.name: otp
setters.doc:
Provide a one-time password.

Carried in `npm_config_otp` rather than on the command line — see
NpmSettings.applyOtp for why.

settings.name: NpmTokenSettings
settings.doc:
Settings for `npm token`. Pick the subcommand with list,
create, or revoke.

setters.name: list
setters.doc: List this account's tokens (`token list`), the default.

setters.name: create
setters.doc: Create a token (`token create`).

setters.name: revoke
setters.doc:
Revoke a token by id or value (`token revoke <id|token>`).

npm takes this positionally, with no environment route, so the value
reaches the child's argv either way. It is registered with the run's
redactor so every *rendering* of the command masks it; the process table
is not something the wrapper can do anything about here.

Masked whichever it is, because the two are indistinguishable from here —
npm accepts the id or the token itself, and nothing in the string says
which. Masking an id costs a `[redacted]` in this run's output; not
masking a token puts a live credential in it.

setters.name: readOnly
setters.doc: Create a token that cannot publish (`--read-only`).

setters.name: cidr
setters.doc: Restrict a created token to these ranges (`--cidr=<range>`); repeatable.

setters.name: otp
setters.doc:
Provide a one-time password.

Carried in `npm_config_otp` rather than on the command line — see
NpmSettings.applyOtp for why.

setters.name: initializer
setters.doc:
The initializer package to run, e.g. `vite` for `npm init vite`
(positional). With none, npm writes a `package.json` itself.

setters.name: yes
setters.doc: Accept the defaults instead of prompting (`--yes`).

setters.name: scope
setters.doc: Scope the created package (`--scope=<@scope>`).

setters.name: initArgs
setters.doc: Arguments forwarded to the initializer (after `--`).

settings.name: NpmPkgSettings
settings.doc:
Settings for `npm pkg`. Pick the operation with get, set,
deleteKeys, or fix.

setters.name: get
setters.doc: Read one or more `package.json` fields (`pkg get <key>...`).

setters.name: set
setters.doc:
Write fields (`pkg set <key>=<value>...`). Each argument is npm's own
`key=value` form, which is also how it addresses arrays and nested keys.

setters.name: deleteKeys
setters.doc: Remove fields (`pkg delete <key>...`).

setters.name: fix
setters.doc: Repair what npm can correct automatically (`pkg fix`).

setters.name: force
setters.doc: Skip npm's confirmation for a destructive edit (`--force`).

settings.name: NpmConfigSettings
settings.doc:
Settings for `npm config`. Pick the operation with get, set,
deleteKeys, list, or fix.

setters.name: get
setters.doc: Read config keys (`config get <key>...`).

setters.name: set
setters.doc: Write config keys (`config set <key>=<value>...`).

setters.name: deleteKeys
setters.doc: Remove config keys (`config delete <key>...`).

setters.name: list
setters.doc: List the effective configuration (`config list`).

setters.name: fix
setters.doc: Repair invalid config entries (`config fix`).

setters.name: location
setters.doc: Which file to read or write (`--location=<global|user|project>`).

setters.name: long
setters.doc: Include defaults in a listing (`--long`).

settings.name: NpmCacheSettings
settings.doc:
Settings for `npm cache`. Pick the operation with add,
clean, ls, or verify.

setters.name: add
setters.doc: Add a package to the cache (`cache add <spec>`).

setters.name: clean
setters.doc:
Empty the cache (`cache clean`). npm refuses this without `--force`, so
pair it with force — see the error this reports otherwise.

setters.name: ls
setters.doc: List what the cache holds (`cache ls`).

setters.name: verify
setters.doc: Check and compact the cache (`cache verify`), the default.

setters.name: cache
setters.doc: Use a specific cache directory (`--cache=<path>`).

setters.name: force
setters.doc: Confirm a clean npm would otherwise refuse (`--force`).

tasks.name: npx

setters.doc: Follow a symlink in the source (`-L`/`--follow-link`).

setters.doc: The image name to give the snapshot (positional).

setters.name: change
setters.doc: Apply a Dockerfile instruction to the result (`-c`/`--change`); repeatable.

setters.name: noPause
setters.doc:
Leave the container running while it is committed (`--pause=false`).
docker pauses it by default, which is what makes the snapshot consistent.

setters.name: container
setters.doc: The container whose filesystem to export (required).

setters.name: output
setters.doc: Write to a file rather than stdout (`-o`/`--output`).

setters.name: username
setters.doc: The username (`-u`).

setters.name: password
setters.doc:
The password (`-p`), which docker accepts and which therefore stays on the
wrapper.

Prefer passwordStdin. This flag puts the password in the child's
argv, and a child's argv is world-readable on a default Linux host —
through `ps` or `/proc/<pid>/cmdline` — to every other user on the machine
and every process the build starts. On a shared or self-hosted runner that
is every co-tenant.

The value is registered with the run's redactor, so Zuke's own renderings
of the command mask it. That does not cover the process table: the argv
handed to the operating system is not redacted, and docker itself warns
about `-p` for the same reason. Masking is what can be done here, not a
fix for the exposure.

setters.name: passwordStdin
setters.doc:
Pipe the password to docker through STDIN (`--password-stdin`), which
keeps it off the command line entirely.

This is the route docker documents for exactly this reason, and the one to
use in CI. The token goes to the child's standard input, which — unlike its
argv — no other process on the host can read.

The password is required, because the flag on its own means nothing: it
tells docker to read standard input, and this wrapper is what has to put
something there. A `--password-stdin` with no writer leaves docker reading
a stream that is never written.

setters.name: registry

setters.name: term

setters.name: format

setters.name: format

read just the daemon's version.

settings.name: DockerSystemSettings
settings.doc:
Settings for `docker system`. Pick the subcommand with prune,
df, or info.

setters.name: prune
setters.doc: Reclaim space (`system prune`).

setters.name: df
setters.doc: Report what is using disk (`system df`).

setters.name: info
setters.doc: Describe the daemon (`system info`).

setters.name: all
setters.doc:
Prune every unused image, not only the dangling ones (`--all`) — the
difference between reclaiming a little space and reclaiming a lot.

setters.name: force
setters.doc: Do not prompt for confirmation (`--force`), which a build always needs.

setters.name: volumes
setters.doc: Also remove unused volumes (`--volumes`), which a prune otherwise keeps.

setters.name: filter
setters.doc: Limit what is pruned (`--filter`), e.g. `until=24h`; repeatable.

setters.name: verbose
setters.doc: Break the `df` report down per object (`-v`/`--verbose`).

setters.name: format
setters.doc: Render through a Go template (`--format`).

settings.name: DockerContextSettings
settings.doc:

ls, use, inspect, remove, or show.

setters.name: create
setters.doc: Create a context (`context create <name>`).

setters.name: ls
setters.doc: List contexts (`context ls`), the default.

setters.name: use
setters.doc: Make a context the default for later commands (`context use <name>`).

setters.name: inspect
setters.doc: Describe contexts (`context inspect [<name>...]`).

setters.name: remove
setters.doc: Remove contexts (`context rm <name>...`).

setters.name: show
setters.doc: Print the context in use (`context show`).

setters.name: dockerHost
setters.doc: The daemon a created context points at (`--docker host=<address>`).

setters.name: description
setters.doc: A human description for a created context (`--description`).

setters.name: from
setters.doc: Copy an existing context (`--from <name>`).

setters.name: format
setters.doc: Render each context through a Go template (`--format`).

setters.name: quietOutput
setters.doc: Only print context names (`-q`/`--quiet`).

setters.name: force
setters.doc: Remove even the context in use (`-f`/`--force`).

`compose wait` exits with the container's own status, so every code is a
legitimate answer and none is left to mean "compose broke". This hands the
code back rather than failing the target, and still fails when compose
never reached a container at all.

setters.name: volumes

setters.name: removeOrphans

setters.name: services
setters.doc: Restrict the kill to these services.

The signal to send (`--signal`), `SIGKILL` by default. Send `SIGTERM` to
let a service run its shutdown path — `kill` skips the grace period `stop`
gives it.

setters.name: removeOrphans
setters.doc: Remove containers for services no longer in the file (`--remove-orphans`).

setters.doc:
Leave containers that already exist as they are, even when their
configuration changed (`--no-recreate`). Scaling a service with it only
adds or removes replicas; the ones already running keep their image.

setters.doc: Remove containers for services no longer defined (`--remove-orphans`).

Start only the named services, leaving their dependencies alone
(`--no-deps`).

Without it compose starts or recreates a dependency that is stopped or
whose configuration changed. With an already-healthy stack the two agree,
so the difference shows up only on the runs where a dependency was not
ready — which is where a target that meant "just this service" wants to be

When to fetch images before starting (`--pull`). `always` keeps a stack on

Settings for `compose wait`.

The command blocks until the named services' containers stop, then exits
with the first container's own exit status. That makes its exit code a
result rather than a failure — see DockerComposeTasks.waitExitCode,
which hands the code back instead of failing the target.

Delete and recreate rather than update (`--force`). This is not a retry

setters.name: gracePeriod

setters.name: timeout

setters.name: cascade
setters.doc: The cascading strategy for dependents (`--cascade`).

setters.name: wait

setters.name: dryRun

settings.name: KubectlDiffSettings
settings.doc:
Settings for `kubectl diff` — what an apply would change, without changing
it.

`diff` reports its answer through the exit status: **0** when there is no
difference and **1** when there is, with anything above 1 meaning kubectl or
the differ failed. "./kubectl.ts".KubectlTasksApi.diff keeps the
ordinary contract, so a build that wants the printed diff and a failed
target on drift gets both;
"./kubectl.ts".KubectlTasksApi.diffHasChanges is the reader that
turns the code into a boolean.

setters.name: file
setters.doc: Diff a manifest file, directory, or URL (`-f`); repeatable.

setters.name: kustomize
setters.doc: Diff a kustomization directory (`-k`).

setters.name: recursive
setters.doc: Recurse into directories given to `-f` (`-R`).

setters.name: serverSide
setters.doc: Diff the server-side apply (`--server-side`).

setters.name: forceConflicts
setters.doc: Take ownership of conflicting fields (`--force-conflicts`).

setters.name: prune
setters.doc: Include what a prune would delete (`--prune`).

setters.name: selector
setters.doc: Restrict to resources matching a label selector (`-l`).

setters.name: showManagedFields
setters.doc: Include the managed fields, which are otherwise hidden (`--show-managed-fields`).

setters.name: concurrency
setters.doc: How many objects to diff in parallel (`--concurrency`).

setters.name: resource
setters.doc: Resource tokens, e.g. `("pods")` or `("pod", "web")`; repeatable.

setters.name: output
setters.doc: Output format, e.g. `wide`, `yaml`, `json`, `jsonpath=…` (`-o`).

setters.name: selector
setters.doc: Restrict to resources matching a label selector (`-l`).

setters.name: fieldSelector
setters.doc: Restrict by field selector (`--field-selector`).

setters.name: allNamespaces
setters.doc: List across all namespaces (`-A`).

setters.name: watch
setters.doc: Watch for changes instead of returning once (`-w`); pass `false` to disable.

setters.name: showLabels
setters.doc: Include resource labels as columns (`--show-labels`).

setters.name: resource
setters.doc: Resource tokens, e.g. `("pod", "web")` or `("deployment/api")`; repeatable.

setters.name: selector
setters.doc: Restrict to resources matching a label selector (`-l`).

setters.name: resource
setters.doc: Resource tokens, e.g. `("deploy", "api")` or `("pods", "-l", "app=web")`; repeatable.

setters.name: annotation
setters.doc: Set an annotation as a `key=value` token; repeatable.

setters.name: remove
setters.doc: Remove an annotation, rendered as kubectl's `key-` syntax; repeatable.

setters.name: overwrite
setters.doc: Overwrite existing annotations (`--overwrite`).

setters.name: all
setters.doc: Apply to all resources of the given type (`--all`).

setters.name: selector
setters.doc: Restrict to resources matching a label selector (`-l`).

setters.name: resource
setters.doc: Resource tokens, e.g. `("deploy", "api")` or `("pods", "-l", "app=web")`; repeatable.

setters.name: label
setters.doc: Set a label as a `key=value` token; repeatable.

setters.name: remove
setters.doc: Remove a label, rendered as kubectl's `key-` syntax; repeatable.

setters.name: overwrite
setters.doc: Overwrite existing labels (`--overwrite`).

setters.name: all
setters.doc: Apply to all resources of the given type (`--all`).

setters.name: selector
setters.doc: Restrict to resources matching a label selector (`-l`).

setters.name: resource
setters.doc: The resource to patch, e.g. `deployment/api` (required).

setters.name: patch
setters.doc: The patch document (`-p`, required).

setters.name: type
setters.doc: The patch strategy (`--type`).

settings.name: KubectlExplainSettings
settings.doc: Settings for `kubectl explain` — the schema of a resource type.

setters.name: type
setters.doc: The type to explain, e.g. `pods` or `deployments.spec.replicas`.

setters.name: recursive
setters.doc: Print nested fields too (`-R`).

setters.name: maxDepth
setters.doc: Cap how deep recursive goes (`--max-depth`).

setters.name: apiVersion
setters.doc: Explain a particular API group/version (`--api-version`).

setters.name: output
setters.doc: How to render the schema (`-o`): `plaintext` or `plaintext-openapiv2`.

setters.name: status
setters.doc: Show rollout status (`rollout status`).

setters.name: restart
setters.doc: Restart a rollout (`rollout restart`).

setters.name: undo
setters.doc: Roll back to the previous revision (`rollout undo`).

setters.name: history
setters.doc: Show rollout history (`rollout history`).

setters.name: pause
setters.doc:
Stop the rollout where it is (`rollout pause`) — half of a canary. A
paused workload takes no further updates until resume.

setters.name: resume
setters.doc: Let a paused rollout continue (`rollout resume`).

setters.name: resource
setters.doc: The resource, e.g. `deployment/api` (required).

setters.name: toRevision
setters.doc: With `undo`, the revision to roll back to (`--to-revision`).

setters.name: timeout
setters.doc: With `status`, how long to wait, e.g. `60s` (`--timeout`).

setters.name: replicas
setters.doc: Desired replica count (`--replicas`, required).

setters.name: resource
setters.doc: The resource to scale, e.g. `deployment/api`.

setters.name: file
setters.doc: Scale a resource defined in a file (`-f`).

setters.name: currentReplicas
setters.doc: Only scale if the current replica count matches (`--current-replicas`).

setters.name: selector
setters.doc: Restrict to resources matching a label selector (`-l`).

setters.name: all
setters.doc: Scale all resources of the given type (`--all`).

setters.name: resource
setters.doc: The resource to update, e.g. `deployment/api` (required).

setters.name: image
setters.doc: Set a container's image (`container=image`); repeatable, at least one.

setters.name: selector
setters.doc: Restrict to resources matching a label selector (`-l`).

setters.name: all
setters.doc: Apply to all resources of the given type (`--all`).

settings.name: KubectlSetSettings
settings.doc:
Base for the `kubectl set` subcommands that change a pod template in place:
they share the target (a resource, a manifest, or everything in the
namespace) and the container selection.

setters.name: resource
setters.doc: The resource to change, e.g. `deployment/api`; repeatable.

setters.name: file
setters.doc: Change the resource identified by a manifest instead (`-f`); repeatable.

setters.name: all
setters.doc: Change every resource of the named types in the namespace (`--all`).

setters.name: containers
setters.doc: Which containers to change (`-c`); kubectl's default is every one.

setters.name: selector
setters.doc: Restrict to resources matching a label selector (`-l`).

setters.name: local
setters.doc: Rewrite the local manifest without contacting the server (`--local`).

setters.name: dryRun
setters.doc: Preview without persisting (`--dry-run=`; defaults to `client`).

setters.name: set
setters.doc: Set a variable (`-e KEY=VALUE`); repeatable.

setters.name: remove
setters.doc: Remove a variable, which kubectl spells `KEY-` (`-e KEY-`); repeatable.

setters.name: from
setters.doc: Inject every key of a ConfigMap or Secret (`--from`), e.g. `secret/db`.

setters.name: keys
setters.doc: Only these keys of the from resource (`--keys`).

setters.name: prefix
setters.doc: Prefix the injected variable names (`--prefix`).

setters.name: list
setters.doc: Print the environment instead of changing it (`--list`).

setters.name: resolve
setters.doc: Show what the references resolve to when listing (`--resolve`).

setters.name: overwrite
setters.doc: Whether an existing variable may be replaced (`--overwrite`).

setters.name: limit
setters.doc: A resource limit, e.g. `.limit("cpu", "500m")`; repeatable.

setters.name: request
setters.doc: A resource request, e.g. `.request("memory", "256Mi")`; repeatable.

settings.name: KubectlRunSettings
settings.doc:
Settings for `kubectl run` — one pod, imperatively.

This is for a one-off: a migration job, a debug shell. A workload a build
owns belongs in a manifest and goes through
"./manifests.ts".KubectlApplySettings, which is declarative and can
be diffed.

setters.name: name
setters.doc: The pod's name (required).

setters.name: image
setters.doc: The image to run (`--image`, required).

setters.name: restart
setters.doc: The restart policy (`--restart`).

setters.name: envVar
labels
setters.doc: Labels for the pod (`--labels`), comma-separated.

setters.name: port
setters.doc: The port the container exposes (`--port`).

setters.name: overrides
setters.doc: An inline JSON override for the generated pod (`--overrides`).

setters.name: expose
setters.doc: Also create a ClusterIP service (`--expose`), which needs port.

setters.name: command
setters.doc:
The command and arguments to run, after kubectl's `--` separator. Passing
any also sets `--command`, so they replace the image's entrypoint rather
than being appended to it.

setters.name: dryRun
setters.doc: Preview without persisting (`--dry-run=`; defaults to `client`).

settings.name: KubectlExposeSettings
settings.doc: Settings for `kubectl expose` — a service in front of an existing workload.

setters.name: resource
setters.doc: The workload to expose, e.g. `deployment/api`.

setters.name: file
setters.doc: Expose the workload a manifest identifies instead (`-f`); repeatable.

setters.name: port
setters.doc: The port the service serves on (`--port`).

setters.name: targetPort
setters.doc: The container port traffic goes to (`--target-port`).

setters.name: type
setters.doc: The service type (`--type`), e.g. `LoadBalancer`.

setters.name: name
setters.doc: The new service's name (`--name`).

setters.name: protocol
setters.doc: The protocol (`--protocol`), e.g. `TCP`.

setters.name: selector
setters.doc:
The selector the service routes by (`--selector`). kubectl infers it from
the exposed resource when it is omitted, and only equality-based
requirements are supported here.

setters.name: labels
setters.doc: Labels for the created service (`--labels`), comma-separated.

setters.name: sessionAffinity
setters.doc: Session affinity (`--session-affinity`): `None` or `ClientIP`.

setters.name: dryRun
setters.doc: Preview without persisting (`--dry-run=`; defaults to `client`).

setters.name: resource
setters.doc: The pod (or `type/name`) to read logs from.

setters.name: container
setters.doc: Read from a specific container (`-c`).

setters.name: selector
setters.doc: Select pods by label instead of naming one (`-l`).

setters.name: follow
setters.doc: Stream new log output (`-f`).

setters.name: previous
setters.doc: Read the previous container instance's logs (`--previous`).

setters.name: tail
setters.doc: Show only the last N lines (`--tail`).

setters.name: since
setters.doc: Only logs newer than a duration, e.g. `5m` (`--since`).

setters.name: allContainers
setters.doc: Include all containers in the pod (`--all-containers`).

setters.name: timestamps
setters.doc: Prefix each line with a timestamp (`--timestamps`).

setters.name: resource
setters.doc: The pod (or `type/name`) to exec into (required).

setters.name: container
setters.doc: Target a specific container (`-c`).

setters.name: stdin
setters.doc: Keep STDIN open (`-i`).

setters.name: tty
setters.doc: Allocate a TTY (`-t`).

setters.name: command
setters.doc: The command and arguments to run in the container (required).

setters.name: resource
setters.doc: The pod or service, e.g. `svc/api` (required).

setters.name: port
setters.doc: A port mapping, e.g. `8080:80` or `8080`; repeatable, at least one.

setters.name: address
setters.doc: The local address(es) to bind (`--address`).

settings.name: KubectlCpSettings
settings.doc:
Settings for `kubectl cp` — copying files into and out of a container.

This is how a build gets a report out of a pod that produced it. Each side
is either a local path or a `[namespace/]pod:path` spec, and kubectl takes
exactly one of each.

setters.name: from
setters.doc: Where to copy from: a local path, or `pod:path` / `namespace/pod:path`.

setters.name: to
setters.doc: Where to copy to, in the same two forms.

setters.name: container
setters.doc: Which container of the pod (`-c`).

setters.name: noPreserve
setters.doc: Do not carry ownership and permissions across (`--no-preserve`).

setters.name: retries
setters.doc: Retry a copy out of a container this many times (`--retries`).

setters.name: file
setters.doc: Wait on resources defined in a file (`-f`); repeatable.

setters.name: resource
setters.doc: Resource tokens, e.g. `("pod/web")` or `("pods")`; repeatable.

setters.name: forCondition
setters.doc: The condition to wait for, e.g. `condition=Available` or `delete`.

setters.name: timeout
setters.doc: How long to wait, e.g. `60s` (`--timeout`).

setters.name: selector
setters.doc: Restrict to resources matching a label selector (`-l`).

setters.name: all
setters.doc: Wait on all resources of the given type (`--all`).

setters.name: pods
setters.doc: Report pod usage (`top pods`).

setters.name: nodes
setters.doc: Report node usage (`top nodes`).

setters.name: name
setters.doc: Limit to a single named pod or node.

setters.name: selector
setters.doc: Restrict to resources matching a label selector (`-l`).

setters.name: containers
setters.doc: Break pod usage down by container (`--containers`).

setters.name: allNamespaces
setters.doc: Report across all namespaces (`-A`).

settings.name: KubectlEventsSettings
settings.doc:
Settings for `kubectl events` — the first thing to read when a rollout
stalls and `rollout status` will not say why.

setters.name: forResource
setters.doc: Only events about this resource, as `TYPE/NAME` (`--for`).

setters.name: types
setters.doc: Only events of these types, e.g. `Warning` (`--types`).

setters.name: allNamespaces
setters.doc: Across every namespace (`-A`).

setters.name: watch
setters.doc:
Keep watching after the listing (`--watch`). A target that watches blocks
until something stops it, so pair it with `.killAfter(...)` unless the
wait is the point.

setters.name: noHeaders
setters.doc: Leave the header row out (`--no-headers`).

setters.name: output
setters.doc: The output format (`-o`), e.g. `json`.

setters.name: namesOnly
setters.doc: Print only the names (`-o name`), the one output format gh accepts here.

setters.name: noHeaders
setters.doc: Leave the header row out (`--no-headers`).

setters.name: contextName
setters.doc: The context to switch to (required).

settings.name: KubectlConfigSetContextSettings
settings.doc:
Settings for `kubectl config set-context`.

Note that `set-context` has its own `--namespace`, which sets the namespace
recorded **in the context entry** rather than scoping one command. The
inherited `.namespace(...)` renders that same flag, which is what a caller
of this command wants.

setters.name: contextName
setters.doc: The context to write (required unless current is set).

setters.name: current
setters.doc: Modify the current context rather than a named one (`--current`).

setters.name: cluster
setters.doc: The cluster the context points at (`--cluster`).

setters.name: user
setters.doc: The user the context authenticates as (`--user`).

setters.name: minify
setters.doc: Keep only what the current context uses (`--minify`).

setters.name: flatten
setters.doc: Inline the referenced files, for a portable kubeconfig (`--flatten`).

setters.name: raw
setters.doc:
Print the credentials in the clear (`--raw`). kubectl redacts them by
default; anything this prints belongs in a `parameter().secret()`, not in
a build's log.

setters.name: output
setters.doc: The output format (`-o`), e.g. `json`; kubectl's default is `yaml`.

setters.name: clientOnly
setters.doc: Report the client's version without reaching a cluster (`--client`).

setters.name: output
setters.doc: The output format (`-o`): `json` or `yaml`.

setters.name: apiGroup
setters.doc: Only resources in this API group (`--api-group`).

setters.name: namespaced
setters.doc:
Whether to list namespaced resources (`--namespaced`); kubectl's default
is `true`, so pass `false` for the cluster-scoped ones.

setters.name: verbs
setters.doc: Only resources supporting these verbs (`--verbs`).

setters.name: categories
setters.doc: Only resources in these categories (`--categories`).

setters.name: sortBy
setters.doc: Sort by `name` or `kind` (`--sort-by`).

setters.name: output
setters.doc: The output format (`-o`), e.g. `name` or `wide`.

setters.name: noHeaders
setters.doc: Leave the header row out (`--no-headers`).

setters.name: cached
setters.doc: Use the discovery cache rather than asking the server (`--cached`).

settings.name: KubectlAuthCanISettings
settings.doc:
Settings for `kubectl auth can-i`.

The command answers through its exit status — **0** when the action is
allowed and non-zero when it is not — so
"./kubectl.ts".KubectlTasksApi.canI reads the code into a boolean
rather than failing the build on a routine "no".

setters.name: verb
setters.doc: The API verb to check, e.g. `create` (required unless list).

setters.name: resource
setters.doc: The resource, e.g. `deployments` or `deployments/api`.

setters.name: subresource
setters.doc: A subresource, e.g. `log` or `scale` (`--subresource`).

setters.name: allNamespaces
setters.doc: Check across every namespace (`--all-namespaces`).

setters.name: list
setters.doc: Print every allowed action instead of checking one (`--list`).

setters.name: quietAnswer
setters.doc:
Print nothing and answer only through the exit code (kubectl's
`--quiet`). Named apart from the inherited `.quiet()`, which suppresses
Zuke's own echo of the command rather than kubectl's output.

settings.name: KubectlKustomizeSettings
settings.doc: Settings for `kubectl kustomize` — rendering a kustomization to stdout.

setters.name: dir
setters.doc: The kustomization directory or repository URL; kubectl assumes `.`.

setters.name: output
setters.doc: Write the rendered output to a file instead of stdout (`-o`).

setters.name: enableHelm
setters.doc: Allow the Helm chart inflator generator (`--enable-helm`).

setters.name: loadRestrictor
setters.doc: Relax where a kustomization may load files from (`--load-restrictor`).

settings.name: KubectlCordonSettings
settings.doc:
Settings for `kubectl cordon` and `kubectl uncordon` — marking a node
unschedulable, and letting it take pods again.

setters.name: node
setters.doc: The node to act on; required unless a selector picks them.

setters.name: uncordon
setters.doc: Make the node schedulable again instead — `kubectl uncordon`.

setters.name: selector
setters.doc: Act on every node matching a label selector (`-l`).

setters.name: dryRun
setters.doc: Preview without persisting (`--dry-run=`; defaults to `client`).

settings.name: KubectlDrainSettings
settings.doc:
Settings for `kubectl drain`.

kubectl refuses to drain a node whose pods it cannot safely move, and the
two flags that override that refusal are exactly the ones worth being
deliberate about: `--ignore-daemonsets` and `--delete-emptydir-data`, the
second of which destroys local data. Neither is defaulted here.

setters.name: node
setters.doc: The node to drain; required unless a selector picks them.

setters.name: force
setters.doc: Evict pods no controller manages, which nothing will recreate (`--force`).

setters.name: ignoreDaemonSets
setters.doc: Proceed past DaemonSet-managed pods, which drain never deletes (`--ignore-daemonsets`).

setters.name: deleteEmptyDirData
setters.doc: Proceed past pods using emptyDir, destroying that data (`--delete-emptydir-data`).

setters.name: disableEviction
setters.doc:
Delete rather than evict (`--disable-eviction`), which bypasses every
PodDisruptionBudget — the guardrail an operator wrote down on purpose.

setters.name: gracePeriod
setters.doc: Seconds each pod gets to terminate (`--grace-period`).

setters.name: timeout
setters.doc: How long to wait for the drain overall, e.g. `5m` (`--timeout`).

setters.name: podSelector
setters.doc: Only drain pods matching this label selector (`--pod-selector`).

setters.name: selector
setters.doc: Drain every node matching this label selector (`-l`).

setters.name: skipWaitForDeleteTimeout
setters.doc: Stop waiting on pods already deleting this long (`--skip-wait-for-delete-timeout`).

setters.name: dryRun
setters.doc: Preview without persisting (`--dry-run=`; defaults to `client`).

setters.name: node
setters.doc: A node to taint; repeatable.

setters.name: taint
setters.doc: Add a taint, as `key=value:effect`; repeatable.

setters.name: removeTaint
setters.doc: Remove a taint, which kubectl spells with a trailing `-`; repeatable.

setters.name: all
setters.doc: Taint every node in the cluster (`--all`).

setters.name: overwrite
setters.doc: Replace a taint of the same key rather than failing (`--overwrite`).

setters.name: selector
setters.doc: Taint every node matching a label selector (`-l`).

setters.name: dryRun
setters.doc: Preview without persisting (`--dry-run=`; defaults to `client`).

setters.name: token
setters.doc:
Authenticate with a token instead of the interactive flow (`--token`).

Registered with the run's redactor, so every *rendering* of the command
masks it — a dry-run echo, a failure message. That is as far as it goes:
`jsr publish` accepts the token only as a flag, so the value still reaches
the child's argv, where `ps` and `/proc/<pid>/cmdline` expose it to every
other user on the host and to every process the build starts. There is no
environment variable to move it to.

On GitHub Actions, prefer OIDC and pass no token at all: the publish is
authenticated by the workflow's identity, so there is no credential to
expose. This is for the cases where that is not available.
