tasks.name: evaluate
tasks.doc:
Import a Node module and resolve to one of its exports' JSON value — the
way a target reads something *out* of the Node side of a project (an
OpenAPI document, a resolved config) instead of shelling out to a script
that has to write it somewhere first.

`module` is a path, resolved against the working directory. The export
(`default` unless NodeEvaluateSettings.export names another) is
awaited; when it is a function it is called with
NodeEvaluateSettings.callWith's arguments first.

```ts
// tools/openapi.mjs: export default async () => document
const spec = await NodeTasks.evaluate("tools/openapi.mjs");
```

The evaluation waits for the Node process to exit, so a module that leaves
a live handle on the event loop (a server, a pool, a timer) would block on
a value it has already produced. NodeEvaluateSettings.exitAfterResult
ends the process as soon as the result has been written, for modules in
that shape.

The module runs as a real Node process with the build's own permissions —
the same trust level as a script handed to NodeTasks.run, and the
reason this is a build-authoring API rather than an input-processing one.
`module` is code: build it from a literal or from the project's own layout,
never from an untrusted source (a pull request title, a webhook payload),
exactly as for every other command a build spawns. Values passed through
NodeEvaluateSettings.callWith cannot inject into the driver — they
are embedded as JSON literals — but they do reach the module, so whatever
the module does with them is the module's contract to uphold.

settings.name: NodeSettings
settings.doc: Shared base for every `node` task: it pins the binary to `node`.

settings.name: NodeEvaluateSettings
settings.doc:
Settings for "./node.ts".NodeTasks.evaluate — which export of the
module to take, and what to call it with.

setters.name: export
setters.doc:
The named export to take, instead of the default one.

The export is awaited; when it is a function it is called first, with
callWith's arguments.

setters.name: callWith
setters.doc:
Arguments for the exported function, in order. Each must be
JSON-serialisable — they cross a process boundary as JSON.

Named `callWith` rather than `args` because `ToolSettings.args` already
means "append raw arguments to the `node` command line", which is a
different thing.

setters.name: exitAfterResult
setters.doc:
End the Node process as soon as the result has been written, instead of
waiting for the module to let Node exit on its own.

A module that leaves a live handle on the event loop — an HTTP server, a
database pool, a timer — never exits, and the evaluation then blocks
forever on a value it has *already* produced and written. This makes the
driver exit once that write has flushed, so such a module can be evaluated
as it is, without a `process.exit` of its own.

What the module does *after* handing back its value does not happen. The
process ends at the write, so anything it would still print is cut off,
anything it would still do — a `beforeExit` handler, a teardown scheduled
on the next tick, a flush that has not been awaited — does not run, and its
own exit code is no longer observed (the driver exits `0`). That is the
trade the option makes, and why it is opt-in rather than the default:
choose it for a module whose value is the whole point of running it, and
whose remaining work is process teardown the operating system is about to
do anyway. A module whose after-the-value work *matters* — one that writes
a file, commits a transaction, or reports its own failure through an exit
code — should keep the default and be given a way to exit on its own.

Two shapes are unaffected either way: a module that throws before producing
a result still rejects the evaluation, since the driver never reaches its
final write, and a module that exits on its own never notices the option.

settings.name: GcloudLoggingReadSettings
settings.doc:
Settings for `gcloud logging read`: which entries (the filter), from where
(project, folder, organization, billing account, or a log view), and how
many.

setters.name: filter
setters.doc:
Raw filter text in the Logging query language, joined with every other
part by `AND`; repeatable. It is the caller's own text and is not
escaped — never build it from an untrusted value; use the typed setters
for those.

setters.name: resourceType
setters.doc: Only entries from this monitored-resource type: `resource.type="…"`.

setters.name: resourceLabel
setters.doc: Only entries whose resource label `key` is `value`; repeatable.

setters.name: label
setters.doc: Only entries whose own label `key` is `value`; repeatable.

setters.name: minSeverity
setters.doc: Only entries at `severity` or above: `severity>=ERROR`.

setters.name: since
setters.doc: Only entries at or after `time`: `timestamp>="…"`.

setters.name: until
setters.doc: Only entries before `time`: `timestamp<"…"`.

setters.name: freshness
setters.doc:
Only entries newer than this — `"1h"`, `"90s"`, or ms — sent as an
explicit `timestamp>="<now − duration>"` in the filter, measured from
now. gcloud's own `--freshness` is not used: gcloud silently
drops it whenever the filter's text contains the word `timestamp`
anywhere, or the order is `asc`, and the read then spans the whole
retention period.

setters.name: order
setters.doc: Newest first (`desc`, gcloud's default) or oldest first (`--order`).

setters.name: limit
setters.doc: Read at most this many entries (`--limit`; gcloud's default is unlimited).

setters.name: organization
setters.doc:
Read from an organization's logs (`--organization`). gcloud takes one of
`--organization`, `--folder`, `--billing-account` and `--project`.

setters.name: folder
setters.doc: Read from a folder's logs (`--folder`).

setters.name: billingAccount
setters.doc: Read from a billing account's logs (`--billing-account`).

setters.name: logView
setters.doc: Read through a log view (`--bucket`, `--location`, `--view`).

setters.name: resourceNames
setters.doc:
Read from these resources instead (`--resource-names`): a project,
folder or organization name, or a full log-view path. gcloud takes these
or a log view, not both.

settings.doc:

above it fails as "more than n".

and names its own command path.

setters.name: filter

settings.name: CloudMonitoringTimeSeriesSettings
settings.doc:
Settings for a Cloud Monitoring time-series read, configured through
`CloudMonitoringTasks.timeSeriesList((s) => …)`.

```ts
s.project("my-proj")
  .metricType("run.googleapis.com/request_count")
  .resourceType("cloud_run_revision")
  .resourceLabel("service_name", "api")
  .metricLabel("response_code_class", "5xx")
  .alignmentPeriod("60s").perSeriesAligner("ALIGN_SUM")
  .crossSeriesReducer("REDUCE_SUM")
  .window("15m")
```

setters.name: project
setters.doc:
The project to read from; when omitted, `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT` (then
`GCLOUD_PROJECT`).

setters.name: metricType
setters.doc:
The metric to read: `metric.type = "<type>"`, e.g.
`"run.googleapis.com/request_count"`. The API reads exactly one metric
type per call.

setters.name: resourceType
setters.doc: Only series on this monitored-resource type: `resource.type = "<type>"`.

setters.name: resourceLabel
setters.doc: Only series whose resource label `key` is `value`; repeatable.

setters.name: metricLabel
setters.doc: Only series whose metric label `key` is `value`; repeatable.

setters.name: filter
setters.doc:
Raw text in the Monitoring filter language, joined with the typed parts
by `AND`; repeatable. It is the caller's own text and is not escaped —
never build it from an untrusted value. With no metricType, it
must name the metric itself.

setters.name: window
setters.doc:
How far back to read (`"15m"`, or ms; default five minutes), ending now
— or, with an alignmentPeriod, at the last period boundary, so
the period still being written is not read. The window must be at least
one period long.

setters.name: interval
setters.doc: Read exactly this interval instead of a window ending now.

setters.name: alignmentPeriod
setters.doc:
What each aligned point covers (`aggregation.alignmentPeriod`) —
`"60s"`, `"5m"`, or ms; whole seconds, at least 60, as the API requires.

setters.name: perSeriesAligner
setters.doc: How each series is aligned (`aggregation.perSeriesAligner`).

setters.name: crossSeriesReducer
setters.doc: How aligned series are combined (`aggregation.crossSeriesReducer`).

setters.name: groupByFields
setters.doc:
The labels the reducer keeps series apart by
(`aggregation.groupByFields`), e.g. `"resource.labels.revision_name"`.

setters.name: view
setters.doc: `FULL` (the default) returns points; `HEADERS` only each series' labels.

setters.name: pageSize
setters.doc: The most results per page (`pageSize`; the API's default is 100,000).

setters.name: maxPages
setters.doc:
The most pages to read (default 100). A read that still has a next page
after that many fails — a partial answer is never returned as a whole.

setters.name: delay
setters.doc:
End the window this long before now (`"2m"`, or ms) — for the time a
metric takes to become readable. Google's metrics list gives it per
metric: Cloud Run's `request_count` and `request_latencies` are "not
visible for up to 120 seconds" after sampling. Without it the newest
points may not exist yet, or hold only part of their period. Default
`0` for a read; the `cloudMonitoring(...)` analysis defaults to two
minutes.

setters.name: token
setters.doc: A pre-resolved OAuth access token.

setters.name: gcloud
setters.doc:
Global gcloud flags for the default token read,
`gcloud auth print-access-token` — `(g) => g.account("ci@p.iam…")`, or a
`.runner(...)`, the seam a test answers through. Unused when a
token or tokenProvider is set.

settings.name: CloudMonitoringMetricValueSettings
settings.doc:
Settings for `CloudMonitoringTasks.metricValue`: a time-series read, and
how to turn it into one number. The view is always `FULL` — the reader
needs the points.

setters.name: aggregate
setters.doc:
How to turn the points into one number, across every series the answer
holds. `"latest"` (the default) sums each series' own newest point, so a
metric split by a label reads as its total. The others combine every
point in the window: a `"sum"` of per-minute `ALIGN_SUM` points is the
window's total.

A `DISTRIBUTION` point reads as its mean. `"average"` weights each mean
by its sample count; `"maximum"` and `"minimum"` are of the means.
Means cannot be added, so `"sum"` refuses distributions, and `"latest"`
refuses more than one distribution series — collapse them with
`.crossSeriesReducer(...)`, or align them to a number with
`ALIGN_PERCENTILE_99`, `ALIGN_MEAN` and the like.

setters.name: missingDataAs
setters.doc:
Return `value` when there are no points, instead of failing. Cloud
Monitoring writes no point for a period with no events, so for a count
of errors no data does mean `0`; for a latency it usually means the
filter is looking in the wrong place.

tasks.doc:
**Publish** a new version of the function — `aws lambda publish-version`,
which changes the account — and return the number it was given. Pins
`--query Version --output text`. Not a lookup: every call publishes.

tasks.name: lambdaUpdateAlias
tasks.doc: Move an alias: `aws lambda update-alias`.

tasks.name: lambdaGetAlias
tasks.doc: Describe an alias: `aws lambda get-alias`.

tasks.name: lambdaGetFunction
tasks.doc: Describe a function: `aws lambda get-function`.

tasks.name: lambdaWait
tasks.doc: Wait for a function or version to reach a state: `aws lambda wait`.

tasks.name: lambdaInvoke
tasks.doc: Invoke a function: `aws lambda invoke`.

tasks.name: cloudformationDeploy
tasks.doc: Create or update a stack: `aws cloudformation deploy`.

tasks.name: cloudformationDescribeStacks
tasks.doc: Describe stacks: `aws cloudformation describe-stacks`.

tasks.name: stackOutput
tasks.doc:
One output of a stack, read back as a string. Pins a `--query` projecting
that output and `--output json`; fails when the stack has no such output.

tasks.name: cloudformationDeleteStack
tasks.doc: Delete a stack: `aws cloudformation delete-stack`.

tasks.name: cloudformationWait
tasks.doc: Block until a stack reaches a state: `aws cloudformation wait <waiter>`.

tasks.name: secretsmanagerGetSecretValue
tasks.doc: Read a secret: `aws secretsmanager get-secret-value` (captured, never streamed).

tasks.name: secretString
tasks.doc:
A secret's `SecretString`, read back exactly — multi-line values and
surrounding whitespace included. Pins `--query SecretString --output
json`; fails for a binary secret.

tasks.name: ssmGetParameter
tasks.doc: Read a parameter: `aws ssm get-parameter` (captured, never streamed).

tasks.name: parameterValue
tasks.doc:
A parameter's value, read back exactly. Pins `--query Parameter.Value
--output json`; add `.withDecryption()` for a `SecureString`.

tasks.name: ssmPutParameter
tasks.doc: Write a parameter: `aws ssm put-parameter`.

tasks.name: eksUpdateKubeconfig
tasks.doc: Write a kubeconfig entry for a cluster: `aws eks update-kubeconfig`.

tasks.name: eksDescribeCluster
tasks.doc: Describe a cluster: `aws eks describe-cluster`.

tasks.name: cloudwatchGetMetricData
tasks.doc: Read metric datapoints: `aws cloudwatch get-metric-data`.

tasks.name: metricValue
tasks.doc:
One number from CloudWatch: the latest datapoint of a series, or an
aggregate over the window. Pins `--query MetricDataResults --output
json`; fails on no data unless `.missingDataAs(value)` says what it
means.

tasks.name: cloudwatchGetMetricStatistics
tasks.doc: Read metric statistics: `aws cloudwatch get-metric-statistics`.

tasks.name: cloudwatchDescribeAlarms
tasks.doc: Describe alarms: `aws cloudwatch describe-alarms`.

tasks.name: alarmState
tasks.doc: The state of one metric, composite or log alarm: `OK`, `ALARM` or `INSUFFICIENT_DATA`.

tasks.name: logsStartQuery
tasks.doc: Start a Logs Insights query: `aws logs start-query`.

tasks.name: logsGetQueryResults
tasks.doc: Read a Logs Insights query's results: `aws logs get-query-results`.

tasks.name: logsStopQuery
tasks.doc: Stop a running Logs Insights query: `aws logs stop-query`.

tasks.name: logsInsightsQuery
tasks.doc:
Run a Logs Insights query to the end and return its rows: start it, poll
`get-query-results` until it is `Complete`, and fail with an
`AwsLogsQueryError` when it ends otherwise or outlasts the timeout.

tasks.name: logsFilterLogEvents
tasks.doc: Search a log group's events: `aws logs filter-log-events`.

tasks.name: logsTail
tasks.doc: Print a log group's recent events: `aws logs tail`.

settings.name: AwsSettings
settings.doc:
Settings for an `aws` invocation.

Every instance sets two variables in the child's environment so the CLI
can never sit waiting for a keypress in a build: `AWS_PAGER` to the empty
string (CLI v2 pipes output through `less` by default) and
`AWS_CLI_AUTO_PROMPT` to `off` (a profile's `cli_auto_prompt` would
otherwise open the interactive prompt). Setting them there keeps the argv
exactly what the settings say; override either with `.env({...})`, or add
the explicit flag with noCliPager.

setters.name: profile
setters.doc: The named profile from the shared config and credentials files (`--profile`).

setters.name: region
setters.doc: The AWS Region to send the request to (`--region`), e.g. `"eu-west-1"`.

setters.name: output
setters.doc: The output format (`--output`): `json`, `text`, `table`, `yaml` or `yaml-stream`.

setters.name: query
setters.doc: A JMESPath expression that filters the response (`--query`).

setters.name: endpointUrl
setters.doc: Send the request to this URL instead of the service's default endpoint (`--endpoint-url`).

setters.name: noCliPager
setters.doc:
Pass `--no-cli-pager` explicitly. The pager is already off through
`AWS_PAGER` (see AwsSettings); the flag is for a build that wants
it on the command line as well. AWS CLI v2 only.

setters.name: noVerifySsl
setters.doc:
Skip TLS certificate verification (`--no-verify-ssl`). This disables the
check that the endpoint is who it claims to be — meant for a local
emulator, never for a real account; prefer caBundle.

setters.name: noSignRequest
setters.doc: Send the request unsigned, without loading credentials (`--no-sign-request`).

setters.name: caBundle
setters.doc: The CA certificate bundle to verify TLS against (`--ca-bundle`).

setters.name: cliReadTimeout
setters.doc: The socket read timeout in seconds; `0` blocks forever (`--cli-read-timeout`).

setters.name: cliConnectTimeout
setters.doc: The socket connect timeout in seconds; `0` blocks forever (`--cli-connect-timeout`).

setters.name: debug
setters.doc:
Turn on the CLI's debug logging (`--debug`), written to stderr.

**The debug log carries credentials**: request headers with the session
token, and response bodies — a secret's value among them. The access key,
secret key and session token in the environment are registered with the
run's redactor when this is called, but a credential the CLI loads from a
profile, an SSO cache or a role is not known here and is not masked. Keep
it for a local investigation, never a shared CI log.

setters.name: flag
setters.doc:
Add an arbitrary option: `--name value`, or the bare `--name`.

Two hazards come with the escape hatch, which the typed setters guard and
this does not: a value that starts with `-` is read by the CLI as the next
option, and a value that starts with `file://` or `fileb://` is replaced
by that file's contents — which then leave the machine in the request.
Never pass an untrusted value here.

settings.name: AwsStsAssumeRoleSettings
settings.doc:
Settings for `aws sts assume-role`.

The response carries a secret access key and a session token, so the
command always runs quietly — its output is captured, never streamed — with
`--output json` pinned whatever the settings or the user's config say, and
both values are registered with the run's redactor once it returns.

setters.name: roleArn
setters.doc: The role to assume (`--role-arn`).

setters.name: roleSessionName
setters.doc: An identifier for the session, shown in CloudTrail (`--role-session-name`).

setters.name: durationSeconds
setters.doc: How long the credentials last, in seconds (`--duration-seconds`).

setters.name: externalId
setters.doc: The external id the role's trust policy requires (`--external-id`).

setters.name: policy
setters.doc: An inline session policy, as a JSON document (`--policy`).

setters.name: serialNumber
setters.doc: The MFA device's serial number or ARN (`--serial-number`).

setters.name: tokenCode
setters.doc: The code the MFA device shows (`--token-code`).

settings.name: AwsConfigureGetSettings
settings.doc:
Settings for `aws configure get`.

Reading a credential — `aws_secret_access_key`, `aws_session_token`, in any
profile — runs quietly and registers what it printed with the run's
redactor.

setters.name: varname
setters.doc: The setting to read (positional), e.g. `"region"`.

settings.name: AwsConfigureSetSettings
settings.doc:
Settings for `aws configure set`.

`aws configure set` takes the value on its command line, where every user
on the host can read it from the process table. Setting
`aws_secret_access_key` or `aws_session_token` this way registers the value
with the run's redactor so Zuke's own output masks it, but that does not
hide it from the process table — prefer the `AWS_*` environment variables
or a role for credentials.

setters.name: varname
setters.doc: The setting to write (positional), e.g. `"region"`.

setters.name: value
setters.doc: The value to write (positional).

setters.name: source
setters.doc: The local path or `s3://` URI to copy from (positional).

setters.name: destination
setters.doc: The local path or `s3://` URI to copy to (positional).

setters.name: recursive
setters.doc: Copy every file under a directory or prefix (`--recursive`).

setters.name: exclude
setters.doc: Skip files matching the pattern (`--exclude`); repeatable, order kept.

setters.name: include
setters.doc: Copy files matching the pattern despite an earlier exclude (`--include`).

setters.name: dryrun
setters.doc: Print what would be copied without copying it (`--dryrun`).

setters.name: acl
setters.doc: A canned ACL for the uploaded objects (`--acl`), e.g. `"private"`.

setters.name: contentType
setters.doc: The uploaded objects' content type (`--content-type`).

setters.name: cacheControl
setters.doc: The uploaded objects' `Cache-Control` (`--cache-control`).

setters.name: storageClass
setters.doc: The storage class for the uploaded objects (`--storage-class`).

setters.name: sse
setters.doc: Server-side encryption (`--sse`): `"AES256"` or `"aws:kms"`.

setters.name: sseKmsKeyId
setters.doc: The KMS key for `aws:kms` server-side encryption (`--sse-kms-key-id`).

setters.name: onlyShowErrors
setters.doc: Print only errors and warnings (`--only-show-errors`).

setters.name: noProgress
setters.doc: Leave out the file-transfer progress lines (`--no-progress`).

setters.name: path
setters.doc: The `s3://` URI to list (positional); the buckets when omitted.

setters.name: recursive
setters.doc: List every object under the prefix (`--recursive`).

setters.name: humanReadable
setters.doc: Print sizes as KiB, MiB, … (`--human-readable`).

setters.name: summarize
setters.doc: Print the object count and total size (`--summarize`).

setters.name: bucket
setters.doc: The bucket to make, as an `s3://` URI (positional).

settings.name: AwsS3PresignSettings
settings.doc:
Settings for `aws s3 presign`.

A presigned URL is a bearer credential for the object until it expires:
anyone holding it can read the object, and when the build runs on
temporary credentials it also carries the session token itself
(`X-Amz-Security-Token`), which is good for far more than one object. So
the command always runs quietly — the URL is captured, never streamed — and
the URL and that token are registered with the run's redactor.

setters.name: path
setters.doc: The `s3://` object to presign (positional).

setters.name: expiresIn
setters.doc: How long the URL stays valid, in seconds (`--expires-in`; default 3600).

setters.name: path
setters.doc: The `s3://` object or prefix to remove (positional).

setters.name: recursive
setters.doc: Remove every object under the prefix (`--recursive`).

setters.name: exclude
setters.doc: Keep objects matching the pattern (`--exclude`); repeatable, order kept.

setters.name: include
setters.doc: Remove objects matching the pattern despite an earlier exclude (`--include`).

setters.name: dryrun
setters.doc: Print what would be removed without removing it (`--dryrun`).

setters.name: source
setters.doc: The local directory or `s3://` prefix to sync from (positional).

setters.name: destination
setters.doc: The local directory or `s3://` prefix to sync to (positional).

setters.name: delete
setters.doc:
Delete files at the destination that the source does not have
(`--delete`), which makes the destination a mirror rather than a superset.

setters.name: exclude
setters.doc: Skip files matching the pattern (`--exclude`); repeatable, order kept.

setters.name: include
setters.doc: Sync files matching the pattern despite an earlier exclude (`--include`).

setters.name: dryrun
setters.doc: Print what would change without changing it (`--dryrun`).

setters.name: exactTimestamps
setters.doc: Treat same-size files with different timestamps as changed (`--exact-timestamps`).

setters.name: sizeOnly
setters.doc: Compare by size alone, ignoring timestamps (`--size-only`).

setters.name: acl
setters.doc: A canned ACL for the uploaded objects (`--acl`).

setters.name: contentType
setters.doc: The uploaded objects' content type (`--content-type`).

setters.name: cacheControl
setters.doc: The uploaded objects' `Cache-Control` (`--cache-control`).

setters.name: storageClass
setters.doc: The storage class for the uploaded objects (`--storage-class`).

setters.name: onlyShowErrors
setters.doc: Print only errors and warnings (`--only-show-errors`).

setters.name: noProgress
setters.doc: Leave out the file-transfer progress lines (`--no-progress`).

setters.name: repositoryName
setters.doc: The repository to delete from (`--repository-name`).

setters.name: registryId
setters.doc: The registry's account id, when not the caller's (`--registry-id`).

setters.name: imageTag
setters.doc: Delete the image with this tag (`--image-ids`); repeatable.

setters.name: imageDigest
setters.doc: Delete the image with this digest (`--image-ids`); repeatable.

setters.name: repositoryName
setters.doc: The repository to describe (`--repository-name`).

setters.name: registryId
setters.doc: The registry's account id, when not the caller's (`--registry-id`).

setters.name: imageTag
setters.doc: Describe the image with this tag (`--image-ids`); repeatable.

setters.name: imageDigest
setters.doc: Describe the image with this digest (`--image-ids`); repeatable.

setters.name: tagStatus
setters.doc: Only images with this tag status (`--filter tagStatus=…`).

setters.name: repositoryNames
setters.doc: Only these repositories (`--repository-names`); all when omitted.

setters.name: registryId
setters.doc: The registry's account id, when not the caller's (`--registry-id`).

settings.name: AwsEcrGetLoginPasswordSettings
settings.doc:
Settings for `aws ecr get-login-password`.

The password is a registry credential, so the command always runs quietly
and the password is registered with the run's redactor once it returns.
Hand it to `docker login --password-stdin` (`DockerTasks.login` with
`.passwordStdin(...)`), never to `-p`.

setters.name: cluster
setters.doc: The cluster the services run in (`--cluster`).

setters.name: services
setters.doc: The services to describe (`--services`); repeatable.

settings.name: AwsEcsRegisterTaskDefinitionSettings
settings.doc:
Settings for `aws ecs register-task-definition`.

Either hand the whole definition over with cliInputJson — the usual
form, a `file://` path to a JSON document — or set the family and its
container definitions. Environment values in a container definition land
on the command line; keep secrets in the definition's `secrets` (Secrets
Manager or SSM references) rather than its `environment`.

setters.name: cliInputJson
setters.doc:
The whole request as JSON (`--cli-input-json`): a `file://` path to the
document, or the document itself.

setters.name: family
setters.doc: The task definition family (`--family`).

setters.name: containerDefinitions
setters.doc: The container definitions, as a JSON array or a `file://` path (`--container-definitions`).

setters.name: taskRoleArn
setters.doc: The role the task's containers assume (`--task-role-arn`).

setters.name: executionRoleArn
setters.doc: The role ECS uses to pull images and read secrets (`--execution-role-arn`).

setters.name: networkMode
setters.doc: The Docker networking mode (`--network-mode`), e.g. `"awsvpc"`.

setters.name: requiresCompatibilities
setters.doc: The launch types the definition must suit (`--requires-compatibilities`).

setters.name: cpu
setters.doc: CPU units for the task (`--cpu`), e.g. `"256"`.

setters.name: memory
setters.doc: Memory for the task in MiB (`--memory`), e.g. `"512"`.

setters.name: cluster
setters.doc: The cluster to run the task in (`--cluster`).

setters.name: taskDefinition
setters.doc: The task definition to run (`--task-definition`).

setters.name: count
setters.doc: How many copies to start (`--count`).

setters.name: launchType
setters.doc: The launch type (`--launch-type`): `"FARGATE"`, `"EC2"` or `"EXTERNAL"`.

setters.name: networkConfiguration
setters.doc: The `awsvpc` network configuration, as JSON (`--network-configuration`).

setters.name: overrides
setters.doc: Container overrides, as JSON (`--overrides`).

setters.name: startedBy
setters.doc: A label for who started the task (`--started-by`).

setters.name: group
setters.doc: The task group name (`--group`).

setters.name: cluster
setters.doc: The cluster the service runs in (`--cluster`); the default cluster when omitted.

setters.name: service
setters.doc: The service to update (`--service`).

setters.name: taskDefinition
setters.doc: The task definition to run, as `family:revision` or an ARN (`--task-definition`).

setters.name: desiredCount
setters.doc: How many tasks to keep running (`--desired-count`).

setters.name: forceNewDeployment
setters.doc: Start a new deployment even when nothing changed (`--force-new-deployment`).

setters.name: healthCheckGracePeriodSeconds
setters.doc: Seconds to ignore failing health checks after a task starts (`--health-check-grace-period-seconds`).

settings.name: AwsEcsWaitServicesStableSettings
settings.doc:
Settings for `aws ecs wait services-stable`: block until every named
service has its desired count running on one deployment. The CLI polls
every 15 seconds and gives up after 40 attempts with a non-zero exit, which
surfaces as a `CommandError`.

setters.name: cluster
setters.doc: The cluster the services run in (`--cluster`).

setters.name: services
setters.doc: The services to wait for (`--services`); repeatable.

setters.name: functionName
setters.doc: The function's name or ARN (`--function-name`).

setters.name: name
setters.doc: The alias to describe (`--name`), e.g. `"live"`.

setters.name: functionName
setters.doc: The function's name or ARN (`--function-name`).

setters.name: qualifier
setters.doc: A version or alias to describe instead of `$LATEST` (`--qualifier`).

settings.name: AwsLambdaInvokeSettings
settings.doc:
Settings for `aws lambda invoke`.

The function's response is written to the outfile; what the CLI
prints is the invocation's status. A function that throws still exits 0:
the CLI reports it in the printed `FunctionError` field, so read that (or
the outfile) before treating an invocation as a success.

setters.name: functionName
setters.doc: The function's name or ARN (`--function-name`).

setters.name: payload
setters.doc:
The event to send, as JSON text (`--payload`). AWS CLI v2 reads a payload
as base64 unless told otherwise, so this also passes
`--cli-binary-format raw-in-base64-out` to send the text as it is.

setters.name: invocationType
setters.doc: Wait for the response, queue the event, or only check access (`--invocation-type`).

setters.name: logType
setters.doc: `"Tail"` returns the last 4 KB of the execution log, base64-encoded (`--log-type`).

setters.name: qualifier
setters.doc: A version or alias to invoke (`--qualifier`).

setters.name: outfile
setters.doc: The file the function's response is written to (positional).

setters.name: functionName
setters.doc: The function's name or ARN (`--function-name`).

setters.name: description
setters.doc: A description of the version (`--description`).

setters.name: codeSha256
setters.doc: Publish only if the code still has this SHA-256 (`--code-sha256`).

setters.name: revisionId
setters.doc: Publish only if the function is still at this revision (`--revision-id`).

setters.name: functionName
setters.doc: The function's name or ARN (`--function-name`).

setters.name: name
setters.doc: The alias to move (`--name`), e.g. `"live"`.

setters.name: functionVersion
setters.doc: The version the alias points at (`--function-version`).

setters.name: description
setters.doc: A description of the alias (`--description`).

setters.name: additionalVersionWeight
revisionId
setters.doc:
Update only if the alias is still at this revision (`--revision-id`) — the
`RevisionId` a `get-alias` read, so a change made in between fails the
update instead of being overwritten.

setters.name: clearRouting
setters.doc:
Clear the alias's weighted routing, sending all traffic to its version
(`--routing-config` with no additional weights).

setters.name: functionName
setters.doc: The function's name or ARN (`--function-name`).

setters.name: zipFile
setters.doc:
The deployment package on disk (`--zip-file`). The CLI reads the file
when the path carries its `fileb://` prefix, which this adds unless the
path already has it.

setters.name: s3Bucket
setters.doc: The bucket holding the deployment package (`--s3-bucket`).

setters.name: s3Key
setters.doc: The package's key in that bucket (`--s3-key`).

setters.name: s3ObjectVersion
setters.doc: The package object's version (`--s3-object-version`).

setters.name: imageUri
setters.doc: The container image, for an image-packaged function (`--image-uri`).

setters.name: publish
setters.doc: Publish a new version once the code is updated (`--publish`).

setters.name: dryRun
setters.doc: Validate the request without updating the function (`--dry-run`).

setters.name: revisionId
setters.doc: Update only if the function is still at this revision (`--revision-id`).

setters.name: architectures
setters.doc: The instruction set architectures (`--architectures`), e.g. `"arm64"`.

setters.name: functionName
setters.doc: The function's name or ARN (`--function-name`).

setters.name: environment
setters.doc:
The function's environment variables (`--environment`). This **replaces**
the whole set — a variable left out is removed — and the values travel on
the command line, so keep secrets in Secrets Manager or SSM and pass their
names instead.

setters.name: timeout
setters.doc: The longest an invocation may run, in seconds (`--timeout`).

setters.name: memorySize
setters.doc: Memory for the function in MiB (`--memory-size`).

setters.name: handler
setters.doc: The handler entry point (`--handler`), e.g. `"index.handler"`.

setters.name: runtime
setters.doc: The runtime (`--runtime`), e.g. `"nodejs22.x"`.

setters.name: role
setters.doc: The execution role's ARN (`--role`).

setters.name: description
setters.doc: A description of the function (`--description`).

setters.name: layers
setters.doc: The layers to attach, by version ARN (`--layers`); replaces the set.

settings.name: AwsLambdaWaitSettings
settings.doc:
Settings for `aws lambda wait`: poll the function until it reaches the
state named, exiting non-zero — a `CommandError` — when it fails or the
waiter gives up.

setters.name: waiter
setters.doc: The state to wait for, e.g. `"published-version-active"`.

setters.name: functionName
setters.doc: The function's name or ARN (`--function-name`).

setters.name: qualifier
setters.doc: The version or alias to wait on (`--qualifier`).

setters.name: stackName
setters.doc: The stack to delete (`--stack-name`).

setters.name: roleArn
setters.doc: The role CloudFormation assumes to delete (`--role-arn`).

setters.name: retainResources
setters.doc: Logical ids to keep when a delete is retried (`--retain-resources`).

setters.name: templateFile
setters.doc: The template to deploy (`--template-file`).

setters.name: stackName
setters.doc: The stack to create or update (`--stack-name`).

setters.name: parameterOverride
setters.doc: Set a template parameter (`--parameter-overrides Key=Value`); repeatable.

setters.name: capabilities
setters.doc: Acknowledge what the template creates (`--capabilities`), e.g. `"CAPABILITY_IAM"`.

setters.name: tag
setters.doc: Tag the stack and its resources (`--tags Key=Value`); repeatable.

setters.name: noExecuteChangeset
setters.doc: Create the change set without executing it (`--no-execute-changeset`).

setters.name: noFailOnEmptyChangeset
setters.doc: Exit 0 when there is nothing to change (`--no-fail-on-empty-changeset`).

setters.name: roleArn
setters.doc: The role CloudFormation assumes to deploy (`--role-arn`).

setters.name: s3Bucket
setters.doc: The bucket a large template is uploaded to (`--s3-bucket`).

setters.name: s3Prefix
setters.doc: The key prefix for that upload (`--s3-prefix`).

setters.name: kmsKeyId
setters.doc: The KMS key that encrypts that upload (`--kms-key-id`).

setters.name: stackName
setters.doc: The stack to describe (`--stack-name`); every stack when omitted.

settings.name: AwsCloudformationWaitSettings
settings.doc:
Settings for `aws cloudformation wait <waiter>`: block until the stack
reaches the waiter's state. The CLI polls every 30 seconds and exits
non-zero after 120 attempts, or as soon as the stack lands in a failed
state — which surfaces as a `CommandError`.

setters.name: waiter
setters.doc: The state to wait for, e.g. `"stack-update-complete"`.

setters.name: stackName
setters.doc: The stack to wait on (`--stack-name`).

settings.name: AwsSecretsmanagerGetSecretValueSettings
settings.doc:
Settings for `aws secretsmanager get-secret-value`.

The response is the secret, so the command always runs quietly — captured,
never streamed — with `--output json` pinned, and the `SecretString` or
`SecretBinary` it returns is registered with the run's redactor.

setters.name: secretId
setters.doc: The secret's name or ARN (`--secret-id`).

setters.name: versionId
setters.doc: A specific version, by id (`--version-id`).

setters.name: versionStage
setters.doc: A specific version, by staging label (`--version-stage`); `AWSCURRENT` by default.

settings.name: AwsSsmGetParameterSettings
settings.doc:
Settings for `aws ssm get-parameter`.

A parameter may be a `SecureString`, so the command always runs quietly —
captured, never streamed — with `--output json` pinned, and the value it
returns is registered with the run's redactor.

setters.name: name
setters.doc: The parameter's name or ARN (`--name`).

setters.name: withDecryption

Return a `SecureString` decrypted (`--with-decryption`). Without it, a
`SecureString` comes back as ciphertext.

settings.name: AwsSsmPutParameterSettings
settings.doc:
Settings for `aws ssm put-parameter`.

`--value` is a command-line argument, which every user on the host can read
from the process table. For a `SecureString`, write the value to a file
with owner-only permissions and use valueFile: the CLI reads it, so
it never appears in the argv. A literal value given to a
`SecureString` is registered with the run's redactor, which masks Zuke's
own output but not the process table.

setters.name: name
setters.doc: The parameter's name (`--name`).

setters.name: value
setters.doc:
The value, given literally (`--value`). Refuses a value starting with
`file://` or `fileb://`: the CLI would read the named file rather than
store the text — use valueFile when that is the intent.

setters.name: valueFile
setters.doc:
Read the value from a file (`--value=file://<path>`), which keeps it off
the command line. The CLI stores the file's contents exactly, trailing
newline included.

setters.name: type
setters.doc: The parameter's type (`--type`).

setters.name: overwrite
setters.doc: Replace an existing parameter (`--overwrite`).

setters.name: keyId
setters.doc: The KMS key that encrypts a `SecureString` (`--key-id`).

setters.name: description

setters.name: tier

setters.name: dataType

setters.name: name

The kinds of alarm to return (`--alarm-types`): metric, composite or log

alarms only.

setters.name: scanBy

setters.name: maxDatapoints
setters.doc:
The most datapoints to return (`--max-datapoints`). Setting it turns off
the CLI's automatic pagination — the CLI treats it as a page size and
returns one page with a `NextToken` — so the answer may hold only part
of the window. `AwsTasks.metricValue` refuses it for that reason.

setters.name: namespace

setters.name: dimension

How to turn the series into one number (default `"latest"`, the newest

Return `value` when the series has no datapoints, instead of failing.

setters.name: logStreamNames
setters.doc: Only these streams (`--log-stream-names`); repeatable.

setters.doc: Only streams whose name starts with this (`--log-stream-name-prefix`).

settings.doc: Settings for `AwsTasks.logsInsightsQuery`: the query, and how long to wait for it.

setters.name: logGroupNames
setters.doc: The log groups to query (`--log-group-names`); repeatable.

setters.name: queryString

setters.name: startTime

setters.doc: The `duration` up to `end` — now, unless given — as the time range.

How long to wait for the query to finish (`"2m"`, or ms; default 5

settings.name: AzSettings
settings.doc:
Settings for an `az` invocation.

Every instance sets three of the CLI's configuration variables in the
child's environment, so the CLI never waits on a keypress, installs code,
or colours a build log:

- `AZURE_EXTENSION_USE_DYNAMIC_INSTALL=no` — a command from an extension
  that is not installed fails, instead of prompting (on a terminal) or
  silently downloading and installing the extension (without one). The
  CLI's message does not name the extension — it says the command `is
  misspelled or not recognized by the system` and exits 2 — so install what
  a build needs up front with `az extension add --name <name>`.
- `AZURE_CORE_LOGIN_EXPERIENCE_V2=off` — an interactive `az login` does not
  open its subscription selector.
- `AZURE_CORE_NO_COLOR=true` — no ANSI colour codes in captured output.

Setting them there keeps the argv exactly what the settings say; override
any of them with `.env({...})`. A confirmation prompt (`group delete`
without `--yes`) is not switched off: on a terminal it asks, without one
the CLI fails — call the command's `.yes()` to confirm in the build.

setters.name: subscription
setters.doc:
The subscription to run against, by name or id (`--subscription`); the
CLI's default subscription when omitted. Most commands take it; the
`account` commands read it as the subscription they act on.

setters.name: output
setters.doc:
The output format (`--output`): `json`, `jsonc`, `yaml`, `yamlc`,
`table`, `tsv` or `none`.

setters.name: query
setters.doc: A JMESPath expression that filters the output (`--query`).

setters.name: onlyShowErrors
setters.doc:
Print errors only, suppressing warnings (`--only-show-errors`). The CLI
refuses it beside `--debug` or `--verbose`, and so do these settings.

setters.name: verbose
setters.doc: More logging, on stderr (`--verbose`).

setters.name: env
setters.doc:
Merge additional environment variables for the process. Under
debug — set before or after — a credential variable set here is
registered with the run's redactor, like one in the build's environment.

setters.name: debug
setters.doc:
Turn on the CLI's debug logging (`--debug`), written to stderr.

**The debug log can carry credentials**: request and response details,
which for a Key Vault or storage command include what was read or sent.
The credentials the CLI reads from the environment — `AZURE_STORAGE_KEY`,
`AZURE_STORAGE_CONNECTION_STRING`, `AZURE_STORAGE_SAS_TOKEN`,
`AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET`, `AZURE_DEVOPS_EXT_PAT`, and Terraform's
`ARM_CLIENT_SECRET` beside them — are registered with the run's redactor,
whether they are in the build's environment or set with env, but a token the CLI holds in its own cache
(`~/.azure`) is not known here and is not masked. Keep it for a local
investigation, never a shared CI log.

setters.name: flag
setters.doc:
Add an arbitrary option: `--name value`, or the bare `--name`.

Two hazards come with the escape hatch, which the typed setters guard and
this does not: a value that starts with `-` is read by the CLI as the next
option, and a value that starts with `@` — or, in a `key=value` list
element, a value after the `=` that does — is replaced by that file's
contents (`@-` by standard input), which then leave the machine in the
request. Never pass an untrusted value here, or through `.args(...)` or
`.command(...)`.

settings.name: AzLoginSettings
settings.doc:
Settings for `az login`, for the non-interactive forms a build uses. The
interactive browser and device-code forms are left to `.command("login")`.

Exactly one credential is sent: a secret (password), a
certificate or a federatedToken for a service principal,
or identity for a managed identity. A service principal without
one would make the CLI prompt for a password, so it is refused here.

`az login` reads the global `.subscription(...)` as the subscription to
make the default once it has signed in. Its output lists the account's
subscriptions — no credential — so it is not masked.

The service principal's client secret (`--password`), sent on standard

the run's redactor. Prefer federatedToken (no long-lived secret)
or certificate.

settings.name: AzAcrBuildSettings
settings.doc:
Settings for `az acr build`: build an image in the registry from a local
directory, a git URL or a tarball, and push it.

`--build-arg` values are visible to the ACR team for debugging, as the CLI
warns; pass a credential with secretBuildArg, whose value is also
registered with the run's redactor.

setters.name: registry
setters.doc: The registry to build in (`--registry`).

setters.name: source
setters.doc: The build context: a directory, a git URL or a tarball URL (the positional source).

setters.name: image
setters.doc: A `name:tag` to give the image (`--image`); repeatable.

setters.name: file
setters.doc: The Dockerfile, relative to the source (`--file`).

setters.name: buildArg
setters.doc: A build argument (`--build-arg name=value`); repeatable. Never a credential.

setters.name: secretBuildArg
setters.doc:
A build argument the ACR team does not see (`--secret-build-arg
name=value`); repeatable. The value is registered with the run's
redactor; it is still part of the argv.

setters.name: platform
setters.doc: The platform to build for (`--platform`), e.g. `"linux/arm64"`.

setters.name: target
setters.doc: The Dockerfile stage to build (`--target`).

setters.name: timeout
setters.doc: The build's timeout in seconds (`--timeout`).

setters.name: resourceGroup
setters.doc: The registry's resource group (`--resource-group`).

setters.name: noPush
setters.doc: Build without pushing (`--no-push`).

setters.name: noLogs
setters.doc: Do not stream the build's logs (`--no-logs`).

setters.name: noWait
setters.doc: Return once the build is queued (`--no-wait`).

settings.name: AzAcrLoginSettings
settings.doc:
Settings for `az acr login`.

Without exposeToken the CLI logs the local Docker client in itself.
With it, the CLI prints a registry refresh token instead — for
`docker login` with the user `00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000` — so the
command always runs quietly with `--output json` pinned, and the token is
registered with the run's redactor once it returns.

setters.name: name
setters.doc: The registry's name (`--name`).

setters.name: exposeToken
setters.doc: Print a token instead of logging Docker in (`--expose-token`).

setters.name: username
setters.doc: A registry user, instead of the signed-in identity (`--username`).

setters.name: password
setters.doc:
The registry user's password (`--password`), sent on standard input as
`--password=@-` so it never enters the argv, and registered with the
run's redactor.

setters.name: suffix
setters.doc: The tenant suffix of the registry's login server (`--suffix`).

settings.name: AzAcrRepositoryDeleteSettings
settings.doc:
Settings for `az acr repository delete`: one image, by tag or digest, or a
whole repository. The CLI asks for confirmation unless yes is set.

setters.name: name
setters.doc: The registry's name (`--name`).

setters.name: image
setters.doc: The image to delete, `repo:tag` or `repo@digest` (`--image`).

setters.name: repository
setters.doc: Delete the whole repository, every tag in it (`--repository`).

setters.name: yes
setters.doc: Delete without asking (`--yes`).

setters.name: name
setters.doc: The registry's name (`--name`).

setters.name: repository
setters.doc: The repository whose tags to list (`--repository`).

setters.name: top
setters.doc: At most this many tags (`--top`).

setters.name: orderby
setters.doc: Order by time, oldest or newest first (`--orderby`); by name otherwise.

setters.name: detail
setters.doc: Each tag's details, not only its name (`--detail`).

settings.name: AzAksGetCredentialsSettings
settings.doc:
Settings for `az aks get-credentials`. The credentials go to a file —
`~/.kube/config` unless file says otherwise. Printing them
(`--file -`) would put a cluster credential in the build log, so a `-` is
refused.

setters.name: admin
setters.doc: Get the cluster-admin credentials (`--admin`).

setters.name: file
setters.doc: The kubeconfig file to write (`--file`); `~/.kube/config` by default.

setters.name: overwriteExisting
setters.doc: Replace an existing entry of the same name (`--overwrite-existing`).

setters.name: context
setters.doc: The context name to write, instead of the cluster's (`--context`).

setters.name: publicFqdn
setters.doc: Point the kubeconfig at the cluster's public FQDN (`--public-fqdn`).

setters.name: format
setters.doc: The credential format (`--format`): `azure` or `exec` (kubelogin).

settings.name: AzContainerappIngressTrafficSetSettings

setters.name: revisionWeight
setters.doc:
A revision's share of traffic, in percent (`--revision-weight
revision=weight`); repeatable. `"latest"` is the newest revision.

setters.name: labelWeight
setters.doc: A label's share of traffic, in percent (`--label-weight label=weight`); repeatable.

setters.name: all
setters.doc: Include inactive revisions (`--all`).

settings.name: AzContainerappRevisionSettings
settings.doc:
Settings for `az containerapp revision activate` and `deactivate`: the
app, and the revision to switch.

setters.name: revision
setters.doc: The revision to activate or deactivate (`--revision`).

settings.name: AzContainerappShowSettings
settings.doc: Settings for `az containerapp show`. Secrets stay out: `--show-secrets` is not typed.

settings.name: AzContainerappUpdateSettings
settings.doc:
Settings for `az containerapp update`: a new image, environment or scale,
which makes a new revision.

setters.name: image
setters.doc: The container image (`--image`), e.g. `"myregistry.azurecr.io/api:1.4.0"`.

setters.name: containerName
setters.doc: The container to update, when the app has several (`--container-name`).

setters.name: revisionSuffix
setters.doc: A suffix for the new revision's name (`--revision-suffix`).

setters.name: setEnvVar
removeEnvVars
setters.doc: Remove environment variables (`--remove-env-vars`); repeatable.

setters.name: cpu
setters.doc: CPU cores for the container (`--cpu`), e.g. `0.5`.

setters.name: memory
setters.doc: Memory for the container (`--memory`), e.g. `"1.0Gi"`.

setters.name: minReplicas
setters.doc: The fewest replicas (`--min-replicas`).

setters.name: maxReplicas
setters.doc: The most replicas (`--max-replicas`).

setters.name: yaml
setters.doc: Take the whole configuration from a YAML file (`--yaml`); other options are ignored.

settings.name: AzWebappConfigAppsettingsSetSettings
settings.doc:
Settings for `az webapp config appsettings set`.

Each setting's value is part of the argv, so it is visible in the process
table and in the command line the build logs; a credential belongs in Key
Vault, referenced with keyVaultReference. A value that starts with
`@` is otherwise refused, because the CLI would read it from a file. The
CLI's answer lists every setting with its value redacted.

setters.name: setting
setters.doc: An app setting (`--settings name=value`); repeatable.

setters.name: keyVaultReference
setters.doc:
An app setting whose value App Service reads from Key Vault; repeatable.
Sent as the JSON object `{"name":"@Microsoft.KeyVault(SecretUri=<uri>)"}`,
a form `--settings` accepts: written as `name=@Microsoft…` the CLI would
first try to read a file of that name, and send its contents if one
existed.

setters.name: slotSetting
setters.doc:
A setting that stays with its slot through a swap (`--slot-settings
name=value`); repeatable.

setters.name: slot
setters.doc: A slot instead of production (`--slot`).

settings.name: AzWebappDeploymentSlotSwapSettings
settings.doc:
Settings for `az webapp deployment slot swap`: swap a slot with production,
or with targetSlot.

setters.name: slot
setters.doc: The slot to swap from (`--slot`).

setters.name: targetSlot
setters.doc: The slot to swap with; production by default (`--target-slot`).

setters.name: action
setters.doc:
`preview` applies the target's settings to the source first, `swap`
completes the swap, `reset` cancels a preview (`--action`).

setters.name: preserveVnet
setters.doc: Keep the virtual network with the slot (`--preserve-vnet`).

settings.name: AzWebappDeploySettings
settings.doc:
Settings for `az webapp deploy`, the current deploy command (the older
`webapp deployment source config-zip` is deprecated in its favour).

setters.name: srcPath
setters.doc: The artifact to deploy, a local path (`--src-path`).

setters.name: srcUrl
setters.doc: The artifact to deploy, a URL the app pulls it from (`--src-url`).

setters.name: type
setters.doc: The artifact's type, when its extension does not say (`--type`).

setters.name: targetPath
setters.doc: Where to deploy it, an absolute path on the app (`--target-path`).

setters.name: slot
setters.doc: The slot to deploy to; production when omitted (`--slot`).

setters.name: async
setters.doc: Return once the artifact is pushed, without waiting for it to deploy (`--async`).

setters.name: restart
setters.doc: Restart the app after deploying (`--restart`); the CLI's default is to.

setters.name: clean
setters.doc: Empty the target directory first (`--clean`).

setters.name: timeout
setters.doc: How long to wait for the deployment, in milliseconds (`--timeout`).

setters.name: slot
setters.doc: A slot instead of production (`--slot`).

settings.name: AzFunctionappDeploymentSourceConfigZipSettings

setters.name: src
setters.doc: The zip package (`--src`).

setters.name: buildRemote
setters.doc: Build the package on the service — install dependencies there (`--build-remote`).

setters.name: timeout
setters.doc: How long to wait for the deployment's status, in seconds (`--timeout`).

setters.name: slot
setters.doc: A slot instead of production (`--slot`).

settings.name: AzKeyvaultSecretSetSettings
settings.doc:
Settings for `az keyvault secret set`.

The value comes from a file — read exactly, with its
encoding — or from value, which is sent on standard input
as `--value=@-` so it never enters the argv. The CLI strips trailing line
breaks from what it reads that way; use a file for a value that must keep
them.

setters.name: vaultName
setters.doc: The vault's name (`--vault-name`).

setters.name: name
setters.doc: The secret's name (`--name`).

setters.name: value
setters.doc:
The value, sent on standard input as `--value=@-` and registered with the
run's redactor.

setters.name: file
setters.doc: Read the value from a file (`--file`) — the way to keep it exact.

setters.name: encoding
setters.doc:
How the file is encoded (`--encoding`); `utf-8` by default.
Refused without a file: the CLI saves it as a `file-encoding` tag that
`keyvault secret download` later decodes with.

setters.name: contentType
setters.doc: What the value is, e.g. `"password"` (`--content-type`).

setters.name: expires
setters.doc:
When the secret expires (`--expires`): a `Date`, or a string such as
`2027-01-01T00:00:00Z` — the CLI takes UTC to the second, no fractions.

setters.name: notBefore
setters.doc: When the secret becomes usable (`--not-before`), in the same form as expires.

setters.name: disabled
setters.doc: Create the secret disabled, or enabled (`--disabled`).

setters.name: tag
setters.doc: A tag (`--tags key=value`); repeatable.

setters.name: vaultName
setters.doc: The vault's name (`--vault-name`).

setters.name: name
setters.doc: The secret's name (`--name`).

setters.name: version
setters.doc: A specific version; the latest when omitted (`--version`).

setters.name: id
setters.doc: The secret's full identifier, instead of vault and name (`--id`).

settings.name: AzDeploymentGroupTemplateSettings
settings.doc:
The template, parameters and mode a deploying `deployment group` command
shares — `create` and `what-if` read them identically. The deployment's
`--name` is optional here; the CLI defaults it to the template file's name.

setters.name: templateFile
setters.doc: A local ARM template or Bicep file (`--template-file`).

setters.name: templateUri
setters.doc: A template at a URL (`--template-uri`).

setters.name: templateSpec
setters.doc: A template spec, by resource id (`--template-spec`).

setters.name: parametersFile
setters.doc:
A parameters file — JSON or `.bicepparam` (`--parameters <path>`);
repeatable, later values winning.

setters.name: parameter
setters.doc:
One parameter (`--parameters name=value`); repeatable. The value is
converted to the type the template declares. It is part of the argv, so a
secure value belongs in a parameters file or a Key Vault reference.

setters.name: mode
setters.doc: `Incremental` (the default) or `Complete`, which deletes what the template omits (`--mode`).

setters.name: noWait
setters.doc: Return once the deployment has started (`--no-wait`).

settings.name: AzDeploymentGroupWhatIfSettings
settings.doc: Settings for `az deployment group what-if`: what a deployment would change.

setters.name: resultFormat
setters.doc: How much of each change to show (`--result-format`).

setters.name: excludeChangeTypes
setters.doc: Leave these kinds of change out (`--exclude-change-types`); repeatable.

setters.name: noPrettyPrint
setters.doc: Print the result as JSON rather than the formatted diff (`--no-pretty-print`).

settings.name: AzStorageBlobSettings
settings.doc:
The account and credential options every `storage blob` command takes.
One credential at most: the CLI reads it from standard input.

setters.name: accountName
setters.doc: The storage account (`--account-name`).

setters.name: authMode
setters.doc: `login` uses the signed-in identity; `key` an account key (`--auth-mode`).

setters.name: accountKey
setters.doc: The account key (`--account-key`), sent on standard input.

setters.name: sasToken
setters.doc:
A SAS token (`--sas-token`), sent on standard input. Its signature is
registered on its own as well — as written, decoded and URL-encoded —
since the CLI's debug log prints the token URL-encoded inside a request
URL, where the token as a whole never appears.

setters.name: connectionString
setters.doc: A connection string (`--connection-string`), sent on standard input.

setters.name: containerName
setters.doc: The container (`--container-name`).

setters.name: name
setters.doc: The blob's name (`--name`).

setters.name: file
setters.doc: The local file to write (`--file`).

setters.name: overwrite
setters.doc: Replace an existing local file (`--overwrite`).

settings.name: AzStorageBlobUploadBatchSettings
settings.doc: Settings for `az storage blob upload-batch`: upload a directory.

setters.name: source
setters.doc: The local directory to upload (`--source`).

setters.name: destination
setters.doc: The container, by name or URL (`--destination`).

setters.name: pattern
setters.doc: Upload only the files matching this glob (`--pattern`).

setters.name: destinationPath
setters.doc: A path inside the container to upload under (`--destination-path`).

setters.name: overwrite
setters.doc: Replace existing blobs (`--overwrite`).

setters.name: dryrun
setters.doc: Show what would be uploaded without uploading (`--dryrun`).

setters.name: containerName
setters.doc: The container (`--container-name`).

setters.name: name
setters.doc: The blob's name (`--name`).

setters.name: file
setters.doc: The local file to upload (`--file`).

setters.name: overwrite
setters.doc: Replace an existing blob (`--overwrite`).

setters.name: contentType
setters.doc: The blob's MIME type (`--content-type`).

setters.name: contentCacheControl
setters.doc: The blob's `Cache-Control` (`--content-cache-control`).

setters.name: tag
setters.doc: A blob index tag (`--tags key=value`); repeatable.

settings.name: AzMonitorActivityLogListSettings
settings.doc:
Settings for `az monitor activity-log list`: the control-plane events of a
subscription, resource group or resource. The CLI returns at most
maxEvents — 50 unless told otherwise.

setters.name: startTime
setters.doc: The start of the range (`--start-time`).

setters.name: endTime
setters.doc: The end of the range (`--end-time`); now by default.

setters.name: offset
setters.doc: The length of the range when only one end is given (`--offset`); six hours by default.

setters.name: resourceGroup
setters.doc: Only events in this resource group (`--resource-group`).

setters.name: resourceId
setters.doc: Only events on this resource (`--resource-id`).

setters.name: namespace
setters.doc: Only events from this resource provider (`--namespace`).

setters.name: caller
setters.doc: Only events by this caller (`--caller`).

setters.name: status
setters.doc: Only events with this status, e.g. `"Failed"` (`--status`).

setters.name: correlationId
setters.doc: Only the events of this operation (`--correlation-id`).

setters.name: maxEvents
setters.doc: The most events to return (`--max-events`); 50 by default.

setters.name: select
setters.doc: Only these properties of each event (`--select`); repeatable.

settings.name: AzMonitorMetricsAlertListSettings
settings.doc: Settings for `az monitor metrics alert list`.

setters.name: resourceGroup
setters.doc: Only the rules in this resource group (`--resource-group`).

settings.name: AzMonitorMetricsAlertShowSettings
settings.doc:
Settings for `az monitor metrics alert show`: one metric alert rule. The
rule's definition, not whether it is firing — that lives in Azure Monitor's
alerts, not in the rule.

settings.name: AzMonitorMetricsListDefinitionsSettings
settings.doc: Settings for `az monitor metrics list-definitions`: the metrics a resource has.

setters.name: resource
setters.doc: The resource, by full resource id (`--resource`).

setters.name: namespace
setters.doc: Only this metric namespace (`--namespace`).

settings.name: AzMonitorMetricsListSettings
settings.doc:
Settings for `az monitor metrics list`: a resource's metrics over a time
range, one datapoint per interval.

The CLI returns at most top time series per metric — ten unless
told otherwise — so a query that splits by a dimension can silently lose
series; raise `top` to cover them.

setters.name: resource
setters.doc: The resource, by full resource id (`--resource`).

setters.name: metrics
setters.doc: The metrics to read, by name (`--metrics`); repeatable.

setters.name: aggregation
setters.doc: The aggregations to compute per interval (`--aggregation`); repeatable.

setters.name: interval
setters.doc:
The time grain of each datapoint (`--interval`); one minute by default.
The range set by window is not aligned to it, so the newest
datapoint may cover an interval that is still being written.

setters.name: startTime
setters.doc: The start of the range (`--start-time`).

setters.name: endTime
setters.doc: The end of the range (`--end-time`); now by default.

setters.name: window
setters.doc:
The `duration` (`"15m"`, or milliseconds) up to `end` — now, unless
given — as `--start-time` and `--end-time`.

setters.name: offset
setters.doc:
The length of the range when only one end is given (`--offset`, as
`"30m"` or milliseconds); an hour by default.

setters.name: filter
setters.doc:
An OData filter on the dimensions (`--filter`), e.g.
`"ApiName eq 'GetBlob' and GeoType eq '*'"`. For plain equality, prefer
dimension, which quotes the value.

setters.name: dimension
setters.doc:
Only the series where the dimension `name` is `value` — rendered into
`--filter` as `name eq 'value'`, joined with `and`; repeatable.

setters.name: splitBy
setters.doc: Split the series by these dimensions (`--dimension`); repeatable.

setters.name: namespace
setters.doc: The metric namespace (`--namespace`).

setters.name: top
setters.doc: The most time series to return per metric (`--top`); 10 by default.

setters.name: orderby
setters.doc: The aggregation and direction to sort series by (`--orderby`), e.g. `"sum desc"`.

settings.name: AzMonitorMetricValueSettings
settings.doc:
Settings for `AzTasks.metricValue`: a `metrics list` request with exactly
one AzMonitorMetricsListSettings.aggregation, and how to read it.

setters.name: metric
setters.doc:
The metric to read, by name. Needed only when the request names more
than one with `.metrics(...)`.

setters.name: aggregate
setters.doc:
How to turn the datapoints into one number, across every series the
answer holds. `"latest"` (the default) is the newest interval — the sum
of the series' values at the newest timestamp any of them has, so a
metric split by a dimension reads as its total. The others combine every
datapoint in the range: a `"sum"` of per-minute `Total`s is the range's
total.

setters.name: missingDataAs
setters.doc:
Return `value` when there are no datapoints, instead of failing. Azure
Monitor reports an interval with no events without a value, so for a
count of errors no data does mean `0`; for a latency it usually means the
query is looking in the wrong place.

setters.name: workspace
setters.doc: The workspace's id — its customer id, a GUID (`--workspace`).

setters.name: analyticsQuery
setters.doc: The KQL query (`--analytics-query`).

setters.name: timespan
setters.doc:
The range to query (`--timespan`): a duration back from now, as `"30m"`
or milliseconds (sent as ISO 8601), or an ISO 8601 interval string such
as `"2026-10-07T10:00:00Z/2026-10-07T11:00:00Z"`, sent as written. All
the data by default.

setters.name: workspaces
setters.doc: Further workspaces to union into the query (`--workspaces`); repeatable.

packages.name: git
packages.summary: `@zuke/git` — typed `git` task wrappers for Zuke builds.

tasks.name: GitTasks
tasks.doc: Typed task functions for the `git` commands.

tasks.name: init
tasks.doc: Create a repository: `git init`.

tasks.name: clone
tasks.doc: Clone a repository: `git clone`.

tasks.name: add
tasks.doc: Stage changes: `git add`.

tasks.name: rm
tasks.doc: Remove tracked files: `git rm`.

tasks.name: mv
tasks.doc: Move or rename a tracked file: `git mv`.

tasks.name: restore
tasks.doc: Restore working-tree or index contents: `git restore`.

tasks.name: clean
tasks.doc: Delete untracked files: `git clean`.

tasks.name: commit
tasks.doc: Record changes: `git commit`.

tasks.name: status
tasks.doc: Show working-tree status: `git status`.

tasks.name: statusEntries
tasks.doc:
The working tree's changes as parsed GitStatusEntry values, from
`git status --porcelain -z` — the form no path can corrupt. An empty array
means a clean tree.

The lambda configures the rest (`.dir()`, `.untrackedFiles()`, `.paths()`);
the output format is fixed, since the parse depends on it.

tasks.name: checkout
tasks.doc: Switch branches or restore files: `git checkout`.

tasks.name: switch
tasks.doc: Switch branches: `git switch`, `checkout`'s modern half.

tasks.name: branch
tasks.doc: Manage branches: `git branch`.

tasks.name: tag
tasks.doc: Manage tags: `git tag`.

tasks.name: push
tasks.doc: Update remote refs: `git push`.

tasks.name: pull
tasks.doc: Fetch and integrate: `git pull`.

tasks.name: fetch
tasks.doc: Download objects and refs: `git fetch`.

tasks.name: remote
tasks.doc: Manage remotes: `git remote add|remove|rename|set-url|get-url|show|prune`.

tasks.name: remoteList
tasks.doc:
The configured remotes as parsed GitRemote entries, each with the
fetch and push URL folded together, from `git remote --verbose`.

tasks.name: lsRemote
tasks.doc: List a remote's refs without fetching them: `git ls-remote`.

tasks.name: log
tasks.doc: Show history: `git log`.

tasks.name: logEntries
tasks.doc:
History as parsed GitCommitEntry values — SHA, parents, author,
dates, subject, and body — for building a changelog or deciding what a
range contains.

The lambda configures the walk (`.range()`, `.maxCount()`, `.paths()`);
the `--format` is fixed, since the parse depends on it.

tasks.name: show
tasks.doc: Show an object: `git show`.

tasks.name: diff
tasks.doc: Show changes: `git diff`.

tasks.name: diffNames
tasks.doc:
The changed paths of a diff, from `git diff --name-only -z`. What a target
needs to decide whether the work it guards has to run at all.

tasks.name: lsFiles
tasks.doc: List index and working-tree files: `git ls-files`.

tasks.name: lsFileNames
tasks.doc:
The paths of a `git ls-files -z` listing — git's own file list, ignore
rules already applied.

tasks.name: revParse
tasks.doc: Resolve revisions and repository paths: `git rev-parse`.

tasks.name: revision
tasks.doc:
A `git rev-parse` result as a trimmed string — the commit SHA, ref name,
or path a version stamp or cache key is built from.

tasks.name: describe
tasks.doc: Name a commit after the nearest tag: `git describe`.

tasks.name: merge
tasks.doc: Join two histories: `git merge`.

tasks.name: rebase
tasks.doc: Replay commits onto another base: `git rebase`.

tasks.name: cherryPick
tasks.doc: Apply existing commits here: `git cherry-pick`.

tasks.name: revert
tasks.doc: Undo commits with new ones: `git revert`.

tasks.name: reset
tasks.doc: Move the branch, index, and optionally the working tree: `git reset`.

tasks.name: stash
tasks.doc: Park and restore uncommitted work: `git stash`.

tasks.name: config
tasks.doc: Read or write configuration: `git config`.

tasks.name: configGet
tasks.doc:
One configuration value, or `undefined` when the key is unset — which
`git config --get` reports as a non-zero exit rather than as empty output.
The lambda must pick the key with `.get(...)` or `.getAll(...)`.

tasks.name: submodule
tasks.doc: Manage submodules: `git submodule add|init|update|sync|status|foreach`.

tasks.name: archive
tasks.doc: Package a tree as a tarball or zip: `git archive`.

tasks.name: apply
tasks.doc: Apply a patch file: `git apply`.

tasks.name: worktree
tasks.doc:
Manage worktrees: `git worktree add|list|remove|prune`. Pick the
subcommand in the lambda — `s.add(path)`, `s.list()`, `s.remove(path)`, or
`s.prune()`. For a listing to read rather than print, use
GitTasksApi.worktreeList.

tasks.name: worktreeList
tasks.doc:
List the repository's worktrees as parsed GitWorktree entries,
from `git worktree list --porcelain`.

The lambda configures the global options (`.dir()`, `.config()`); the
subcommand itself is fixed, since the parse depends on it.

tasks.name: defaultBranch
tasks.doc:
The name of a remote's default branch — `main`, `master`, or whatever it
chose — so a build does not have to hardcode one.

Reads the local `refs/remotes/<remote>/HEAD` first, which costs no network,
and asks the remote itself when that ref was never populated. Fails when
neither names a branch, rather than guessing.

tasks.name: mergeBase
tasks.doc: Find the common ancestor of commits: `git merge-base`.

tasks.name: isAncestor
tasks.doc:
Whether the first commit is an ancestor of the second:
`git merge-base --is-ancestor`, read back from its exit status.

tasks.name: revList
tasks.doc: Walk history as a list of commits: `git rev-list`.

tasks.name: commitCount
tasks.doc: How many commits the walk holds: `git rev-list --count`.

tasks.name: forEachRef
tasks.doc: List refs with a format: `git for-each-ref`.

tasks.name: refs
tasks.doc: The refs and what they point at, parsed: `git for-each-ref`.

tasks.name: showRef
tasks.doc: List or verify local refs: `git show-ref`.

tasks.name: symbolicRef
tasks.doc: Read or set a symbolic ref: `git symbolic-ref`.

tasks.name: nameRev
tasks.doc: Find symbolic names for commits: `git name-rev`.

tasks.name: lsTree
tasks.doc: List the contents of a tree: `git ls-tree`.

tasks.name: treeEntries
tasks.doc: The entries of a tree, parsed: `git ls-tree -z`.

tasks.name: catFile
tasks.doc: Read an object's contents or attributes: `git cat-file`.

tasks.name: blobText
tasks.doc: An object's contents as text, untrimmed: `git cat-file -p`.

tasks.name: checkIgnore
tasks.doc: Report which paths the ignore rules exclude: `git check-ignore`.

tasks.name: isIgnored
tasks.doc:
Whether a path is excluded, read from the exit status of
`git check-ignore`.

tasks.name: blame
tasks.doc: Annotate a file's lines with their commits: `git blame`.

tasks.name: blameLines
tasks.doc: The annotated lines, parsed: `git blame --porcelain`.

tasks.name: shortlog
tasks.doc: Summarise commits by contributor: `git shortlog`.

tasks.name: shortlogEntries
tasks.doc: The per-contributor commit counts, parsed: `git shortlog -s`.

tasks.name: grep
tasks.doc: Search tracked content: `git grep`.

tasks.name: verifyCommit
tasks.doc: Check a commit's signature: `git verify-commit`.

tasks.name: verifyTag
tasks.doc: Check a tag's signature: `git verify-tag`.

tasks.name: isSignatureValid
tasks.doc: Whether a commit's signature is good: `git verify-commit`.

tasks.name: isTagSignatureValid
tasks.doc: Whether a tag's signature is good: `git verify-tag`.

tasks.name: mergeTree
tasks.doc:
Merge in memory, leaving the index and working tree alone:
`git merge-tree`.

tasks.name: mergesCleanly
tasks.doc: Whether two commits merge without conflict: `git merge-tree`.

tasks.name: run
tasks.doc: Run any other git command via `.command(...)`.

settings.name: GitSettings
settings.doc: Shared base for every `git` subcommand: the binary and global options.

setters.name: dir
setters.doc: Run git as if started in `path` (`-C <path>`).

setters.name: config
setters.doc: Set a one-off config value (`-c key=value`); repeatable.

setters.name: revisions
setters.doc: Revisions to walk (positional), e.g. `HEAD` or `origin/main`; repeatable.

setters.name: range
setters.doc:
Walk the commits in `from..to` — what is on `to` and not on `from`, the
range a changelog since the last tag is built from. `to` defaults to
`HEAD`.

setters.name: paths
setters.doc: Limit the walk to these pathspecs (positional, after `--`); repeatable.

setters.name: maxCount
setters.doc: Stop after this many commits (`--max-count=<n>`).

setters.name: skip
setters.doc: Skip this many commits before reporting any (`--skip=<n>`).

setters.name: oneline
setters.doc: One abbreviated line per commit (`--oneline`).

setters.name: format
setters.doc:
Render each commit through a format string (`--format=<fmt>`), e.g.
`%H %s`. Given after oneline, so it wins when both are set.

setters.name: since
setters.doc: Only commits more recent than this date (`--since=<date>`).

setters.name: until
setters.doc: Only commits older than this date (`--until=<date>`).

setters.name: author
setters.doc: Only commits whose author matches this pattern (`--author=`); repeatable.

setters.name: grep
setters.doc: Only commits whose message matches this pattern (`--grep=`); repeatable.

setters.name: noMerges
setters.doc: Skip merge commits (`--no-merges`).

setters.name: firstParent
setters.doc: Follow only the first parent of a merge (`--first-parent`).

setters.name: reverse
setters.doc: Report oldest first (`--reverse`).

setters.name: follow
setters.doc: Keep following a single file across renames (`--follow`).

setters.name: object
setters.doc:
The objects to show (positional); repeatable. A commit, a tag, or a blob
at a revision such as `HEAD:deno.json` — the way a build reads a file as
it was, without checking anything out.

setters.name: paths
setters.doc: Limit the output to these pathspecs (positional, after `--`); repeatable.

setters.name: format
setters.doc: Render the commit header through a format string (`--format=<fmt>`).

setters.name: noPatch
setters.doc: Suppress the diff (`--no-patch`), leaving only the header.

setters.name: nameOnly
setters.doc: List the changed paths instead of the diff (`--name-only`).

setters.name: nameStatus
setters.doc: List the changed paths with their status letters (`--name-status`).

setters.name: stat
setters.doc: Summarise the changes (`--stat`).

setters.name: commits
setters.doc:
The commits to compare (positional); repeatable. One rev diffs the working
tree against it; two diff them against each other.

setters.name: mergeBase
setters.doc:
Compare the two ends of a range — `from...to` with three dots, which diffs
`to` against the point the two branches last shared. That is the diff a
pull request shows, and the one a review or an "affected" check wants,
since it excludes whatever landed on the base branch meanwhile.

setters.name: paths
setters.doc: Limit the diff to these pathspecs (positional, after `--`); repeatable.

setters.name: staged
setters.doc: Diff the index against `HEAD` rather than the working tree (`--staged`).

setters.name: nameOnly
setters.doc: List the changed paths instead of the patch (`--name-only`).

setters.name: nameStatus
setters.doc: List the changed paths with their status letters (`--name-status`).

setters.name: stat
setters.doc: Summarise the changes per file (`--stat`).

setters.name: shortstat
setters.doc: One summary line for the whole diff (`--shortstat`).

setters.name: unified
setters.doc: Lines of context around each hunk (`--unified=<n>`).

setters.name: ignoreAllSpace
setters.doc: Ignore whitespace entirely when comparing (`--ignore-all-space`).

setters.name: exitCode
setters.doc:
Report differences through the exit code (`--exit-code`): 1 when there are
any, 0 when there are none. Pair it with `.noThrow()` to branch on
`output.code` instead of catching.

setters.name: diffFilter
setters.doc:
Keep only files whose change matches these status letters
(`--diff-filter=<letters>`), e.g. `ACM` for added, copied, and modified —
how a lint target skips paths the diff only deleted.

setters.name: nulTerminated
setters.doc: Terminate output records with a NUL rather than a newline (`-z`).

setters.name: paths
setters.doc: Limit the listing to these pathspecs (positional); repeatable.

setters.name: cached
setters.doc: List files in the index (`--cached`), git's default.

setters.name: modified
setters.doc: List files modified in the working tree (`--modified`).

setters.name: deleted
setters.doc: List files deleted from the working tree (`--deleted`).

setters.name: others
setters.doc:
List untracked files (`--others`). Pair it with excludeStandard,
or the listing includes everything `.gitignore` covers.

setters.name: ignored
setters.doc: List ignored files (`--ignored`); only meaningful with others.

setters.name: stage
setters.doc: Show the mode, object name, and stage of each entry (`--stage`).

setters.name: excludeStandard
setters.doc: Apply the standard ignore rules (`--exclude-standard`).

setters.name: directory
setters.doc: Report an untracked directory once rather than every file in it (`--directory`).

setters.name: errorUnmatch
setters.doc:
Exit non-zero when a pathspec matches nothing (`--error-unmatch`), which
is how a build asserts that a path is tracked rather than reading the
listing to see whether it came back empty.

git only applies it to the paths it was given, so it needs
paths — the flag on its own describes a whole-tree listing, which
always matches something.

setters.name: nulTerminated
setters.doc: Terminate each entry with a NUL rather than a newline (`-z`).

setters.name: commitish
setters.doc: The commit to describe (positional); defaults to `HEAD`.

setters.name: tags
setters.doc: Consider lightweight tags too, not only annotated ones (`--tags`).

setters.name: all
setters.doc: Consider every ref, not only tags (`--all`).

setters.name: always
setters.doc: Fall back to an abbreviated SHA when no tag matches (`--always`).

setters.name: exactMatch
setters.doc: Fail unless the commit is exactly at a tag (`--exact-match`).

setters.name: abbrev
setters.doc:
How many SHA characters to append (`--abbrev=<n>`). `0` suppresses the
suffix entirely, which is how a build reads the nearest tag's bare name.

setters.name: dirty
setters.doc: Append a marker when the working tree is dirty (`--dirty[=<suffix>]`).

setters.name: match
setters.doc: Only consider tags matching this glob (`--match <pattern>`); repeatable.

setters.name: rev
setters.doc: The revisions or arguments to resolve (positional); repeatable.

setters.name: short
setters.doc:
Abbreviate the SHA (`--short`, or `--short=<n>` with a length). git picks
a length long enough to stay unambiguous when none is given.

setters.name: abbrevRef
setters.doc: Print the ref's short name (`--abbrev-ref`), e.g. `main` for `HEAD`.

setters.name: verify
