setters.doc: Fail rather than echo the argument when it names no object (`--verify`).

setters.name: gitDir
setters.doc: Print the path of the `.git` directory (`--git-dir`).

setters.name: showToplevel
setters.doc: Print the absolute path of the working tree's root (`--show-toplevel`).

setters.name: showPrefix
setters.doc: Print the current directory's path relative to that root (`--show-prefix`).

setters.name: isInsideWorkTree
setters.doc: Print whether this is inside a working tree (`--is-inside-work-tree`).

setters.name: short
setters.doc: Short-format output (`-s`/`--short`).

setters.name: porcelain
setters.doc: Stable machine-readable output (`--porcelain`).

setters.name: branch
setters.doc: Show branch information (`-b`/`--branch`).

setters.name: nulTerminated
setters.doc:
Terminate each record with a NUL rather than a newline (`-z`), which also
turns on `--porcelain` and stops git quoting unusual paths.

setters.name: untrackedFiles
setters.doc:
How much of an untracked directory to report (`--untracked-files=<mode>`):
`no`, `normal` (the default — the directory), or `all` (every file in it).

setters.name: ignored
setters.doc: Also report ignored files (`--ignored`).

setters.name: paths
setters.doc: Limit the report to these pathspecs (positional); repeatable.

setters.name: remote
setters.doc: The remote (or URL) to ask; defaults to the branch's upstream.

setters.name: patterns
setters.doc: Limit the listing to refs matching these patterns (positional); repeatable.

setters.name: heads
setters.doc: List branch refs only (`--heads`).

setters.name: tags
setters.doc: List tag refs only (`--tags`).

setters.name: refs
setters.doc: Hide peeled tags and pseudo-refs (`--refs`).

setters.name: symref
setters.doc: Also report what the remote's `HEAD` points at (`--symref`).

setters.name: exitCode
setters.doc: Exit 2 when nothing matched (`--exit-code`).

settings.name: GitRemoteSettings
settings.doc:
Settings for `git remote`. Pick the subcommand with list,
add, remove, rename, setUrl,
getUrl, show, or prune.

setters.name: list
setters.doc: List the configured remotes (`git remote`), the default.

setters.name: add
setters.doc: Add a remote (`git remote add <name> <url>`).

setters.name: remove
setters.doc: Remove a remote and its tracking refs (`git remote remove <name>`).

setters.name: rename
setters.doc: Rename a remote (`git remote rename <old> <new>`).

setters.name: setUrl
setters.doc:
Change a remote's URL (`git remote set-url <name> <url>`). Add
pushUrl to change only the push URL.

setters.name: getUrl
setters.doc: Print a remote's URL (`git remote get-url <name>`).

setters.name: show
setters.doc: Describe a remote and its branches (`git remote show <name>`).

setters.name: prune
setters.doc: Delete tracking refs the remote no longer has (`git remote prune <name>`).

setters.name: verbose
setters.doc: Show each remote's URLs when listing (`-v`/`--verbose`).

setters.name: fetch
setters.doc: Fetch from the remote right after adding it (`-f`, `add` only).

setters.name: track
setters.doc: Track only this branch (`-t <branch>`, `add` only).

setters.name: pushUrl
setters.doc: Operate on the push URL (`--push`), for setUrl and getUrl.

settings.name: GitConfigSettings
settings.doc:
Settings for `git config`. Pick the operation with get,
getAll, set, add, unset, or list,
and the file with global, local, system,
worktree, or file.

setters.name: get
setters.doc: Read a key's value (`--get <key>`).

setters.name: getAll
setters.doc: Read every value of a multi-valued key (`--get-all <key>`).

setters.name: set
setters.doc: Set a key, replacing any existing value (`git config <key> <value>`).

setters.name: add
setters.doc: Add another value to a multi-valued key (`--add <key> <value>`).

setters.name: unset
setters.doc: Remove a key (`--unset <key>`).

setters.name: list
setters.doc: List every configured key (`--list`).

setters.name: global
setters.doc: Use the user's configuration (`--global`).

setters.name: local
setters.doc: Use the repository's configuration (`--local`).

setters.name: system
setters.doc: Use the machine's configuration (`--system`).

setters.name: worktree
setters.doc: Use the worktree's configuration (`--worktree`).

setters.name: file
setters.doc: Use a specific file (`--file <path>`), rather than one of the scopes.

setters.name: defaultValue
setters.doc:
What to report when the key is unset (`--default <value>`), which also
makes `--get` exit 0 instead of 1.

settings.name: GitSequencerSettings
settings.doc:
Base for the commands that can be left in progress by a conflict. Subclasses
expose only the actions their command accepts — `merge` has no `--skip` —
and call GitSequencerSettings.sequencer_ to record one.

setters.name: continue
setters.doc: Resume the operation once the conflict is resolved (`--continue`).

setters.name: abort
setters.doc: Undo it and restore the pre-operation state (`--abort`).

setters.name: quit
setters.doc: Forget the operation, leaving the tree as it is (`--quit`).

settings.name: GitReplaySettings
settings.doc:
Shared base for `cherry-pick` and `revert`: the same commit list, the same
`--no-commit`/`--mainline`, and the same four control flags. Only the
subcommand's name and the extra flags differ, which is why they are one
implementation rather than two that drift.

setters.name: commits
setters.doc: The commits to replay (positional, required); repeatable.

setters.name: noCommit
setters.doc: Apply the change without committing it (`-n`/`--no-commit`).

setters.name: mainline
setters.doc:
Which parent of a merge commit to treat as the mainline
(`-m <parent-number>`), counting from 1. Replaying a merge needs it: git
cannot otherwise tell which side of the merge the change is.

setters.name: signoff
setters.doc: Add a `Signed-off-by` trailer (`--signoff`).

setters.name: skip
setters.doc: Drop the current commit and carry on (`--skip`).

setters.name: allowEmpty
setters.doc: Keep a commit that produces no changes (`--allow-empty`).

setters.name: ff
setters.doc: Fast-forward instead of rewriting when the parent matches `HEAD` (`--ff`).

setters.name: noEdit
setters.doc: Take the generated message without opening an editor (`--no-edit`).

settings.name: GitWorktreeSettings
settings.doc:
Settings for `git worktree`. Pick the subcommand with add,
list, remove, or prune; the remaining methods apply
to the one picked, mirroring the flags git accepts for it.

setters.name: add
setters.doc: Check a new worktree out at `path` (`git worktree add <path>`).

setters.name: list
setters.doc: List the repository's worktrees (`git worktree list`).

setters.name: remove
setters.doc: Remove the worktree at `path` (`git worktree remove <path>`).

setters.name: prune
setters.doc: Discard records of worktrees whose directories are gone (`git worktree prune`).

setters.name: branch
setters.doc:
The branch to check out in the new worktree — or, with
createBranch, the name of the branch to create there.

setters.name: createBranch
setters.doc: Create branch rather than checking out an existing one (`-b`).

setters.name: startPoint
setters.doc:
The commit the new branch forks from — git's trailing `<commit-ish>`, e.g.
`origin/main`. Only meaningful with createBranch: without a start
point git branches from the *parent* checkout's `HEAD`, which is whatever
the developer happened to have open.

Setting this and branch without createBranch is refused:
both want the same trailing position, and there is no reading of the
command where git would take them both.

setters.name: detach
setters.doc: Check out with a detached `HEAD` (`--detach`).

setters.name: force
setters.doc:
Force the operation (`--force`): check out a branch already checked out
elsewhere, or remove a worktree with modifications. Without it git refuses
both.

setters.name: porcelain
setters.doc: Emit the stable machine-readable listing (`--porcelain`).

settings.name: GitDefaultBranchSettings
settings.doc:
Settings for "./git.ts".GitTasks.defaultBranch: which remote to ask,
plus the global options every git task shares.

setters.name: remote
setters.doc: The remote whose default branch is wanted (default `origin`).

setters.name: all
setters.doc: Output every common ancestor rather than one (`--all`).

setters.name: octopus
setters.doc: Find the ancestors for a single n-way merge (`--octopus`).

setters.name: independent
setters.doc: List the revisions not reachable from any other (`--independent`).

setters.name: isAncestor
setters.doc:
Ask whether the first commit is an ancestor of the second
(`--is-ancestor`), which git answers by exit status and prints nothing.
Prefer "./git.ts".GitTasks.isAncestor, which reads that status
back as a boolean.

setters.name: forkPoint
setters.doc: Find where a commit forked from a ref's reflog (`--fork-point`).

setters.name: commits
setters.doc: The commits to consider (positional); repeatable.

setters.name: count
setters.doc:
Print how many commits the walk found rather than listing them
(`--count`). Prefer "./git.ts".GitTasks.commitCount, which reads
that number back.

setters.name: maxCount
setters.doc: Stop after this many commits (`--max-count=<n>`).

setters.name: skip
setters.doc: Skip this many commits before printing (`--skip=<n>`).

setters.name: all
setters.doc: Walk every ref in `refs/` (`--all`).

setters.name: branches
setters.doc: Walk every branch (`--branches`).

setters.name: tags
setters.doc: Walk every tag (`--tags`).

setters.name: remotes
setters.doc: Walk every remote-tracking branch (`--remotes`).

setters.name: noMerges
setters.doc: Omit merge commits (`--no-merges`).

setters.name: merges
setters.doc: Keep only merge commits (`--merges`).

setters.name: firstParent
setters.doc: Follow only the first parent of each merge (`--first-parent`).

setters.name: reverse
setters.doc: Emit the commits oldest first (`--reverse`).

setters.name: topoOrder
setters.doc: Order by topology rather than date (`--topo-order`).

setters.name: dateOrder
setters.doc: Order by commit date (`--date-order`).

setters.name: since
setters.doc: Only commits after this date (`--since=<date>`).

setters.name: until
setters.doc: Only commits before this date (`--until=<date>`).

setters.name: author
setters.doc: Only commits whose author matches (`--author=<pattern>`).

setters.name: commits
setters.doc:
The commits or ranges to walk (positional), e.g. `"HEAD"` or
`"origin/main..HEAD"`; repeatable.

setters.name: paths
setters.doc: Limit the walk to commits touching these paths (positional); repeatable.

setters.name: format
setters.doc: The output format (`--format=<format>`), in git's placeholder language.

setters.name: count
setters.doc: Show only this many matched refs (`--count=<n>`).

setters.name: sort
setters.doc:
Sort by a field (`--sort=<key>`), e.g. `"-creatordate"` for newest first;
repeatable, and git applies the keys in the order given.

setters.name: exclude
setters.doc: Exclude refs matching a pattern (`--exclude=<pattern>`); repeatable.

setters.name: pointsAt
setters.doc: Only refs pointing at this object (`--points-at=<object>`).

setters.name: merged
setters.doc: Only refs merged into this commit (`--merged=<commit>`).

setters.name: noMerged
setters.doc: Only refs not merged into this commit (`--no-merged=<commit>`).

setters.name: contains
setters.doc: Only refs whose history contains this commit (`--contains=<commit>`).

setters.name: noContains
setters.doc: Only refs not containing this commit (`--no-contains=<commit>`).

setters.name: ignoreCase
setters.doc: Sort and filter case-insensitively (`--ignore-case`).

setters.name: omitEmpty
setters.doc: Skip the newline after a ref that formats to nothing (`--omit-empty`).

setters.name: patterns
setters.doc: The ref patterns to match (positional), e.g. `"refs/tags/"`; repeatable.

setters.name: tags
setters.doc: Use only tags to name the commits (`--tags`).

setters.name: all
setters.doc: Name every reachable commit (`--all`).

setters.name: nameOnly
setters.doc: Print only the name, not the commit it names (`--name-only`).

setters.name: alwaysName
setters.doc: Fall back to the object name when nothing else names it (`--always`).

setters.name: refs
setters.doc: Only consider refs matching these patterns (`--refs=<pattern>`).

setters.name: commits
setters.doc: The commits to name (positional); repeatable.

setters.name: tags
setters.doc: Only tags (`--tags`); may be combined with heads.

setters.name: heads
setters.doc: Only branch heads (`--heads`); may be combined with tags.

setters.name: head
setters.doc: Include `HEAD` even when a filter would exclude it (`--head`).

setters.name: dereference
setters.doc: Dereference tags into the objects they point at (`--dereference`).

setters.name: hash
setters.doc: Print only the object name, without the ref (`--hash`).

setters.name: verify
setters.doc: Require an exact ref path and fail otherwise (`--verify`).

setters.name: exists
setters.doc: Check a ref exists without resolving it (`--exists`).

setters.name: quietOutput
setters.doc:
Suppress git's own stdout (`--quiet`), leaving the exit status as the
answer — the useful pairing with verify.

Named apart from the inherited `quiet`, which silences Zuke's echo of the
command rather than git's output.

setters.name: abbrev
setters.doc: Abbreviate object names to this many digits (`--abbrev=<n>`).

setters.name: patterns
setters.doc: The ref patterns to show (positional); repeatable.

setters.name: name
setters.doc: The symbolic ref to read or set (positional), e.g. `"HEAD"`.

setters.name: ref
setters.doc: The ref to point it at (positional), which makes this a write.

setters.name: short
setters.doc: Shorten the reported ref name (`--short`).

setters.name: delete
setters.doc: Delete the symbolic ref (`--delete`).

setters.name: quietOutput
setters.doc:
Say nothing and exit non-zero when the ref is not symbolic (`--quiet`).

Named apart from the inherited `quiet`, which silences Zuke's echo.

setters.name: reason
setters.doc: The reflog reason to record for the update (`-m <reason>`).

setters.name: object
setters.doc: The object to read (positional), e.g. `"HEAD:deno.json"`.

setters.name: query
setters.doc:
Report an attribute rather than the contents: `type` (`-t`), `size`
(`-s`), or `exists` (`-e`, which answers by exit status and prints
nothing).

setters.name: textconv
setters.doc: Run the object through its textconv filter (`--textconv`).

setters.name: filters
setters.doc: Run the object through its working-tree filters (`--filters`).

setters.name: tree
setters.doc: The tree-ish to list (positional), e.g. `"HEAD"` or `"v1.0.0"`.

setters.name: recursive
setters.doc: Recurse into subtrees (`-r`).

setters.name: treesOnly
setters.doc: Show only trees, not blobs (`-d`).

setters.name: showTrees
setters.doc: Show the trees themselves while recursing (`-t`).

setters.name: nulTerminated
setters.doc: Terminate entries with NUL rather than newline (`-z`).

setters.name: long
setters.doc: Include each object's size (`--long`).

setters.name: nameOnly
setters.doc: List only the file names (`--name-only`).

setters.name: objectOnly
setters.doc: List only the object names (`--object-only`).

setters.name: fullName
setters.doc: Report paths from the repository root (`--full-name`).

setters.name: fullTree
setters.doc: List the whole tree, not just the current directory (`--full-tree`).

setters.name: abbrev
setters.doc: Abbreviate object names to this many digits (`--abbrev=<n>`).

setters.name: paths
setters.doc: Limit the listing to these paths (positional); repeatable.

setters.name: quietOutput
setters.doc:
Say nothing and answer by exit status alone (`-q`).

Named apart from the inherited `quiet`, which silences Zuke's echo of the
command rather than git's output.

setters.name: verbose
setters.doc: Also report the rule that excluded each path (`-v`).

setters.name: nonMatching
setters.doc: Include the paths that are *not* excluded (`-n`); needs verbose.

setters.name: noIndex
setters.doc: Ignore the index when checking (`--no-index`).

setters.name: nulTerminated
setters.doc: Terminate records with NUL rather than newline (`-z`).

setters.name: paths
setters.doc: The paths to check (positional); repeatable.

setters.name: file
setters.doc: The file to annotate (positional).

setters.name: porcelain
setters.doc:
Machine-readable output (`--porcelain`). Prefer
"./git.ts".GitTasks.blameLines, which parses it.

setters.name: linePorcelain
setters.doc:
Like porcelain, but repeating the commit header on every line
(`--line-porcelain`) rather than only its first appearance.

setters.name: revision
setters.doc: Annotate the file as of this revision (positional).

setters.name: lineRange
setters.doc: Annotate only these lines (`-L <start>,<end>`); repeatable.

setters.name: showEmail
setters.doc: Show the author's email rather than their name (`-e`).

setters.name: ignoreWhitespace
setters.doc: Ignore whitespace-only changes when assigning blame (`-w`).

setters.name: reverse
setters.doc: Walk history forward from this revision instead (`--reverse <rev>`).

setters.name: ignoreRevs
setters.doc: Ignore a revision when assigning blame (`--ignore-rev`); repeatable.

setters.name: summary
setters.doc:
Report only the commit count per author, without the subjects (`-s`).
Prefer "./git.ts".GitTasks.shortlogEntries, which reads that
output back.

setters.name: numbered
setters.doc: Sort by commit count rather than by name (`-n`).

setters.name: email
setters.doc: Include each author's email address (`-e`).

setters.name: committer
setters.doc: Group by committer rather than author (`-c`).

setters.name: group
setters.doc: Group by a named field (`--group=<field>`), e.g. `"trailer:co-authored-by"`.

setters.name: commits
setters.doc: The revision range to summarise (positional); repeatable.

setters.name: paths
setters.doc: Limit the summary to commits touching these paths (positional).

setters.name: pattern
setters.doc: A pattern to search for (`-e <pattern>`); repeatable.

setters.name: ignoreCase
setters.doc: Match case-insensitively (`-i`).

setters.name: wordRegexp
setters.doc: Match only at word boundaries (`-w`).

setters.name: invert
setters.doc: Report the lines that do *not* match (`-v`).

setters.name: lineNumber
setters.doc: Prefix each match with its line number (`-n`).

setters.name: namesOnly
setters.doc: Report only the names of matching files (`-l`).

setters.name: countMatches
setters.doc: Report only how many lines matched per file (`-c`).

setters.name: extendedRegexp
setters.doc: Read the pattern as a POSIX extended regexp (`-E`).

setters.name: fixedStrings
setters.doc: Read the pattern as a literal string (`-F`).

setters.name: cached
setters.doc: Search the index rather than the working tree (`--cached`).

setters.name: untracked
setters.doc: Search untracked files as well as tracked ones (`--untracked`).

setters.name: nulTerminated
setters.doc: Terminate output records with NUL (`-z`).

setters.name: maxDepth
setters.doc: Descend at most this many directories (`--max-depth=<n>`).

setters.name: context
setters.doc: Show this many lines of context around each match (`-C <n>`).

setters.name: revisions
setters.doc: Search these revisions rather than the working tree (positional).

setters.name: paths
setters.doc: Limit the search to these paths (positional); repeatable.

setters.name: verbose
setters.doc: Also print the commit's contents (`-v`).

setters.name: raw
setters.doc: Print gpg's raw status output (`--raw`).

setters.name: objects
setters.doc: The commits to verify (positional); repeatable.

setters.name: verbose
setters.doc: Also print the tag's contents (`-v`).

setters.name: raw
setters.doc: Print gpg's raw status output (`--raw`).

setters.name: format
setters.doc:
The output format (`--format=<format>`), in git's placeholder language.
`verify-tag` accepts this where `verify-commit` does not.

setters.name: objects
setters.doc: The tags to verify (positional); repeatable.

setters.name: writeTree
setters.doc:
Do a real merge and write the resulting tree (`--write-tree`), rather than
the trivial three-way form. This is the default in git 2.38 and later.

setters.name: messages
setters.doc: Also print the informational and conflict messages (`--messages`).

setters.name: nameOnly
setters.doc: List conflicted filenames without modes or object names (`--name-only`).

setters.name: nulTerminated
setters.doc: Separate paths with NUL rather than newline (`-z`).

setters.name: allowUnrelatedHistories
setters.doc: Permit merging histories with no common ancestor (`--allow-unrelated-histories`).

setters.name: mergeBase
setters.doc: Use this commit as the merge base (`--merge-base=<commit>`).

setters.name: branches
setters.doc: The two branches to merge (positional).

settings.name: GitRunSettings
settings.doc: Settings for an arbitrary `git` command not covered by a typed task.

setters.name: command
setters.doc: The subcommand and its arguments, e.g. `command("bisect", "start")`.

setters.name: bare
setters.doc: Create a bare repository (`--bare`).

setters.name: initialBranch
setters.doc: Name the initial branch (`-b`/`--initial-branch`).

setters.name: repository
setters.doc: The repository URL to clone (required).

setters.name: directory
setters.doc: Target directory for the clone.

setters.name: branch
setters.doc: Check out a specific branch (`-b`/`--branch`).

setters.name: depth
setters.doc: Create a shallow clone of the given depth (`--depth`).

setters.name: bare
setters.doc: Clone a bare repository (`--bare`).

setters.name: filter
setters.doc:
Partial-clone filter (`--filter=<spec>`), e.g. `blob:none` for a treeless
clone that fetches blobs on demand — the cheap way to get full history in
CI without the file contents of every revision.

setters.name: singleBranch
setters.doc: Clone only the history of the checked-out branch (`--single-branch`).

setters.name: recurseSubmodules
setters.doc: Also clone submodules (`--recurse-submodules`).

setters.name: paths
setters.doc: Paths/pathspecs to stage (positional); repeatable.

setters.name: all
setters.doc: Stage all changes including new files (`-A`/`--all`).

setters.name: update
setters.doc: Stage modifications and deletions, but not new files (`-u`/`--update`).

setters.name: force
setters.doc: Stage files git would otherwise ignore (`-f`/`--force`).

setters.name: intentToAdd
setters.doc:
Record the paths' existence but not their contents (`-N`/`--intent-to-add`),
which is what makes an untracked file show up in `git diff`.

setters.name: paths
setters.doc: Paths/pathspecs to remove (positional, required); repeatable.

setters.name: cached
setters.doc:
Remove from the index only, leaving the file on disk (`--cached`) — how a
file committed by mistake stops being tracked without being deleted.

setters.name: recursive
setters.doc: Recurse into directories (`-r`).

setters.name: force
setters.doc: Remove even when the file has staged or local changes (`-f`/`--force`).

setters.name: dryRun
setters.doc: Report what would be removed without removing it (`-n`/`--dry-run`).

setters.name: ignoreUnmatch
setters.doc: Exit 0 when no path matches (`--ignore-unmatch`).

setters.name: sources
setters.doc: The path(s) to move (positional, required); repeatable.

setters.name: destination
setters.doc:
Where they move to (required): a file name for a single source, a
directory when there is more than one.

setters.name: force
setters.doc: Overwrite an existing destination (`-f`/`--force`).

setters.name: dryRun
setters.doc: Report what would move without moving it (`-n`/`--dry-run`).

setters.name: paths
setters.doc: The pathspecs to restore (positional, required); repeatable.

setters.name: source
setters.doc:
Restore the contents from this commit or tree (`--source=<tree-ish>`)
rather than from the index.

setters.name: staged
setters.doc:
Restore the index (`--staged`) — unstaging the paths. Combine with
worktree to reset both, which is what `git restore -SW` does.

setters.name: worktree
setters.doc: Restore the working tree (`--worktree`), git's default when neither is given.

setters.name: paths
setters.doc: Limit the clean to these pathspecs (positional); repeatable.

setters.name: force
setters.doc: Actually delete the files (`-f`/`--force`).

setters.name: dryRun
setters.doc: List what would be deleted without deleting it (`-n`/`--dry-run`).

setters.name: directories
setters.doc: Also remove untracked directories (`-d`).

setters.name: includeIgnored
setters.doc:
Remove ignored files too (`-x`) — the switch that turns a clean into a
from-scratch build, since `node_modules` and `target/` are ignored.

setters.name: onlyIgnored
setters.doc: Remove *only* ignored files (`-X`), keeping other untracked ones.

setters.name: exclude
setters.doc: Spare paths matching this pattern (`--exclude=<pattern>`); repeatable.

setters.name: message
setters.doc: The commit message (`-m`).

setters.name: all
setters.doc: Stage modified/deleted files before committing (`-a`/`--all`).

setters.name: amend
setters.doc: Amend the previous commit (`--amend`).

setters.name: noEdit
setters.doc: Keep the existing message when amending (`--no-edit`).

setters.name: allowEmpty
setters.doc: Allow a commit with no changes (`--allow-empty`).

setters.name: noVerify
setters.doc:
Skip the `pre-commit` and `commit-msg` hooks (`--no-verify`) — what a bot
commit wants when the hooks are meant for humans at a terminal.

setters.name: author
setters.doc: Attribute the commit to someone else (`--author="Name <email>"`).

setters.name: paths
setters.doc: Commit only these pathspecs (positional); repeatable.

setters.name: ref
setters.doc:
The branch or commit to check out — or, with paths, the source to
restore those paths from. Required unless paths is given.

setters.name: paths
setters.doc:
Restore one or more paths (`git checkout [<ref>] -- <paths>`). The `--`
separates paths from any ref so a path is never misread as a branch name;
repeatable. With no ref, restores the paths from the index
(discarding working-tree changes).

setters.name: create
setters.doc: Create a new branch (`-b`).

setters.name: detach
setters.doc: Check the ref out with a detached `HEAD` (`--detach`).

setters.name: force
setters.doc: Force checkout, discarding local changes (`-f`/`--force`).

setters.name: branch
setters.doc: The branch to switch to — or, with create, the one to create.

setters.name: startPoint
setters.doc:
The commit the new branch forks from (git's trailing `<start-point>`),
e.g. `origin/main`. Without it a created branch forks from the current
`HEAD`, which is whatever the checkout happened to be on.

setters.name: create
setters.doc: Create the branch (`-c`); fails if it already exists.

setters.name: forceCreate
setters.doc: Create the branch, resetting it if it exists (`-C`).

setters.name: track
setters.doc: Set up upstream tracking (`--track=<mode>`), `direct` or `inherit`.

setters.name: detach
setters.doc:
Switch with a detached `HEAD` (`--detach`) — checking out a commit rather
than a branch, which `switch` otherwise refuses.

setters.name: force
setters.doc: Throw away local changes rather than refusing to switch (`--force`).

setters.name: name
setters.doc: The branch name to create or operate on.

setters.name: startPoint
setters.doc:
The commit a created branch forks from (git's trailing `<start-point>`),
e.g. `origin/main`.

setters.name: deleteBranch
setters.doc: Delete the branch (`-d`, or `-D` when forced).

setters.name: rename
setters.doc: Rename name to `newName` (`-m`, or `-M` when forced).

setters.name: setUpstreamTo
setters.doc: Point the branch's upstream at this ref (`--set-upstream-to=<ref>`).

setters.name: all
setters.doc: List both local and remote-tracking branches (`-a`/`--all`).

setters.name: remotes
setters.doc: List remote-tracking branches only (`-r`/`--remotes`).

setters.name: contains
setters.doc: List only branches containing this commit (`--contains <commit>`).

setters.name: merged
setters.doc:
List only branches already merged into this ref (`--merged <ref>`) — the
listing a cleanup target filters stale branches from.

setters.name: format
setters.doc:
Render a listing through a format string (`--format=<fmt>`), e.g.
`%(refname:short)` for bare branch names with no `*` marker or padding.

setters.name: sort
setters.doc: Order a listing (`--sort=<key>`), e.g. `-committerdate` for most recent first.

setters.name: name
setters.doc: The tag name.

setters.name: commit
setters.doc:
The commit to tag (git's trailing `<commit>`), rather than `HEAD`. Only
meaningful when creating a tag.

setters.name: message
setters.doc: Create an annotated tag with this message (`-a -m`).

setters.name: force
setters.doc: Replace an existing tag (`-f`/`--force`).

setters.name: deleteTag
setters.doc: Delete the tag (`-d`/`--delete`).

setters.name: list
setters.doc:
List tags (`-l`), optionally matching a shell pattern such as `v1.*`.
With no pattern, lists them all.

setters.name: sort
setters.doc:
Order a listing (`--sort=<key>`), e.g. `-v:refname` for newest-version
first — the ordering a release target wants, since the default is
lexicographic and puts `v1.10.0` before `v1.9.0`.

setters.name: remote
setters.doc: The remote to push to (e.g. `origin`).

setters.name: ref
setters.doc: The refspec/branch to push.

setters.name: setUpstream
setters.doc: Set the upstream tracking ref (`-u`/`--set-upstream`).

setters.name: tags
setters.doc: Also push tags (`--tags`).

setters.name: followTags
setters.doc:
Push the annotated tags reachable from the refs being pushed
(`--follow-tags`) — a release target's tag rides along with its commit
instead of needing a second push.

setters.name: forceWithLease
setters.doc: Force push, but only if the remote ref is unchanged (`--force-with-lease`).

setters.name: deleteRef
setters.doc: Delete the remote ref (`--delete`).

setters.name: atomic
setters.doc: Update every ref or none (`--atomic`).

setters.name: dryRun
setters.doc: Report what would be pushed without pushing it (`--dry-run`).

setters.name: pushOption
setters.doc:
Send a server-side option (`--push-option=<value>`); repeatable. GitLab
reads these for `ci.skip` and merge-request creation.

setters.name: remote
setters.doc: The remote to pull from.

setters.name: ref
setters.doc: The refspec/branch to pull.

setters.name: rebase
setters.doc: Rebase instead of merge (`--rebase`).

setters.name: noRebase
setters.doc:
Merge rather than rebase (`--no-rebase`), whatever `pull.rebase` is set to
in the ambient config — the flag a build reaches for when it must not
depend on the machine it runs on.

setters.name: ffOnly
setters.doc: Only fast-forward (`--ff-only`).

setters.name: depth
setters.doc: Limit the fetched history to this many commits (`--depth`).

setters.name: tags
setters.doc: Also fetch tags (`--tags`).

setters.name: prune
setters.doc: Prune deleted remote refs while fetching (`--prune`).

setters.name: remote
setters.doc: The remote to fetch from.

setters.name: refspec
setters.doc:
Add a refspec to fetch, after the remote — `master`, or
`master:refs/remotes/origin/master` to also update the remote-tracking ref
(which is what makes `origin/master` resolvable in a shallow CI checkout
that never fetched it). Repeatable.

Prefix the source with `+` to force the update. Pair it with
depth: a shallow fetch is not a fast-forward of the history
already present, and git rejects such an update unless it is forced.

setters.name: noTags
setters.doc: Skip fetching tags (`--no-tags`).

setters.name: depth
setters.doc:
Limit history to this many commits (`--depth`). `1` is enough to diff
against a base branch and avoids pulling a whole history into a CI job.

setters.name: unshallow
setters.doc:
Deepen a shallow clone into the full history (`--unshallow`) — what a
release target needs before `git describe` or a changelog can see past the
one commit CI checked out.

setters.name: all
setters.doc: Fetch from all remotes (`--all`).

setters.name: tags
setters.doc: Also fetch tags (`--tags`).

setters.name: prune
setters.doc: Prune deleted remote refs (`--prune`).

setters.name: force
setters.doc: Update refs even when the update is not a fast-forward (`--force`).

setters.name: refs
setters.doc: The commits to merge into the current branch (positional); repeatable.

setters.name: message
setters.doc: The merge commit's message (`-m`).

setters.name: noFf
setters.doc: Always create a merge commit (`--no-ff`), even when a fast-forward would do.

setters.name: ffOnly
setters.doc: Refuse anything but a fast-forward (`--ff-only`).

setters.name: squash
setters.doc: Stage the merged result without recording a merge (`--squash`).

setters.name: noCommit
setters.doc: Merge but leave the commit to the caller (`--no-commit`).

setters.name: strategy
setters.doc: The merge strategy (`--strategy=<name>`), e.g. `ours`.

setters.name: strategyOption
allowUnrelatedHistories
setters.doc: Merge histories that share no commit (`--allow-unrelated-histories`).

setters.name: upstream
setters.doc: The commit the current branch is replayed onto (positional).

setters.name: branch
setters.doc: Rebase this branch rather than the checked-out one (git's `<branch>`).

setters.name: onto
setters.doc: Replay onto a different base than the upstream (`--onto <newbase>`).

setters.name: autosquash
setters.doc: Fold `fixup!`/`squash!` commits into their targets (`--autosquash`).

setters.name: autostash
setters.doc:
Stash local changes and restore them afterwards (`--autostash`), instead
of refusing to start on a dirty tree.

setters.name: keepEmpty
setters.doc: Keep commits that produce no changes (`--keep-empty`).

setters.name: rebaseMerges
setters.doc: Recreate merge commits rather than flattening them (`--rebase-merges`).

setters.name: strategy
setters.doc: The merge strategy used to replay each commit (`--strategy=<name>`).

setters.name: strategyOption
setters.doc: An option for that strategy (`--strategy-option=<option>`); repeatable.

setters.name: skip
setters.doc: Drop the current commit and carry on (`--skip`).

setters.name: ref
setters.doc: The commit to reset to (positional); defaults to `HEAD`.

setters.name: paths
setters.doc: Reset only these pathspecs — unstaging them (positional); repeatable.

setters.name: soft
setters.doc: Move the branch only, keeping the index and working tree (`--soft`).

setters.name: mixed
setters.doc: Reset the index but not the working tree (`--mixed`), git's default.

setters.name: hard
setters.doc: Reset the index *and* the working tree (`--hard`), discarding changes.

setters.name: merge
setters.doc: Reset, keeping changes to files that differ between the commits (`--merge`).

setters.name: keep
setters.doc: Like merge, but refuse when a changed file differs (`--keep`).

settings.name: GitStashSettings
settings.doc:
Settings for `git stash`. Pick the subcommand with push,
pop, apply, list, show, drop, or
clear; the remaining methods apply to the one picked.

setters.name: push
setters.doc: Stash the working tree and index (`git stash push`).

setters.name: pop
setters.doc: Restore a stash and drop it (`git stash pop`).

setters.name: apply
setters.doc: Restore a stash and keep it (`git stash apply`).

setters.name: list
setters.doc: List the stashes (`git stash list`).

setters.name: show
setters.doc: Show a stash's diff (`git stash show`).

setters.name: drop
setters.doc: Discard a stash (`git stash drop`).

setters.name: clear
setters.doc: Discard every stash (`git stash clear`).

setters.name: stash
setters.doc:
Which stash to act on, e.g. `stash@{1}` (positional); defaults to the most
recent. Only meaningful for pop, apply, show, and
drop.

setters.name: message
setters.doc: Label the stash being pushed (`-m`).

setters.name: includeUntracked
setters.doc: Stash untracked files too (`--include-untracked`).

setters.name: keepIndex
setters.doc: Leave what is already staged in the index (`--keep-index`).

setters.name: staged
setters.doc: Stash only what is staged (`--staged`).

setters.name: paths
setters.doc: Stash only these pathspecs (positional, after `--`); repeatable.

settings.name: GitSubmoduleSettings
settings.doc:
Settings for `git submodule`. Pick the subcommand with add,
init, deinit, update, sync, status,
or foreach.

setters.name: add
setters.doc: Add a submodule (`git submodule add <url> [<path>]`).

setters.name: init
setters.doc: Register the submodules in `.gitmodules` (`git submodule init`).

setters.name: deinit
setters.doc: Unregister submodules (`git submodule deinit`).

setters.name: update
setters.doc: Check the submodules out at their recorded commits (`git submodule update`).

setters.name: sync
setters.doc: Copy the configured URLs into `.git/config` (`git submodule sync`).

setters.name: status
setters.doc: Report each submodule's checked-out commit (`git submodule status`).

setters.name: foreach
setters.doc: Run a command in each submodule (`git submodule foreach <command>`).

setters.name: paths
setters.doc: Limit the operation to these paths (positional); repeatable.

setters.name: withInit
setters.doc:
Initialise uninitialised submodules first (`--init`), the flag
update needs on a fresh clone. Named for the flag rather than the
`init` subcommand, which is what init runs.

setters.name: recursive
setters.doc: Recurse into nested submodules (`--recursive`).

setters.name: remote
setters.doc: Use the upstream branch's latest commit rather than the recorded one (`--remote`).

setters.name: force
setters.doc: Discard local changes in the submodule (`--force`).

setters.name: depth
setters.doc: Clone the submodules shallowly (`--depth <n>`).

setters.name: jobs
setters.doc: Clone this many submodules in parallel (`--jobs <n>`).

setters.name: branch
setters.doc: Track this branch when adding or updating (`-b <branch>`).

setters.name: treeish
setters.doc: The tree, commit, or tag to archive (positional, required).

setters.name: format
setters.doc: The archive format (`--format=<fmt>`), e.g. `tar`, `tar.gz`, or `zip`.

setters.name: output
setters.doc: Write to this file (`--output=<file>`) instead of stdout.

setters.name: prefix
setters.doc: Prepend this path to every entry (`--prefix=<prefix>/`).

setters.name: remote
setters.doc: Ask a remote repository for the archive (`--remote=<repo>`).

setters.name: paths
setters.doc: Archive only these pathspecs (positional); repeatable.

setters.name: patches
setters.doc: The patch files to apply (positional); repeatable. Reads stdin when empty.

setters.name: check
setters.doc: Report whether the patch would apply, changing nothing (`--check`).

setters.name: reverse
setters.doc: Apply the patch backwards (`--reverse`).

setters.name: threeWay
setters.doc:
Fall back to a three-way merge when the patch does not apply cleanly
(`--3way`), leaving conflict markers instead of refusing outright.

setters.name: index
setters.doc: Apply to the index as well as the working tree (`--index`).

setters.name: cached
setters.doc: Apply to the index only, leaving the working tree alone (`--cached`).

setters.name: strip
setters.doc: Strip this many leading path components (`-p<n>`); git's default is 1.

setters.name: whitespace
setters.doc:
What to do about whitespace errors (`--whitespace=<action>`): `nowarn`,
`warn`, `fix`, `error`, or `error-all`.

setters.name: exclude
setters.doc: Skip files matching this pattern (`--exclude=<pattern>`); repeatable.

packages.name: gh
packages.summary: `@zuke/gh` — typed GitHub tooling for Zuke builds: the `gh` (GitHub CLI) task wrapper plus {@link githubWorkflow}, a wait trigger that dispatches and awaits an external GitHub Actions workflow.

tasks.name: GhTasks
tasks.doc: Typed task functions for GitHub: the `gh` CLI and the REST-only operations.

tasks.name: run
tasks.doc: Run a `gh` command.

tasks.name: api

settings.name: GhApiSettings
settings.doc:
Settings for GhTasks.api, mirroring the
real `gh api` flags: `--method`, `--field`, `--raw-field`, `--header`,
`--jq`, and `--silent`.

setters.name: method
setters.doc: The HTTP method (`--method`, e.g. `"PUT"`; `gh` defaults to GET).

setters.name: field
setters.doc: Add a typed body parameter (`--field key=value`). Repeatable.

setters.name: rawField
setters.doc: Add a string body parameter (`--raw-field key=value`). Repeatable.

setters.name: header
setters.doc: Add a request header (`--header key:value`). Repeatable.

setters.name: jq
setters.doc: Filter the response through a jq expression (`--jq`).

setters.name: silent
setters.doc: Do not print the response body (`--silent`).

setters.name: repo
setters.doc: Target repository as `OWNER/REPO` (`-R`/`--repo`).

packages.name: chocolatey
packages.summary: `@zuke/chocolatey` — ship a prebuilt Windows binary through [Chocolatey](https://chocolatey.org) from a Zuke build: `ChocoTasks` wraps the `choco` CLI, and `ChocolateyTasks` renders a package for a zip hosted on a release, verifies it installs, publishes it, and declares the CI job that verifies it on Windows.

tasks.name: ChocoTasks
tasks.doc: Typed task functions for the Chocolatey `choco` CLI.

tasks.name: run
tasks.doc: Run any `choco` command, built with `.command(...)`/`.flag(...)`.

tasks.name: pack
tasks.doc: Build a `.nupkg` from a `.nuspec` (`choco pack`).

tasks.name: push
tasks.doc: Upload a `.nupkg` to a source (`choco push`); the API key is masked.

tasks.name: install
tasks.doc: Install packages (`choco install`).

tasks.name: uninstall
tasks.doc: Uninstall packages (`choco uninstall`).

tasks.name: apikey
tasks.doc: List, save or remove a source's API key (`choco apikey`).

tasks.name: ChocolateyTasks
tasks.doc: Tasks for shipping a prebuilt Windows binary through Chocolatey.

tasks.name: package
tasks.doc:
The files of a package that installs a prebuilt binary from a zip on a
release: `<id>.nuspec` and `tools/chocolateyinstall.ps1`. Pure: nothing
is read or written.

tasks.name: verify
tasks.doc:
Pack a rendered package in a temporary directory, install it from there,
run the binary it puts on `PATH`, then uninstall it and remove the
directory — the cleanup runs whether or not the install and check
succeeded.

tasks.name: publish
tasks.doc:
Push a package — rendered, or a `.nupkg` already built — to the community
repository or another source, with its API key masked.

tasks.name: verifyJob
tasks.doc:
The CI job that runs a verifying target on Windows runners, ready to
list in `cicd({ invokes: [...] })`.

settings.name: ChocoCommandSettings
settings.doc:
Base for a typed `choco` command: the command, then its operands, then its
own options, then the common switches — the order choco's own usage lines
print (`choco install <pkg> [<options/switches>]`). Anything added through
the inherited `.command(...)`/`.flag(...)` escape hatches follows.

Valued options render as one `--name=value` token, the spelling choco's
help prints, so a value that starts with `-` stays the option's value
rather than becoming a switch of its own.

Operands are refused when choco would read them as a switch: a package id
or file path never starts with `-`, and passing `--force` as a "package"
would change what the command does rather than fail.

setters.name: yes
setters.doc: Answer yes to every prompt (`--yes`), which also accepts licenses.

setters.name: force
setters.doc:
Force the behaviour (`--force`) — reinstall an installed package, say.
Choco warns against it in normal operation.

setters.name: noProgress
setters.doc: Do not print download progress percentages (`--no-progress`).

setters.name: limitOutput
setters.doc: Print only the essential information (`--limit-output`).

setters.name: verbose
setters.doc: Print verbose messages (`--verbose`).

settings.name: ChocoApikeySettings
settings.doc:
Settings for `choco apikey`, which manages the API keys choco saves per
source — so a later `choco push` to that source needs no key on its
command line.

```ts
await ChocoTasks.apikey((s) =>
  s.add().source("https://push.chocolatey.org/").apiKey(key)
);
```

`add` needs a source and an apiKey; `remove` needs a
source. With no action set, choco lists the saved keys (by source; it never
prints a key itself).

setters.name: list
setters.doc: List the saved keys' sources (`apikey list`).

setters.name: add
setters.doc: Save the apiKey for the source (`apikey add`).

setters.name: remove
setters.doc: Remove the key saved for the source (`apikey remove`).

setters.name: source
setters.doc: The source the key is for (`--source`).

setters.name: apiKey
setters.doc:
The key to save (`--api-key`), for add. Masked in every rendering
of the command and in its errors.

setters.name: packages
setters.doc: Package ids to install (required); repeatable.

setters.name: source
setters.doc:
Where to find the packages (`--source`): a feed URL, or a local directory
holding `.nupkg` files. Defaults to the configured feeds.

setters.name: version
setters.doc: The exact version to install (`--version`).

setters.name: prerelease
setters.doc: Consider prerelease versions (`--prerelease`).

settings.name: ChocoPackSettings
settings.doc:
Settings for `choco pack`, which builds a `.nupkg` from a `.nuspec`. With no
nuspec named, choco packs the one in the working directory.

setters.name: nuspec
setters.doc: The `.nuspec` to pack; defaults to the one in the working directory.

setters.name: version
setters.doc: The version to write into the package, overriding the nuspec's (`--version`).

setters.name: outputDirectory
setters.doc: Where to write the `.nupkg` (`--output-directory`); defaults to the working directory.

settings.name: ChocoPushSettings
settings.doc:
Settings for `choco push`, which uploads a `.nupkg` to a source. With no
package named, choco pushes the only `.nupkg` in the working directory.

The API key is an argument — choco reads it from nowhere else — so it is
registered with the run's redactor and masked out of any error the push
raises. It is still visible in the process table for the push's duration;
on a shared host, save it once with `choco apikey add` instead and leave
apiKey unset, and choco looks it up by source.

setters.name: nupkg
setters.doc: The `.nupkg` to push.

setters.name: source
setters.doc:
The source to push to (`--source`), e.g. `https://push.chocolatey.org/`
for the community repository.

setters.name: apiKey
setters.doc:
The source's API key (`--api-key`). Masked in every rendering of the
command and in its errors.

setters.name: packages
setters.doc: Package ids to uninstall (required); repeatable.

setters.name: source
setters.doc: The source the packages came from (`--source`).

setters.name: version
setters.doc: The installed version to uninstall (`--version`).

setters.name: allVersions
setters.doc: Uninstall every installed version (`--all-versions`).

settings.name: ChocolateyPackageSettings
settings.doc: Settings for a package that installs a prebuilt binary from a zip.

setters.name: id
setters.doc:
The package id (required), e.g. `app`: lowercase letters and digits,
joined by single `.`, `-` or `_`, at most 100 characters. It is also the
nuspec's file name, `<id>.nuspec`.

setters.name: version
setters.doc:
The package version (required), a NuGet version such as `1.2.3`,
`1.2.3.4` or `1.2.3-beta.1` — usually the release's own version.

setters.name: title
setters.doc: The display title (`<title>`), e.g. `App (Portable)`.

setters.name: authors
setters.doc: The software's authors (`<authors>`, required); repeatable.

setters.name: owners
setters.doc:
The package's maintainers (`<owners>`) — on the community repository,
the user names that may push it; repeatable.

setters.name: projectUrl
setters.doc: The software's homepage (`<projectUrl>`, required; must be `https`).

setters.name: licenseUrl
setters.doc:
The license's URL (`<licenseUrl>`, `https`) — the community repository
requires it whenever the software has one.

setters.name: iconUrl
setters.doc: The package icon's URL (`<iconUrl>`, `https`).

setters.name: packageSourceUrl
setters.doc:
Where the package's own source lives (`<packageSourceUrl>`, `https`) —
typically the repository whose build renders it.

setters.name: docsUrl
setters.doc: The software's documentation (`<docsUrl>`, `https`).

setters.name: bugTrackerUrl
setters.doc: The software's issue tracker (`<bugTrackerUrl>`, `https`).

setters.name: tags
setters.doc: Search tags (`<tags>`), each one word; repeatable.

setters.name: copyright
setters.doc:
The software's copyright notice (`<copyright>`), one line — e.g. the
line in its LICENSE, `Copyright (c) 2026 Acme`. The community
repository's moderators ask for it whenever the software has one.

setters.name: summary
setters.doc: A one-line summary (`<summary>`).

setters.name: description
setters.doc:
The description (`<description>`, required; Markdown is fine), held to
the community repository's length rules: 30 to 4000 characters.

setters.name: releaseNotes
setters.doc: The release notes (`<releaseNotes>`): text, Markdown, or a URL.

setters.name: url64bit
setters.doc:
The 64-bit zip on the release (required; must be `https`) — what the
install script downloads (`url64bit`) and unpacks into the package's
`tools` directory, where choco shims every `.exe` it holds.

setters.name: checksum64
setters.doc:
The zip's SHA-256 (required; 64 hex digits) — checked by choco before
anything is unpacked (`checksum64`, with `checksumType64 = 'sha256'`).

settings.name: ChocolateyVerifySettings
settings.doc: Settings for verifying a rendered package.

setters.name: package
setters.doc: The package to verify (required) — what `ChocolateyTasks.package` rendered.

setters.name: binary
setters.doc:
The command the package puts on `PATH` (required), e.g. `app` — choco
names each shim after the `.exe` it found in the zip.

setters.name: command
setters.doc: The arguments to run the binary with, e.g. `"--version"`.

setters.name: expectVersion
setters.doc: Require the binary's output to contain the package version.

setters.name: expectOutput
setters.doc: Require the binary's output to contain `text`.

setters.name: toolPath
setters.doc: The `choco` to run, when it is not on `PATH`.

setters.name: package
setters.doc:
The package to publish — what `ChocolateyTasks.package` rendered. It is
packed in a temporary directory and the `.nupkg` pushed. Set this or
nupkg, not both.

setters.name: nupkg
setters.doc: A `.nupkg` already built, pushed as it is. Set this or package.

setters.name: apiKey
setters.doc:
The source's API key — for the community repository, the one on
`https://community.chocolatey.org/account`. Masked in every rendering of
the push and in its errors. When unset, choco uses the key saved for the
source with `choco apikey add`.

setters.name: source
setters.doc:
The source to push to (`https`), defaulting to the community repository,
`https://push.chocolatey.org/`. An internal feed's push URL works too.

setters.name: toolPath
setters.doc: The `choco` to run, when it is not on `PATH`.

settings.name: ChocolateyVerifyJobSettings
settings.doc: Settings for the package-verification CI job.

setters.name: target
setters.doc:
The target to run (required) — one that calls `ChocolateyTasks.verify`,
or otherwise installs, checks and uninstalls the package.

setters.name: runners
setters.doc:
The runner labels to verify on, replacing the default `windows-latest` —
e.g. `"windows-2022", "windows-2025"` to cover both images. Each must be
a Windows runner with Chocolatey installed.

packages.name: homebrew
packages.summary: `@zuke/homebrew` — ship a prebuilt binary through a [Homebrew](https://brew.sh) tap from a Zuke build: `BrewTasks` wraps the `brew` CLI, and `HomebrewTasks` renders a formula, publishes it to the tap, verifies it installs, and declares the CI job that verifies it on macOS and Linux.

tasks.name: BrewTasks
tasks.doc: Typed task functions for the Homebrew `brew` CLI.

tasks.name: run
tasks.doc: Run any `brew` command, built with `.command(...)`/`.flag(...)`.

tasks.name: install
tasks.doc: Install formulae (`brew install`).

tasks.name: uninstall
tasks.doc: Uninstall formulae (`brew uninstall`).

tasks.name: test
tasks.doc: Run installed formulae's `test do` blocks (`brew test`).

tasks.name: audit
tasks.doc: Audit formulae against Homebrew's rules (`brew audit`).

tasks.name: style
tasks.doc: Check formulae against Homebrew's RuboCop style (`brew style`).

tasks.name: livecheck
tasks.doc: Look for newer upstream versions (`brew livecheck`).

tasks.name: tap
tasks.doc: Add a tap (`brew tap`).

tasks.name: untap
tasks.doc: Remove taps (`brew untap`).

tasks.name: tapNew
tasks.doc: Generate a new local tap (`brew tap-new`).

tasks.name: trust
tasks.doc: Trust a non-official tap's formulae, casks or commands (`brew trust`).

tasks.name: repository
tasks.doc:
The directory of Homebrew's repository, or of a tap
(`brew --repository [tap]`), as a path with the trailing newline removed.

tasks.name: info
tasks.doc:
Describe formulae (`brew info --json=v2`), parsed into a BrewInfo:
names, versions and the installed versions.

tasks.name: HomebrewTasks
tasks.doc: Tasks for shipping a prebuilt binary through a Homebrew tap.

tasks.name: formula
tasks.doc:
The Ruby source of a formula that installs prebuilt binaries — one
archive per OS and CPU family. Pure: nothing is read or written.

tasks.name: publish
tasks.doc:
Write `Formula/<name>.rb` into a tap repository on GitHub, or leave it
alone — reporting `unchanged` — when the tap already holds exactly that
source.

tasks.name: verify
tasks.doc:
Install a formula file through a throwaway local tap, trusted first, run
its test, then uninstall it and remove the tap — the cleanup runs whether
or not the install and test succeeded.

tasks.name: verifyJob
tasks.doc:
The CI job that runs a verifying target across macOS and Linux runners,
ready to list in `cicd({ invokes: [...] })`.

settings.name: BrewCommandSettings
settings.doc:
Base for a typed `brew` subcommand: the verb, then its own flags, then its
operands — the order brew's own usage lines print. Anything added through
the inherited `.command(...)`/`.flag(...)` escape hatches follows.

Operands are refused when they start with `-`. A formula or tap name never
does, and brew would read one that did as an option — so `--force` passed as
a "formula" would change what the command does rather than fail.

settings.name: BrewAuditSettings
settings.doc:
Settings for `brew audit`. With no formulae named, brew audits every
formula it can find.

setters.name: formulae
setters.doc: Formulae to audit; repeatable.

setters.name: strict
setters.doc: Run the additional, stricter checks (`--strict`).

setters.name: online
setters.doc: Run the additional checks that need the network (`--online`).

setters.name: new
setters.doc:
Run the checks for a formula new to Homebrew (`--new`), which imply
`--strict` and `--online`.

setters.name: formula
setters.doc: Treat every name as a formula, not a cask (`--formula`).

settings.name: BrewInstallSettings
settings.doc:
Settings for `brew install`. A formula is named by its name, its
`user/tap/name`, or — where Homebrew still allows it — a local `.rb` path.

setters.name: formulae
setters.doc: Formulae to install (required); repeatable.

setters.name: formula
setters.doc: Treat every name as a formula, not a cask (`--formula`).

setters.name: buildFromSource
setters.doc: Compile from source even when a bottle exists (`--build-from-source`).

setters.name: force
setters.doc: Install without checking for keg-only or unmigrated versions (`--force`).

setters.name: verbose
setters.doc: Print the verification and post-install steps (`--verbose`).

settings.name: BrewLivecheckSettings
settings.doc: Settings for `brew livecheck`, which looks for a newer upstream version.

setters.name: formulae
setters.doc: Formulae to check; repeatable.

setters.name: json
setters.doc: Print the result as JSON (`--json`).

setters.name: newerOnly
setters.doc: Report only versions newer than the installed one (`--newer-only`).

setters.name: formula
setters.doc: Check only formulae, not casks (`--formula`).

settings.name: BrewRepositorySettings
settings.doc:
Settings for `brew --repository`, which prints where Homebrew's repository
is — or, given a tap, where that tap's directory is.

setters.name: tap
setters.doc: The tap whose directory to print, `user/repo`.

settings.name: BrewStyleSettings
settings.doc:
Settings for `brew style`, Homebrew's RuboCop check. With nothing named it
checks Homebrew's own code and every tap.

setters.name: targets
setters.doc: Files, taps or formulae to check; repeatable.

setters.name: fix
setters.doc: Correct what RuboCop can correct (`--fix`).

settings.name: BrewTapNewSettings
settings.doc: Settings for `brew tap-new`, which generates a new, local tap.

setters.name: name
setters.doc: The tap to create (required), `user/repo`.

setters.name: noGit
setters.doc: Do not initialise a git repository for it (`--no-git`).

setters.name: branch
setters.doc: Initialise git on this branch, with its CI workflows (`--branch=`).

settings.name: BrewTapSettings
settings.doc: Settings for `brew tap`, which adds a formula repository.

setters.name: name
setters.doc:
The tap to add (required), `user/repo` — brew clones
`github.com/user/homebrew-repo` — and optionally the URL to clone it from
instead.

setters.name: force
setters.doc: Tap a core tap even under API mode (`--force`).

settings.name: BrewTestSettings
settings.doc: Settings for `brew test`, which runs a formula's `test do` block.

setters.name: formulae
setters.doc: Installed formulae to test (required); repeatable.

setters.name: force
setters.doc: Test even when the formula is unlinked (`--force`).

setters.name: keepTmp
setters.doc: Keep the temporary files the test created (`--keep-tmp`).

setters.name: retry
setters.doc: Retry once if the test fails (`--retry`).

settings.name: BrewTrustSettings
settings.doc:
Settings for `brew trust`, which lets Homebrew load a non-official tap's
formulae, casks or commands. Current Homebrew refuses to load them from a tap
it has not been told to trust.

setters.name: targets
setters.doc: What to trust: taps, formulae, casks or commands by name; repeatable.

setters.name: tap
setters.doc: The names are taps (`--tap`).

setters.name: formula
setters.doc: The names are formulae (`--formula`).

setters.name: cask
setters.doc: The names are casks (`--cask`).

setters.name: externalCommand
setters.doc: The names are external commands (`--command`).

setters.name: formulae
setters.doc: Formulae to uninstall (required); repeatable.

setters.name: formula
setters.doc: Treat every name as a formula, not a cask (`--formula`).

setters.name: force
setters.doc: Delete every installed version (`--force`).

setters.name: ignoreDependencies
setters.doc: Uninstall even when another formula depends on it (`--ignore-dependencies`).

settings.name: BrewUntapSettings
settings.doc: Settings for `brew untap`, which removes taps.

setters.name: taps
setters.doc: Taps to remove (required), `user/repo`; repeatable.

setters.name: force
setters.doc: Uninstall the tap's formulae first, rather than refusing (`--force`).

settings.name: BrewInfoSettings
settings.doc:
Settings for `brew info`, which always runs with `--json=v2` — the
documented, machine-readable form — so the task can hand back a
BrewInfo.

setters.name: formulae
setters.doc: Formulae to describe; repeatable.

setters.name: formula
setters.doc: Treat every name as a formula, not a cask (`--formula`).

setters.name: installed
setters.doc: Describe every installed formula (`--installed`), instead of naming them.

settings.name: FormulaSettings
settings.doc: Settings for a formula that installs prebuilt binaries.

setters.name: name
setters.doc:
The formula name (required), e.g. `app` or `app@2`: a lowercase letter,
then lowercase letters, digits, `-`, `_`, `.`, `+` or `@`. The Ruby class
name is derived from it exactly as Homebrew does — `app-cli` defines
`AppCli`, `app@2` defines `AppAT2`.

setters.name: description
setters.doc:
The one-line description (`desc`, required), held to `brew audit`'s rules:
at most 80 characters, starting with a capital letter, not with an
article or the formula's name, and with no trailing period.

setters.name: homepage
setters.doc: The project's homepage (required; must be `https`).

setters.name: version
setters.doc:
The version, e.g. `1.2.3` — set it only when Homebrew cannot read it from
the archive URLs.

Homebrew detects a formula's version from its URL, and `brew audit`
rejects a `version` line that repeats what it detected ("version … is
redundant with version scanned from URL"). A GitHub release asset such as
`…/releases/download/v1.2.3/app-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.gz` carries it, so
leave this unset there; `expectVersion()` in the test still works, against
the detected version. Set it for a URL with no version in it, such as a
`…/releases/latest/download/…` link or a content-addressed store.

setters.name: license
setters.doc: The SPDX license identifier, e.g. `MIT`.

setters.name: binary
setters.doc:
Add a prebuilt archive for one OS and CPU family. Call once per platform;
at least one is required, and each OS/arch pair at most once.

setters.name: install
setters.doc:
Files from the archive to place in the formula's `bin` (`bin.install`);
at least one is required. Plain file names only — no directory part.

setters.name: caveats
setters.doc: Text Homebrew prints after installing (`def caveats`).

setters.name: test
setters.doc:
The formula's `test do` block, which `brew test` runs. Without one,
`brew test` (and so `HomebrewTasks.verify`) fails.

settings.name: FormulaBinarySettings
settings.doc:
Settings for one prebuilt binary of a formula, rendered as
`on_<os> do on_<arch> do url "…" sha256 "…" end end`.

```ts
s.binary((b) =>
  b.os("macos").arch("arm").url("https://…/app-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.gz")
    .sha256("…")
)
```

setters.name: os
setters.doc: The operating system the archive runs on (required).

setters.name: arch
setters.doc: The CPU family the archive runs on (required).

setters.name: url
setters.doc: Where Homebrew downloads the archive (required; must be `https`).

setters.name: sha256
setters.doc: The archive's SHA-256 (required; 64 lowercase hex digits).

settings.name: FormulaTestSettings

setters.name: binary
setters.doc:
Which installed binary to run. Defaults to the first one the formula
installs; it must be one of them.

setters.name: command
setters.doc: The arguments to run the binary with, e.g. `"--version"`.

setters.name: expectVersion
setters.doc: Require the output to contain the formula's version.

setters.name: expectOutput
setters.doc: Require the output to contain `text`.

settings.name: HomebrewPublishSettings
settings.doc: Settings for publishing a formula to a tap.

setters.name: tap
setters.doc:
The tap (required): its GitHub repository `owner/homebrew-x`, or brew's
short form `owner/x`, which names the same repository.

setters.name: formula
setters.doc:
The formula to publish (required): its name, which becomes the file
`Formula/<name>.rb`, and its Ruby source — typically what
`HomebrewTasks.formula` rendered.

setters.name: token
setters.doc:
The token to write with — needs `contents: write` on the tap repository.
Defaults to `GITHUB_TOKEN`, which only works when the tap is the
repository the job runs in; a separate tap needs its own token.

setters.name: branch
setters.doc: The branch to commit on. Defaults to the tap's default branch.

setters.name: message
setters.doc: The commit message. Defaults to `<name>: update formula`.

setters.name: baseUrl
setters.doc: The API root, for GitHub Enterprise.

settings.name: HomebrewVerifySettings
settings.doc: Settings for verifying a formula file.

setters.name: formulaFile
setters.doc: The formula's Ruby source on disk (required), e.g. `dist/app.rb`.

setters.name: name
setters.doc:
The formula's name (required) — the class the file defines is derived
from it, and it is installed and tested under it.

setters.name: toolPath
setters.doc:
The `brew` to run, when it is not on `PATH` — on a GitHub Linux runner
Homebrew is installed but not on `PATH`:
`/home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/bin/brew`.

settings.name: HomebrewVerifyJobSettings
settings.doc: Settings for the formula-verification CI job.

setters.name: target
setters.doc:
The target to run (required) — one that calls `HomebrewTasks.verify`, or
otherwise installs, tests and uninstalls the formula.

setters.name: runners
setters.doc:
The runner labels to verify on, replacing the default `macos-latest` and
`ubuntu-latest` — e.g. `"macos-15", "macos-15-intel", "ubuntu-latest"` to
cover both Mac CPU families. GitHub's ARM Linux runners
(`ubuntu-24.04-arm`) ship without Homebrew, so they cannot verify a
formula without installing it first.

packages.name: codecov
packages.summary: `@zuke/codecov` — a typed Codecov CLI (`codecovcli`) task wrapper for Zuke builds.

tasks.name: CodecovTasks
tasks.doc: Typed task functions for the Codecov CLI.

tasks.name: upload
tasks.doc: Upload coverage reports: `codecovcli upload-process`.

setters.name: files
setters.doc: A coverage report file to upload (`--file`). Repeatable.

setters.name: flags
setters.doc: Tag the uploaded reports with a flag (`--flag`). Repeatable.

setters.name: plugins
setters.doc: Run an upload plugin, e.g. `gcov` or `noop` (`--plugin`). Repeatable.

setters.name: token
setters.doc:
Repository upload token.

Routed through `CODECOV_TOKEN` rather than `--token`, because a child's
argv is world-readable: `ps` or `/proc/<pid>/cmdline` shows it to every
other user on the host and to every process the build starts. The
environment of another process is not readable the same way, and the CLI
documents the variable, so nothing is given up by preferring it.

Also registered with the run's redactor, so a value that reaches the
output some other way — an error message quoting a URL, a tool echoing its
own configuration — is masked there too.

setters.name: slug
setters.doc: Repository slug as `OWNER/REPO` (`--slug`).

setters.name: sha
setters.doc: Commit SHA the coverage belongs to (`--sha`).

setters.name: branch
setters.doc: Branch the coverage belongs to (`--branch`).

setters.name: pullRequest
setters.doc: Pull request number the coverage belongs to (`--pr`).

setters.name: gitService
setters.doc: Git host the repo lives on, e.g. `github` (`--git-service`).

setters.name: name
setters.doc: A custom display name for this upload (`--name`).

setters.name: dir
setters.doc: Directory to search for coverage reports (`--dir`).

setters.name: networkRootFolder
setters.doc: Root folder used to resolve report file paths (`--network-root-folder`).

setters.name: reportType
setters.doc: Report kind: `coverage` (default) or `test_results` (`--report-type`).

setters.name: disableTelem
setters.doc:
Keep the CLI from reporting its own errors to Codecov's Sentry
(`--disable-telem`). A global flag, so it is emitted before the subcommand.

setters.name: disableSearch
setters.doc: Upload only the named files, skipping the auto-search (`--disable-search`).

setters.name: handleNoReportsFound
setters.doc: Succeed instead of erroring when no reports are found (`--handle-no-reports-found`).

setters.name: failOnError
setters.doc: Exit non-zero when the upload fails (`--fail-on-error`).

setters.name: dryRun

packages.summary: `@zuke/ai` — AI-powered code review for Zuke builds.

tasks.name: AiTasks
tasks.doc: Typed task functions over the reviewers, for a build that calls rather than declares them.

tasks.name: review
tasks.doc:
Run the configured reviewers as peers of one target, in order. Throws when
a reviewer's gate trips, as the target it guards would fail.

tasks.name: preflight
tasks.doc:
Run the reviewers' preflight: on a comment-started run, refuse a commenter
who may not start a review. A no-op on any other run.

settings.name: DiffSettings
settings.doc: Fluent diff source configuration passed to "./reviewer.ts".Reviewer.diff.

setters.name: base
setters.doc: Review the diff against `ref` (e.g. `"origin/main"`).

setters.name: staged
setters.doc: Review the staged changes (`git diff --cached`).

setters.name: text
setters.doc: Review a diff supplied directly, bypassing `git` (useful in tests).

setters.name: fetchBase
setters.doc:
Fetch the base branch (a shallow, tag-less `git fetch`) before diffing, and
diff against it — so CI needs no manual `git fetch` step. With no `branch`,
the base is auto-detected from the CI environment (GitHub's `GITHUB_BASE_REF`
— the pull request's base branch). Honoured by the "./fixer.ts".AiFixer; if the fetch fails it falls back to the working-tree
diff.

setters.name: scoreAbove
setters.doc: Fail when the assessed risk score is strictly above `value` (0–10).

setters.name: severityAtLeast
setters.doc: Fail when the overall severity is at least `value`.

settings.name: DiscussionSettings
settings.doc:
Fluent settings for "./reviewer.ts".Reviewer.discussion — who the
reviewer listens to on the PR thread, and how much of it the model may see.

setters.name: trustAssociations
setters.doc:
Replace the trusted `author_association` set (default `OWNER`, `MEMBER`,
`COLLABORATOR`). Comments from authors outside it (and outside
trustAuthors) are dropped before the model sees them.

setters.name: trustAuthors
setters.doc:
Trust these author logins in addition to the association rule — e.g. an
outside collaborator whose review the project wants the reviewer to
engage with.

setters.name: maxCommentTokens
setters.doc:
Cap the total comment text sent to the model at roughly this many tokens
(default 4000), newest comments kept first — so a wall of text cannot
crowd the diff and the rubric out of the context window.

setters.name: threads
setters.doc:
Also anchor each finding to a file/line **review thread** on the pull
request, so a maintainer contests it by replying in that thread instead of
quoting its id somewhere on the PR.

The summary comment is posted either way and stays the one source of
truth: it lists every finding — anchored or not — and carries the state
block, so a thread that cannot be posted never hides a finding. The
reviewer replies into the thread with the outcome and resolves it once the
finding is fixed or dismissed. GitHub only; on other hosts the reviewer
notes that and posts the summary alone.

setters.name: commands
setters.doc:
Take commands from maintainers, addressed to `mention` — e.g.
`"@zuke-build"`, the account the workflow's comment command is addressed
to, so one handle serves both.

With it set, every review comment carries a collapsed **Commands** panel
listing what a maintainer can say, and a trusted comment starting with
`<mention> accept <id> <reason>` **accepts** the finding: it is recorded as
accepted for this pull request without adjudication, answered in its
thread and the thread resolved, and never re-raised on the pull request
by any reviewer, however it is reworded, moved or escalated. In a
finding's own thread the id may be left out. The trust gate is the one
rebuttals pass — trustAssociations and trustAuthors,
decided in code from the host's author metadata — so a stranger's
`accept` is dropped before anything reads it. Unlike a rebuttal, an
acceptance is **one key**: no adjudicator weighs it. On a host where the
default associations admit accounts that should not decide for the
project (GitHub's `MEMBER` and `COLLABORATOR` include read-only ones),
narrow the gate with trustAssociations or trustAuthors
before turning commands on.

The panel also lists `<mention> review`, the workflow's comment command
that runs the review on demand; pair this with `aiReviewWorkflow`'s
`command` so that both are true.

settings.name: Reviewer
settings.doc:
A fluent AI reviewer. Construct one via securityReviewer (and the
sibling factories), configure it, and attach it to a target with
`.validateBefore(...)` / `.validateAfter(...)`. `.provider(...)` and
`.apiKey(...)` are required; everything else has a default.

setters.name: provider
setters.doc: Set the model provider (required).

setters.name: apiKey
setters.doc: Set the API key, from a secret parameter or a literal string (required).

setters.name: model
setters.doc: Override the model (default: the provider's recommended model).

setters.name: effort
setters.doc: Set the thinking-effort hint (honoured by Claude; ignored elsewhere).

setters.name: criteria
setters.doc:
Optional project-specific notes appended above the diff in the user prompt
— framing that fine-tunes the built-in rubric (e.g. "strict TypeScript,
no `any`/`as`"). Works for every reviewer; the assessment's own system
prompt already covers what to look for, so this is purely additive.

These notes are **read from the head under review**, and cannot be
anything else: they are build code, evaluated by the very build the
pull request changed, so there is no base copy to read short of running
the base's build. A branch can therefore widen what its own review
overlooks, which is real but bounded — the change is first-party code in
the diff a maintainer reads, and a build that could not configure its own
reviewer from its own source would be a different feature.
Reviewer.criteriaFile is the base-anchored form for notes that
should not be editable by the change they judge.

setters.name: diff
setters.doc: Configure the diff source (default: the working-tree diff, `git diff`).

setters.name: include
setters.doc: Only review files matching these globs (default: all files).

setters.name: exclude
setters.doc: Exclude files matching these globs (in addition to lockfiles).

setters.name: maxDiffTokens
setters.doc: Cap the diff at roughly this many tokens, truncating the rest.

setters.name: failWhen
setters.doc: Choose the gate that breaks the build (default: score above 7).

setters.name: onError
setters.doc:
What to do when the review itself fails (API error, refusal, bad JSON):
`"fail"` breaks the build (default), `"warn"` logs and passes.

setters.name: skipIfKeyMissing
setters.doc:
Skip the review (instead of failing) when the API key is missing — handy
when the key is a CI-only secret. The skip is announced on the console and
in the job summary so the gap is visible.

setters.name: comment
setters.doc:
Also post the review to the pull/merge request as a comment. Works on
every supported CI host — GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Azure Pipelines,
Bitbucket Pipelines — dispatched at runtime by detectCiHost. A
no-op outside a PR context (e.g. local runs). On each host the workflow
must grant the right scope: GitHub `pull-requests: write`, GitLab a token
with the `api` scope, Azure `System.AccessToken`, Bitbucket an app
password.

`mode` chooses how re-runs post: `"update"` (default) keeps a single
comment per reviewer, edited in place; `"append"` posts a fresh comment
every run, so earlier assessments — and their finding ids — stay on the
thread as history. The discussion feature works with both: its state block
rides on every comment, and the newest one is read back.

Reviewers attached side by side to one target —
`.validateBefore(security, quality)` — post **one** comment between them
rather than one each: a table of every reviewer's verdict, the findings of
all of them in one table with a column naming the reviewer (and its
badge) that raised each, and each reviewer's full report folded
underneath. Every one of them runs even when an earlier one fails its
gate; the target then fails with all of their reasons. The comment is
posted by the last of them, with its token, and appended when any of
them appends. Each reviewer's discussion state rides in it under the
reviewer's name, and a reviewer that used to post alone still reads its
old comment. Another validation between two reviewers splits them, and a
reviewer alone posts its own comment as before.

setters.name: commentToken
setters.doc:
The token used to post the PR/MR comment. Defaults to the active host's
conventional env var: `GITHUB_TOKEN` (GitHub), `GITLAB_TOKEN` (GitLab),
`SYSTEM_ACCESSTOKEN` (Azure), `BITBUCKET_TOKEN` (Bitbucket).

A function is called each time a post needs the token — for a token that
does not exist until the build mints it, such as a GitHub App installation
token narrowed to `pull_requests: write`, which makes the comments the
app's rather than `github-actions[bot]`'s. A function that mints should
remember its result, since a review posts more than once. The generated
workflow cannot name a secret for a function, so it passes the host's
default token alongside, for the function to fall back to.

setters.name: githubToken
setters.doc: Backwards-compatible alias for commentToken.

setters.name: reactions
setters.doc:
Whether the reviewer reacts on the pull request to show its progress (on
by default, whenever `.comment()` is set). On the description: 👀 while
it runs, then 👍 when it passes clean, 🎉 when it passes clean where the
previous run failed, 🤏 when it has findings under the failing threshold
(😕 on GitHub, whose reaction set has no 🤏), 👎 when it fails. On the
comment that started a comment-started run: 👍 as it starts, 😕 when the
run could not review. On a trusted maintainer's reply: 👀 once read, ❤️
when it decided a finding. The reviewers on one pull request share the
reactions, so the verdict shown is the worst of a run's. GitHub and
GitLab have the reactions; on Azure DevOps and Bitbucket this is a no-op.
`false` turns all of it off, as does `.quiet()`, under which the reviewer
does not speak on the pull request.

setters.name: badge
setters.doc:
The emoji that marks this reviewer's findings — in the combined comment
the reviewers of one target share (see comment), and on the review
threads it opens. Defaults by kind: 🛡️ security, 🧹 code quality
(`genericReviewer`), 🔑 secrets, 🐛 correctness, ⚖️ license. Set one when
two reviewers of a kind review side by side — and give one of them a
name of its own, which is what the comment tells them apart by.

setters.name: quiet
setters.doc: Suppress the findings printout and the job-summary section.

setters.name: conventionsFile
setters.doc:
Feed the project's conventions document (e.g. `AGENTS.md`) to the model as
reference material, so the review judges the change against the project's
documented rules instead of generic taste. When the diff has a base ref
(`.diff((d) => d.base(...))` or a successful `.fetchBase()`), the file is
read from that **base** via `git show` — never from the head under review,
so a pull request cannot rewrite the rules it is judged by. Without a base
(a local working-tree review) it is read from disk. Truncated at roughly
`maxTokens` (default 8000).

setters.name: criteriaFile
setters.doc:
Project-specific notes read from a **file**, appended to whatever
Reviewer.criteria set inline — the base-anchored half of the same
slot.

Read exactly as Reviewer.conventionsFile is: from the diff's base
ref via `git show` when there is one, from disk otherwise, truncated at
roughly `maxTokens` (default 8000). That is the point of it. A note that
tells the reviewer a design is accepted — and so suppresses the findings
that restate it — is a rule the review is judged by, and a pull request
should not be able to add one to its own run. Keeping it in a file the
base supplies costs one merge of lag, which is the same lag the
conventions document already accepts, and is arguably the point: a newly
accepted design should be agreed before it starts muting findings.

Use it for what a branch should not be able to widen; keep
Reviewer.criteria for the framing that travels with the build.

What it does not buy: the build still decides *whether* to read a criteria
document at all, and that decision is head code, so a branch can drop the
call as easily as it can edit a string. This bounds what a change can add
to the rules of its own review, not whether the reviewer is configured —
the same limit Reviewer.conventionsFile has, and the reason the
