diff a maintainer reads remains the control that matters.

setters.name: fileContext
setters.doc:
Also send the full post-image contents of the changed files (read via
`git show HEAD:<path>`), bounded at roughly `maxTokens` (default 12000) —
so the model can check a finding against the surrounding code (an existing
guard, a validation a few lines away) instead of judging hunks in
isolation. Skipped silently for a literal `.diff((d) => d.text(...))`
source with no repository behind it.

setters.name: verify
setters.doc:
Add an adversarial verification pass: after the review produces candidate
findings, a second model call re-checks each against the diff (and the
fileContext, when enabled) and refutes any whose failure path it
cannot concretely trace. Refuted candidates are listed in the report but
neither posted as findings nor gated on. Costs one extra API call per
review with findings; if the pass itself errors, the unverified findings
are kept (fail toward reporting, never toward silence).

setters.name: discussion
setters.doc:
Engage with the pull-request discussion instead of repeating findings: the
reviewer reads the PR's comments, and when a **trusted** commenter (by the
host's own author metadata — see DiscussionSettings) contests a
finding by quoting its ID, an adjudication pass weighs the rebuttal on
technical merit and either upholds the finding (with the gap named) or
dismisses it. Dismissals persist across runs in a state block inside the
reviewer's own PR comment, so a dismissed finding — or a rewording of it —
does not resurface without new evidence. Requires comment (the
comment is where state lives) and a host that can list comments (GitHub
currently); elsewhere the discussion is skipped with a console note.

Untrusted comments are dropped in code before any prompt is built — the
model never sees them, so a drive-by "the maintainer approved this"
comment cannot influence the review.

settings.name: ReviewSettings
settings.doc:
The reviewers one `AiTasks.review` runs, as `.validateBefore(a, b)` would
run them, and the target they review for.

setters.name: target
setters.doc: The target the reviewers are attached to, named in their output; `review` by default.

setters.name: generic
setters.doc: Add a code-quality reviewer, as genericReviewer makes it.

setters.name: security
setters.doc: Add a security reviewer, as securityReviewer makes it.

setters.name: secrets
setters.doc: Add a leaked-secrets reviewer, as secretsReviewer makes it.

setters.name: correctness
setters.doc: Add a correctness reviewer, as correctnessReviewer makes it.

setters.name: license
setters.doc: Add a license reviewer, as licenseReviewer makes it.

packages.name: qr
packages.summary: `@zuke/qr` — QR codes for any data, from a Zuke build, with no dependency.

tasks.name: QrTasks
encode
tasks.doc: Encode `text` (as UTF-8, byte mode) into a QrCode matrix.

tasks.name: renderLines
tasks.doc: Encode `text` and render it as terminal lines (see QrSettings.compact).

tasks.name: render
tasks.doc: Encode `text` and render it as one newline-joined string.

settings.name: QrSettings
settings.doc:
Configuration for encoding and rendering a QR code, set through a lambda
passed to a `QrTasks` method. Every setter returns `this` so calls chain.

setters.name: errorCorrection
setters.doc: Set the error-correction level: `"L"` (~7%), `"M"` (~15%), `"Q"` (~25%) or `"H"` (~30%).

setters.name: boostErrorCorrection
setters.doc:
Whether to raise the error-correction level when a higher one fits the
same version. On by default; turn it off to get exactly the level asked for.

setters.name: quietZone
setters.doc: Set the width of the light border around the symbol, in modules (0 to MAX_QUIET_ZONE).

setters.name: invert
setters.doc:
Swap the colours: light modules become blocks and dark ones spaces. Use it
on a terminal whose text is light on dark, where the default rendering
shows the code with dark and light exchanged.

setters.name: compact
setters.doc:
Whether to draw two module rows per line with `▀`/`▄`/`█` (the default,
which keeps a version-3 code under 20 lines) or one row per line with a
two-character `██` cell per module.

packages.name: apple
packages.summary: `@zuke/apple` — typed task wrappers for Apple's code-signing tools in Zuke builds: `codesign`, `xcrun notarytool`, `security` and `ditto`.

tasks.name: CodesignTasks
tasks.doc: Typed task functions for Apple's `codesign`.

tasks.name: sign
tasks.doc: Sign code with `codesign --sign`.

tasks.name: verify
tasks.doc: Check a signature with `codesign --verify`; a bad one fails the run.

tasks.name: display
tasks.doc:
Describe a signature with `codesign --display`. `codesign` prints the
description on **stderr**, so it is returned parsed, with the raw text and
the command output alongside.

tasks.name: DittoTasks
tasks.doc: Typed task functions for macOS `ditto`.

tasks.name: copy
tasks.doc: Copy a file or directory tree with `ditto`, metadata intact.

tasks.name: archive
tasks.doc: Write a zip archive: `ditto -c -k`, then the lambda's settings.

tasks.name: extract
tasks.doc: Unpack a zip archive: `ditto -x -k`, then the lambda's settings.

tasks.name: NotarytoolTasks
tasks.doc: Typed task functions for `xcrun notarytool`.

tasks.name: submit
tasks.doc:
Upload an archive with `notarytool submit` and return the parsed result.
With `.wait()`, a final status other than `Accepted` fetches the
submission's log and throws a NotarizationError listing its
issues — unless `.noThrow()` was set, when the result is returned for the
caller to inspect.

tasks.name: info
tasks.doc: Read a submission's status with `notarytool info`.

tasks.name: log
tasks.doc: Fetch and parse a submission's notarization log with `notarytool log`.

tasks.name: history
tasks.doc: List the team's past submissions with `notarytool history`.

tasks.name: SecurityTasks
tasks.doc: Typed task functions for macOS `security`.

tasks.name: createKeychain
tasks.doc: Create a keychain with `security create-keychain`.

tasks.name: deleteKeychain
tasks.doc: Delete a keychain with `security delete-keychain`.

tasks.name: unlockKeychain
tasks.doc: Unlock a keychain with `security unlock-keychain`.

tasks.name: setKeychainSettings
tasks.doc: Change a keychain's lock settings with `security set-keychain-settings`.

tasks.name: import
tasks.doc: Import a certificate or key with `security import`.

tasks.name: setKeyPartitionList
tasks.doc: Set which tools may use a key with `security set-key-partition-list`.

tasks.name: listKeychains
tasks.doc:
Read — or, with `.set(...)`, replace — the keychain search list with
`security list-keychains`. Returns the listed paths; empty after a set,
which prints nothing.

tasks.name: findIdentity
tasks.doc: List signing identities with `security find-identity`, parsed.

tasks.name: XcodebuildTasks
tasks.doc: Typed task functions for `xcodebuild`.

tasks.name: archive
tasks.doc: Build an `.xcarchive`: `xcodebuild archive`.

tasks.name: exportArchive
tasks.doc: Export an archive to an `.ipa`, or upload it: `xcodebuild -exportArchive`.

tasks.name: showBuildSettings
tasks.doc: Print the resolved build settings: `xcodebuild -showBuildSettings`.

tasks.name: writeExportOptions
tasks.doc:
Write an `ExportOptions.plist` for exportArchive to `path`. Runs
no subprocess.

tasks.name: AltoolTasks
tasks.doc: Typed task functions for `xcrun altool`.

tasks.name: uploadApp
tasks.doc: Upload an app to App Store Connect: `xcrun altool --upload-app`.

tasks.name: validateApp
tasks.doc: Validate an app without uploading it: `xcrun altool --validate-app`.

tasks.name: ProvisioningProfileTasks
tasks.doc: Read and install provisioning profiles.

tasks.name: inspect
tasks.doc: Read what a profile says about itself, without installing it.

tasks.name: install
tasks.doc:
Install a profile where Xcode looks for it, named by its UUID. Refuses an
expired profile unless `.allowExpired()`.

tasks.name: TestFlightTasks
tasks.doc: Distribute builds in TestFlight through the App Store Connect API.

tasks.name: distribute
tasks.doc:
Wait for an uploaded build to be processed, then distribute it in
TestFlight as configured.

settings.name: CodesignSettings
settings.doc:
The shared shape of every `codesign` operation: the files it acts on and how
verbose it is. Each operation subclass names its mode flag and its own
options.

setters.name: file
setters.doc:
The code to act on (positional) — an app bundle, framework, binary or
disk image; repeatable. A relative path starting with `-` is passed as
`./-…` so `codesign` cannot read it as an option.

setters.name: verbose
setters.doc:
More output (`--verbose`, or `--verbose=<level>` with a level). `display`
shows more of the signature at each level; `4` lists everything.

setters.name: identity
setters.doc:
The signing identity (`--sign <identity>`): a certificate's common name,
a substring of it, or its SHA-1 hash. `-` signs ad hoc. Required.

setters.name: force
setters.doc: Replace an existing signature (`--force`).

setters.name: deep
setters.doc: Sign nested code as well (`--deep`). Apple discourages it for signing.

setters.name: options
setters.doc:
Signature option flags (`--options`, comma-joined); repeatable.
`runtime` enables the hardened runtime notarization requires.

setters.name: timestamp
setters.doc:
Request a secure timestamp (`--timestamp`), from `url` when given
(`--timestamp=<url>`). Notarization requires one.

setters.name: entitlements
setters.doc: The entitlements plist to embed (`--entitlements`).

setters.name: keychain
setters.doc: Look the identity up in this keychain only (`--keychain`).

setters.name: identifier
setters.doc: The code's identifier (`--identifier`), overriding the bundle id.

setters.name: strict
setters.doc: Apply the strict validation rules notarization uses (`--strict`).

setters.name: deep
setters.doc: Verify nested code as well (`--deep`).

setters.name: create
setters.doc: Create an archive rather than copy (`-c`).

setters.name: extract
setters.doc: Extract an archive rather than copy (`-x`).

setters.name: pkzip
setters.doc: Use the PKZip format for the archive (`-k`) instead of CPIO.

setters.name: sequesterRsrc
setters.doc:
Keep resource forks and HFS metadata in a `__MACOSX` directory inside the
archive (`--sequesterRsrc`), the way the Finder's own compress does.

setters.name: keepParent
setters.doc:
Put the source directory itself in the archive, not only its contents
(`--keepParent`) — what makes a zipped `MyApp.app` unzip as `MyApp.app`.

setters.name: source
setters.doc: What to copy or archive (positional). Required.

setters.name: destination
setters.doc: Where to write it (positional). Required.

setters.name: method
setters.doc: How the archive is exported (`method`); required.

setters.name: teamId
setters.doc: The developer team id (`teamID`).

setters.name: signingStyle
setters.doc: Automatic or manual signing (`signingStyle`).

setters.name: signingCertificate
setters.doc: The certificate to sign with, e.g. `Apple Distribution` (`signingCertificate`).

setters.name: provisioningProfile
setters.doc:
The provisioning profile, by name or UUID, for one bundle identifier
(`provisioningProfiles`); repeatable, once per app and extension.

setters.name: destination
setters.doc: Export to a directory, or upload to App Store Connect (`destination`).

setters.name: uploadSymbols
setters.doc: Include symbols for crash reports (`uploadSymbols`).

setters.name: manageAppVersionAndBuildNumber
setters.doc: Let App Store Connect manage the version and build number (`manageAppVersionAndBuildNumber`).

setters.name: stripSwiftSymbols
setters.doc: Strip Swift symbols from the binary (`stripSwiftSymbols`).

setters.name: testFlightInternalTestingOnly
setters.doc: Limit a TestFlight upload to internal testers (`testFlightInternalTestingOnly`).

setters.name: certificate
setters.doc:
The signing certificate and its private key, as a base64-encoded `.p12`
— the form CI secrets hold it in. Whitespace is ignored. Required. It is
decoded only into a `0600` file that is deleted straight after import,
and never appears in a command line or an error message.

setters.name: certificatePassword
setters.doc:
The `.p12`'s export password, handed to `security import -P`. A secret:
masked in every rendering of that command. Defaults to empty, for a
`.p12` exported without one — `security` would otherwise prompt.

setters.name: identity
setters.doc:
Pick the identity whose name contains `filter`, or whose SHA-1 hash it
is. Needed only when the `.p12` holds more than one codesigning identity.

setters.name: application
setters.doc:
An application allowed to use the imported key (`security import -T`);
repeatable. Defaults to `/usr/bin/codesign` when none is named.

setters.name: toolPath
setters.doc: Run this `security` binary instead of the one on `PATH`.

settings.name: NotarytoolSettings
settings.doc:
The shared settings of every `xcrun notarytool` subcommand: the credentials,
and the masking of the app-specific password. A subclass names its
subcommand and builds its own arguments.

setters.name: key
setters.doc: The App Store Connect API private key file, `AuthKey_<id>.p8` (`--key`).

setters.name: keyId
setters.doc: The API key's id (`--key-id`).

setters.name: issuer
setters.doc: The API key's issuer UUID (`--issuer`); omit it for an individual key.

setters.name: keychainProfile
setters.doc:
Authenticate with credentials saved by `notarytool store-credentials`
(`--keychain-profile`).

setters.name: keychain
setters.doc: The keychain to read the keychainProfile from (`--keychain`).

setters.name: appleId
setters.doc: The Apple ID to authenticate as (`--apple-id`).

setters.name: password
setters.doc:
The Apple ID's app-specific password (`--password`). Registered with the
run's redactor and masked out of any error this run raises.

setters.name: teamId
setters.doc: The developer team id the Apple ID signs for (`--team-id`).

setters.name: toolPath
setters.doc: Override the binary, remembered so a follow-up command uses it too.

setters.name: env
setters.doc: Merge environment variables, remembered for a follow-up command too.

setters.name: cwd
setters.doc: Set the working directory, remembered for a follow-up command too.

setters.name: submissionId
setters.doc: The submission to describe (positional). Required.

setters.name: submissionId
setters.doc: The submission whose log to fetch (positional). Required.

setters.name: file
setters.doc: The archive to notarize — a `.zip`, `.pkg` or `.dmg` (positional). Required.

setters.name: wait
setters.doc:
Wait for Apple to finish processing (`--wait`). With it the result
carries the final status, and `NotarytoolTasks.submit` throws a
`NotarizationError` for anything but `Accepted`.

setters.name: timeout
setters.doc: How long `--wait` waits, e.g. `30m` or `1h` (`--timeout`). Needs wait.

setters.name: logFor
setters.doc:
Settings for `notarytool log <id>` that reuse this submission's
credentials, binary, environment and working directory.

settings.name: SecuritySettings
settings.doc:
The shared settings of every `security` subcommand: the binary, and the
secret handling for the passwords a subcommand takes. A subclass names its
subcommand and builds its own arguments.

setters.name: file
setters.doc: The file to import, e.g. a `.p12` (positional). Required.

setters.name: keychain
setters.doc: The keychain to import into (`-k`); the default keychain when omitted.

setters.name: passphrase
setters.doc:
The file's passphrase (`-P`), e.g. a `.p12`'s export password. A secret:
masked in every rendering of the command.

setters.name: application
setters.doc:
An application allowed to use the imported key without a prompt (`-T`),
e.g. `/usr/bin/codesign`; repeatable.

setters.name: type
setters.doc: The type of item in the file (`-t`).

setters.name: format
setters.doc: The file's format (`-f`), e.g. `pkcs12`.

setters.name: nonExtractable
setters.doc: Make the imported private key non-extractable (`-x`).

settings.name: SecuritySetKeyPartitionListSettings
settings.doc:
Settings for `security set-key-partition-list`, which lets Apple's signing
tools use a key without the "allow access" prompt that hangs a headless
build.

setters.name: partitionList
setters.doc:
Partition ids to allow (`-S`, comma-joined); repeatable. `apple-tool:`
and `apple:` cover `codesign` and the other Apple tools.

setters.name: privateKeys
setters.doc: Match private keys only (`-s`).

setters.name: password
setters.doc:
The keychain's password (`-k`). A secret: masked in every rendering of
the command. Without it `security` prompts for one.

setters.name: keychain
setters.doc: The keychain to modify (positional); the default keychain when omitted.

setters.name: password
setters.doc:
The new keychain's password (`-p`). A secret: masked in every rendering
of the command. Without it `security` prompts for one.

setters.name: keychain
setters.doc: The keychain(s) to create (positional); repeatable. Required.

setters.name: keychain
setters.doc: The keychain(s) to delete (positional); repeatable. Required.

settings.name: SecuritySetKeychainSettings
settings.doc:
Settings for `security set-keychain-settings`. With no flags, the keychain
never locks on its own — no timeout, and no lock on sleep — which is what a
CI keychain wants for the length of a build.

setters.name: lockOnSleep
setters.doc: Lock the keychain when the machine sleeps (`-l`).

setters.name: lockAfterTimeout
setters.doc: Lock the keychain after timeout seconds of inactivity (`-u`).

setters.name: timeout
setters.doc: The inactivity timeout, in seconds (`-t`).

setters.name: keychain
setters.doc: The keychain to configure (positional); the default keychain when omitted.

setters.name: password
setters.doc:
The keychain's password (`-p`). A secret: masked in every rendering of
the command. Without it `security` prompts for one.

setters.name: keychain
setters.doc: The keychain to unlock (positional); the default keychain when omitted.

setters.name: policy
setters.doc: Only identities usable under this policy (`-p`), e.g. `codesigning`.

setters.name: search
setters.doc: Only identities whose name contains this string (`-s`).

setters.name: valid
setters.doc: Only valid identities (`-v`) — not expired, revoked or untrusted.

setters.name: keychain
setters.doc: The keychain(s) to search (positional); the search list when omitted.

setters.name: domain
setters.doc: The preference domain to read or set (`-d`).

setters.name: set
setters.doc:
Replace the search list with these keychains (`-s`), in order. Called
with none, it empties the list. Repeat calls append.

settings.name: XcodebuildSettings
settings.doc: Base for all `xcodebuild` settings: the binary is `xcodebuild`, on `PATH`.

setters.name: quietOutput
setters.doc: Print only warnings and errors (`-quiet`).

setters.name: allowProvisioningUpdates
setters.doc:
Let Xcode create and update provisioning profiles and certificates
(`-allowProvisioningUpdates`); on CI, pair it with
authenticationKey.

setters.name: authenticationKey
setters.doc:
Sign in to the developer account with an App Store Connect API key
instead of an Xcode account: the `AuthKey_<id>.p8` file, its key id and
its issuer id (`-authenticationKeyPath`, `-authenticationKeyID`,
`-authenticationKeyIssuerID`).

settings.name: XcodebuildProjectSettings
settings.doc:
The project flags every build action takes. Each action names itself and
its own flags; the project flags come first, then the action, then the
build settings.

setters.name: workspace
setters.doc: The workspace to build, e.g. `App.xcworkspace` (`-workspace`).

setters.name: project
setters.doc: The project to build, e.g. `App.xcodeproj` (`-project`).

setters.name: scheme
setters.doc: The scheme to build (`-scheme`); required with a workspace. A later call replaces it.

setters.name: configuration
setters.doc: The build configuration, e.g. `Release` (`-configuration`). A later call replaces it.

setters.name: sdk
setters.doc: The SDK, e.g. `iphoneos` or `iphonesimulator` (`-sdk`). A later call replaces it.

setters.name: destination
setters.doc:
A destination, e.g. `generic/platform=iOS` or
`platform=iOS Simulator,name=iPhone 16` (`-destination`); repeatable.

setters.name: derivedDataPath
setters.doc: Where intermediate build files go (`-derivedDataPath`).

setters.name: clonedSourcePackagesDirPath
setters.doc: Where Swift packages are checked out (`-clonedSourcePackagesDirPath`).

setters.name: resultBundlePath
setters.doc: Write an `.xcresult` bundle with the logs and results (`-resultBundlePath`).

setters.name: xcconfig
setters.doc: Apply an `.xcconfig` file's settings over every target (`-xcconfig`).

setters.name: buildSetting
setters.doc:
Override a build setting for every target, e.g.
`("DEVELOPMENT_TEAM", "ABCDE12345")` → `DEVELOPMENT_TEAM=ABCDE12345`;
repeatable. A condition goes in the name:
`CODE_SIGN_IDENTITY[sdk=iphoneos*]`.

setters.name: archivePath
setters.doc: Where to write the `.xcarchive` (`-archivePath`); required.

setters.name: json
setters.doc: Print the settings as JSON (`-json`).

setters.name: archivePath
setters.doc: The `.xcarchive` to export (`-archivePath`); required.

setters.name: exportPath
setters.doc: The directory to write the export to (`-exportPath`); required.

setters.name: exportOptionsPlist
setters.doc:
The export options (`-exportOptionsPlist`); required. Write one with
`XcodebuildTasks.writeExportOptions`.

setters.name: file
setters.doc: The `.ipa` or `.pkg` to upload or validate (`--file`); required.

setters.name: type
setters.doc: The app's platform (`--type`); required.

setters.name: apiKey
setters.doc:
Authenticate with an App Store Connect API key: its key id and issuer id
(`--apiKey`, `--apiIssuer`). `altool` finds `AuthKey_<keyId>.p8` in
`~/.appstoreconnect/private_keys` and its other search directories, or in
apiPrivateKeysDir.

setters.name: apiPrivateKeysDir
setters.doc:
The directory holding `AuthKey_<keyId>.p8`, passed to `altool` as
`API_PRIVATE_KEYS_DIR`.

setters.name: appleId
setters.doc:
Authenticate with an Apple ID and an app-specific password
(`--username`, `--password`). The password is handed to `altool` in an
environment variable it reads through `@env:`, so it is never on the
command line, and it is registered with the run's redactor.

settings.name: AppStoreConnectSettings
settings.doc:
Settings for a task that calls the App Store Connect API with an API key
(*Users and Access → Integrations* in App Store Connect): the issuer id, the
key id, and the `AuthKey_<keyId>.p8` private key.

The private key and every token signed with it stay out of progress lines
and errors. Declare them in the build as `parameter(...).secret()` so Zuke
masks them in its own output too.

setters.name: issuerId
setters.doc: The API key's issuer id, a UUID.

setters.name: keyId
setters.doc: The API key's id, e.g. `ABC123`.

setters.name: privateKey
setters.doc: The private key, as the PEM text of `AuthKey_<keyId>.p8`.

setters.name: privateKeyFile
setters.doc: Read the private key from `AuthKey_<keyId>.p8`.

setters.name: apiUrl
setters.doc:
The API's base URL, `https://api.appstoreconnect.apple.com` by default.
It carries the token, so it must be `https:` unless it is loopback or
`ZUKE_ALLOW_INSECURE_URL` is set.

setters.name: file
setters.doc: Read the profile from a `.mobileprovision` file.

setters.name: base64
setters.doc:
Take the profile as base64 — how a CI secret usually holds it
(`base64 -i profile.mobileprovision`).

setters.name: directory
setters.doc: Install into this directory instead of Xcode's two defaults; repeatable.

setters.name: allowExpired
setters.doc: Install the profile even if it has expired.

setters.name: bundleId
setters.doc: The app's bundle id, e.g. `com.example.app`; required.

setters.name: buildNumber
setters.doc: The uploaded build's number, `CFBundleVersion`; required.

setters.name: version
setters.doc:
The uploaded build's version, `CFBundleShortVersionString` — needed when
the same build number exists under several versions.

setters.name: platform
setters.doc: The build's platform — needed when the app ships on several.

setters.name: timeout
setters.doc: The longest wait for the build to finish processing (`"45m"`, or ms); default 30 minutes.

setters.name: pollInterval
setters.doc: The time between two looks at the build (`"1m"`, or ms); default 30 seconds.

setters.name: usesNonExemptEncryption
setters.doc:
Answer the export-compliance question: whether the app uses encryption
beyond the exempt kinds. Until it is answered — here, or by
`ITSAppUsesNonExemptEncryption` in `Info.plist` — the build sits at
*Missing Compliance* and no tester can install it.

setters.name: whatToTest
setters.doc: The "What to Test" notes testers see, per locale; default locale `en-US`.

setters.name: group
setters.doc: Add the build to this beta group, by name; repeatable.

setters.name: submitForBetaReview
setters.doc: Submit the build for beta review, which external testing needs.

packages.name: google
packages.summary: `@zuke/google` — Google Play publishing for Zuke builds, through the Google Play Developer API.

tasks.name: GooglePlayTasks
tasks.doc: Publish to Google Play through the Google Play Developer API.

tasks.name: upload
tasks.doc: Upload an app bundle and release it on a track, in one committed edit.

settings.name: GooglePlaySettings
settings.doc:
Settings for `GooglePlayTasks.upload`.

The service-account key and every token signed with it stay out of progress
lines and errors. Declare the key in the build as `parameter(...).secret()`
so Zuke masks it in its own output too.

setters.name: serviceAccount
setters.doc:
The service account's key, as the text of the JSON file the Play Console
(or Google Cloud) downloaded; required. The account needs the *Release
apps to testing tracks* (or *Release to production*) permission on the
app.

setters.name: packageName
setters.doc: The app's package name, e.g. `com.example.app`; required.

setters.name: bundle
setters.doc: The Android app bundle (`.aab`) to upload; required.

setters.name: track
setters.doc:
The track to release on: `internal` (the default), `alpha`, `beta`,
`production`, or the name of a closed testing track.

setters.name: status
setters.doc: The release's status; default `completed`.

setters.name: releaseNotes
setters.doc:
The release notes users see, per BCP-47 language (`"en-US"`, `"bg"`);
repeatable, one call per language. Default language `en-US`.

setters.name: changesNotSentForReview
setters.doc:
Commit without sending the changes for review, so an app with managed
publishing or a release that review would otherwise hold can go out as
Google allows it to.

setters.name: timeout
setters.doc: The longest the whole upload may take (`"30m"`, or ms); default 15 minutes.

setters.name: apiUrl
setters.doc:
The API's base URL, `https://androidpublisher.googleapis.com` by default.
It carries the access token, so it must be `https:` unless it is loopback
or `ZUKE_ALLOW_INSECURE_URL` is set.

packages.name: signpath
packages.summary: `@zuke/signpath` — Authenticode signing through [SignPath](https://about.signpath.io) from Zuke builds, and `signtool verify` to check the result.

tasks.name: SigntoolTasks
tasks.doc: Typed task functions for the Windows SDK's `signtool`.

tasks.name: verify
tasks.doc:
Check a file's Authenticode signature with `signtool verify`; a file that
is unsigned or fails the policy exits non-zero, which throws unless
`.noThrow()` is set.

tasks.name: SignPathTasks
tasks.doc: Typed task functions for SignPath's code-signing service.

tasks.name: submit
tasks.doc:
Submit a signing request, wait for it to complete, and — with
`.output(path)` — download the signed artifact.

```ts
const { signingRequestId } = await SignPathTasks.submit((s) =>
  s.organizationId(orgId).apiToken(token)
    .projectSlug("zuke").signingPolicySlug("release-signing")
    .gitHubOrigin((g) => g.artifactId(artifactId))
    .timeout("30m").output("dist/signed/zuke.zip")
);
```

tasks.name: status
download

settings.name: SignPathConnectionSettings
settings.doc: The connection half of every SignPath call's settings.

setters.name: organizationId
setters.doc:
The SignPath organization id — the GUID in the web app's URLs and under
*Organization settings*. Defaults to the `SIGNPATH_ORGANIZATION_ID`
environment variable.

setters.name: apiToken
setters.doc:
The API token of a SignPath user with submitter permission on the
project's signing policy, sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.
Defaults to the `SIGNPATH_API_TOKEN` environment variable.

The token never reaches a progress line or an error message: every
message this package builds is scrubbed of it. Declare it in the build as
a `parameter(...).secret()` so Zuke masks it in its own output too.

setters.name: apiUrl
setters.doc:
The REST API's base URL, `https://app.signpath.io/Api` by default; the
version and organization (`/v1/<org>/…`) are appended. It carries the
token, so it must be `https:` unless it is loopback or
`ZUKE_ALLOW_INSECURE_URL` is set. The web app's links in errors and
progress lines use the same origin (`<origin>/Web/<org>/…`).

setters.name: requestTimeout
setters.doc: Abort one API call after this long (`"30s"`, or ms); default one minute.

setters.name: downloadTimeout
setters.doc:
Abort a signed-artifact download that has not finished after this long
(`"10m"`, or ms); default five minutes.

setters.name: maxDownloadBytes
setters.doc: Refuse a signed artifact larger than this many bytes; default 2 GiB.

setters.name: retries
setters.doc:
Retry a transient failure this many times (default 3), with a doubling
delay from one second. A status poll or a download is retried after a
network error, a timeout, or HTTP 429, 502, 503 or 504; a submission only
after 429 or 503, the answers that say the request was not processed, so
a retry cannot create a second signing request.

settings.name: SignPathStatusSettings
settings.doc: Settings for `SignPathTasks.status`: the connection and the request's id.

setters.name: signingRequestId
setters.doc: The signing request to read — the GUID `submit` returned. Required.

settings.name: SignPathDownloadSettings
settings.doc:
Settings for `SignPathTasks.download`: the connection, the signing
request's id, and where to write the signed artifact.

setters.name: output
setters.doc:
The file to write the signed artifact to; its directory is created when
missing, and an existing file is replaced. Required.

settings.name: SignPathGitHubOriginSettings
settings.doc:
Where the artifact to sign lives in GitHub Actions. Only the artifact id is
required: the run, repository and token default to the workflow's own
environment (`GITHUB_RUN_ID`, `GITHUB_REPOSITORY`, `GITHUB_TOKEN`).

```ts
await SignPathTasks.submit((s) =>
  s.projectSlug("zuke").signingPolicySlug("release-signing")
    .gitHubOrigin((g) => g.artifactId(artifactId).token(githubToken))
    .output("dist/signed/zuke.zip")
);
```

setters.name: artifactId
setters.doc:
The id of the artifact `actions/upload-artifact` (v4 or later) uploaded —
its `artifact-id` step output. Required.

setters.name: runId
setters.doc: The workflow run the artifact belongs to; defaults to `GITHUB_RUN_ID`.

setters.name: repository
setters.doc: The repository, `owner/name`; defaults to `GITHUB_REPOSITORY`.

setters.name: token
setters.doc:
The GitHub token the connector reads the run and downloads the artifact
with — the workflow's `GITHUB_TOKEN` (with `actions: read` and
`contents: read`) is enough. Defaults to the `GITHUB_TOKEN` environment
variable. It is masked out of every message, like the API token.

The workflow's own token stops working when the workflow ends, so the
task must wait for SignPath to fetch the artifact; `submit` always waits.

setters.name: connectorUrl
setters.doc:
The SignPath GitHub connector to submit through; SignPath's hosted
GitHub.com one by default. Only a self-hosted GitHub Enterprise Server
needs another. It carries the API token, so it must be `https:`.

setters.name: authenticodePolicy
setters.doc:
Verify against the default Authenticode policy (`/pa`) — what a signed
`.exe` or `.msi` needs. Without it `signtool` applies the Windows driver
policy and rejects ordinary code-signing certificates.

setters.name: kernelPolicy
setters.doc: Verify against the kernel-mode driver signing policy (`/kp`).

setters.name: policy
setters.doc: Verify against the policy with this GUID (`/pg`).

setters.name: allSignatures
setters.doc: Verify every signature of a file that carries several (`/all`).

setters.name: signatureIndex
setters.doc: Verify only the signature at this index, from 0 (`/ds`).

setters.name: hash
setters.doc: Look the file up in a catalog only for this digest algorithm (`/hash`).

setters.name: catalog
setters.doc: Verify against this catalog file (`/c`).

setters.name: rootSubjectName
setters.doc:
Require the signing certificate to chain to a root whose subject name
contains this text (`/r`).

setters.name: timestampWarning
setters.doc: Warn when the signature is not timestamped (`/tw`).

setters.name: description
setters.doc: Print the signature's description and URL (`/d`).

setters.name: verbose
setters.doc: Print the signer, the chain and the timestamp (`/v`).

setters.name: debug
setters.doc: Print debugging information (`/debug`).

setters.name: file
setters.doc:
The files to verify (positional), at least one. A relative path that
starts with `-` is passed as `./-…` so it cannot be read as an option; one
that starts with `/` is refused, since `signtool` would read it as an
option and on Windows it means the current drive's root — give a
drive-qualified or a relative path instead.

setters.name: projectSlug
setters.doc: The SignPath project's slug. Required.

setters.name: signingPolicySlug
setters.doc:
The signing policy's slug, such as `release-signing` — it decides the
certificate and whether an approver must sign off. Required.

setters.name: artifactConfigurationSlug
setters.doc:
The artifact configuration's slug — which files inside the artifact are
signed, and how. The project's default configuration when unset.

setters.name: description
setters.doc: A description shown on the request, such as the version being released.

setters.name: parameter
setters.doc:
A user-defined parameter the artifact configuration reads (a version
number to stamp, say). Names are letters, digits, `.`, `-` and `_`.
Repeatable.

setters.name: artifact
setters.doc:
Upload this local file as the artifact (`SubmitWithArtifact`). Exactly one
of `artifact` and gitHubOrigin is required.

SignPath's open-source programme accepts only builds whose origin it can
verify, so for it use gitHubOrigin instead.

setters.name: gitHubOrigin
setters.doc:
Have SignPath fetch the artifact from a GitHub Actions workflow run and
verify its origin. Exactly one of artifact and `gitHubOrigin` is
required.

setters.name: output
setters.doc:
Download the signed artifact to this file once the request completes; its
directory is created when missing. Without it, `submit` only waits.

setters.name: timeout
setters.doc:
Fail with a `SignPathTimeoutError` when the request is not final after
this long (`"30m"`, or ms); default ten minutes. A policy that needs a
manual approval wants longer.

setters.name: pollInterval
setters.doc:
Poll the request's status this often (`"5s"`, or ms; at least one second);
default ten seconds.

packages.name: flutter
packages.summary: `@zuke/flutter` — typed `FlutterTasks` wrappers for the [Flutter](https://flutter.dev) CLI, for use in Zuke builds: analyze, test, build every artifact, manage pub dependencies, and drive devices and the SDK.

tasks.name: FlutterTasks
tasks.doc: Typed task functions for the `flutter` CLI.

tasks.name: analyze
tasks.doc: Analyze the project's Dart code: `flutter analyze`.

tasks.name: test
tasks.doc: Run the unit and widget tests: `flutter test`.

tasks.name: pubGet
tasks.doc: Resolve dependencies: `flutter pub get`.

tasks.name: pubUpgrade
tasks.doc: Upgrade dependencies: `flutter pub upgrade`.

tasks.name: pubOutdated
tasks.doc: List outdated dependencies: `flutter pub outdated`.

tasks.name: pubDeps
tasks.doc: Print the dependency graph: `flutter pub deps`.

tasks.name: pubAdd
tasks.doc: Add dependencies to `pubspec.yaml`: `flutter pub add`.

tasks.name: pubRemove
tasks.doc: Remove dependencies from `pubspec.yaml`: `flutter pub remove`.

tasks.name: clean
tasks.doc: Delete the build and `.dart_tool` directories: `flutter clean`.

tasks.name: create
tasks.doc: Scaffold a project: `flutter create`.

tasks.name: genL10n
tasks.doc: Generate localizations from `l10n.yaml`: `flutter gen-l10n`.

tasks.name: drive
tasks.doc: Run integration tests on a device: `flutter drive`.

tasks.name: install
tasks.doc: Install a built app on a device: `flutter install`.

tasks.name: devices
tasks.doc: List connected devices: `flutter devices`.

tasks.name: doctor
tasks.doc: Check the toolchain: `flutter doctor`.

tasks.name: precache
tasks.doc: Download platform artifacts: `flutter precache`.

tasks.name: config
tasks.doc: Change SDK settings: `flutter config`.

tasks.name: version
tasks.doc: Print the Flutter, Dart and engine versions: `flutter --version`.

settings.name: FlutterSettings
settings.doc: Base for all `flutter` settings: the binary is `flutter`, found on `PATH`.

setters.name: path
setters.doc: A file or directory to analyze (defaults to the project); repeatable.

setters.name: noFatalInfos
setters.doc: Do not fail on info-level issues (`--no-fatal-infos`).

setters.name: noFatalWarnings
setters.doc: Do not fail on warnings (`--no-fatal-warnings`).

setters.name: write
setters.doc: Also write the analysis results to a file (`--write`).

setters.name: machine
setters.doc: Print the devices as JSON (`--machine`).

settings.name: FlutterCompileSettings
settings.doc:
Flags shared by the commands that compile Dart code: `--no-pub`,
`--dart-define`, `--dart-define-from-file` and `--flavor`.

setters.name: noPub
setters.doc: Skip the implicit `flutter pub get` (`--no-pub`).

setters.name: dartDefine
setters.doc: Define a compile-time constant (`--dart-define=name=value`); repeatable.

setters.name: dartDefineFromFile
setters.doc: Read compile-time constants from a JSON or `.env` file (`--dart-define-from-file`); repeatable.

setters.name: flavor
setters.doc: The build flavor, for apps with product flavors or schemes (`--flavor`).

settings.name: FlutterAppSettings
settings.doc:
Compile flags plus the build mode and the entry point (`--target`), shared by
`flutter build` and `flutter drive`.

setters.name: mode
setters.doc: The build mode (`--debug`, `--profile` or `--release`).

setters.name: release
setters.doc: Build in release mode (`--release`).

setters.name: target
setters.doc: The main entry-point file, instead of `lib/main.dart` (`--target`).

settings.name: FlutterDriveSettings
settings.doc: Settings for `flutter drive`, which runs integration tests on a device.

setters.name: driver
setters.doc: The test driver file, e.g. `test_driver/integration_test.dart` (`--driver`).

setters.name: deviceId
setters.doc: The device to run on, e.g. `chrome` or an emulator id (`--device-id`).

setters.name: screenshot
setters.doc: Save a screenshot to this directory if the run fails (`--screenshot`).

settings.name: FlutterInstallSettings
settings.doc: Settings for `flutter install`, which installs a built app on a device.

setters.name: mode
setters.doc: Install the build of this mode (`--debug`, `--profile` or `--release`).

setters.name: flavor
setters.doc: Install this build flavor (`--flavor`).

setters.name: deviceId
setters.doc: The device to install on (`--device-id`).

setters.name: useApplicationBinary
setters.doc: Install this prebuilt binary instead (`--use-application-binary`).

setters.name: uninstallOnly
setters.doc: Only uninstall the app (`--uninstall-only`).

settings.name: FlutterCommandSettings
settings.doc:
Settings for a flagless command: `flutter clean`, or `flutter gen-l10n`
(configured by `l10n.yaml`). Extra flags go through `.args()`.

setters.name: dir
setters.doc: The directory to create the project in; required.

setters.name: org
setters.doc: The reverse-domain organization, e.g. `com.example` (`--org`).

setters.name: projectName
setters.doc: The Dart package name, instead of the directory's (`--project-name`).

setters.name: description
setters.doc: The project description (`--description`).

setters.name: template
setters.doc: The template: `app`, `module`, `package`, `plugin`, … (`--template`).

setters.name: platform
setters.doc: A platform to scaffold, e.g. `android` or `web` (`--platforms`); repeatable.

setters.name: empty
setters.doc: Scaffold a minimal app without the counter sample (`--empty`).

setters.name: json
setters.doc: Print the dependency graph as JSON (`--json`).

setters.name: offline
setters.doc: Resolve from the local pub cache only (`--offline`).

setters.name: enforceLockfile
setters.doc: Fail rather than change `pubspec.lock` (`--enforce-lockfile`).

setters.name: json
setters.doc: Print machine-readable JSON (`--json`).

setters.name: showAll
setters.doc: Include packages that are already up to date (`--show-all`).

settings.name: FlutterPubPackagesSettings
settings.doc: Settings for `flutter pub add` and `flutter pub remove`.

setters.name: package
setters.doc:
A package to add or remove; repeatable, at least one is required. For
`add` it takes pub's descriptor syntax: `http`, `http:^1.2.0`, or
`dev:mocktail` for a dev dependency.

setters.name: package
setters.doc: Upgrade only this package (defaults to all); repeatable.

setters.name: majorVersions
setters.doc: Also raise constraints in `pubspec.yaml` across majors (`--major-versions`).

setters.name: tighten
setters.doc: Raise lower bounds in `pubspec.yaml` to the resolved versions (`--tighten`).

setters.name: enable
setters.doc: Turn a feature on, e.g. `web` → `--enable-web`; repeatable.

setters.name: disable
setters.doc: Turn a feature off, e.g. `web` → `--no-enable-web`; repeatable.

setters.name: androidSdk
setters.doc: The Android SDK directory (`--android-sdk`).

setters.name: noAnalytics
setters.doc: Turn analytics reporting off (`--no-analytics`).

setters.name: clearFeatures
setters.doc: Reset every feature flag to its default (`--clear-features`).

setters.name: verbose
setters.doc: Show full details for every check (`--verbose`).

settings.name: FlutterPrecacheSettings
settings.doc: Settings for `flutter precache`, which downloads platform artifacts.

setters.name: platform
setters.doc: Fetch a platform's artifacts, e.g. `android` → `--android`; repeatable.

setters.name: force
setters.doc: Re-download even when cached (`--force`).

setters.name: machine
setters.doc: Print the versions as JSON (`--machine`).

setters.name: path
setters.doc: A test file or directory to run (defaults to `test/`); repeatable.

setters.name: coverage
setters.doc: Collect coverage into `coverage/lcov.info` (`--coverage`).

setters.name: coveragePath
setters.doc: Where to write the lcov coverage report (`--coverage-path`).

setters.name: mergeCoverage
setters.doc: Merge with the existing coverage report (`--merge-coverage`).

setters.name: name
setters.doc: Run only tests whose name matches a regular expression (`--name`); repeatable.

setters.name: plainName
setters.doc: Run only tests whose name contains a string (`--plain-name`); repeatable.

setters.name: tags
setters.doc: Run only tests with a tag expression (`--tags`).

setters.name: excludeTags
setters.doc: Skip tests matching a tag expression (`--exclude-tags`).

setters.name: concurrency
setters.doc: How many test suites to run at once (`--concurrency`).

setters.name: reporter
setters.doc: The console reporter: `compact`, `expanded`, `github`, `json`, … (`--reporter`).

setters.name: fileReporter
setters.doc: Also write a reporter's output to a file, e.g. `json:report.json` (`--file-reporter`).

setters.name: updateGoldens
setters.doc: Rewrite golden files instead of comparing against them (`--update-goldens`).

setters.name: platform
setters.doc: Run on a platform other than the VM, e.g. `chrome` (`--platform`).

setters.name: randomizeOrderingSeed
setters.doc: Shuffle test order with a seed, or `random` (`--test-randomize-ordering-seed`).

setters.name: timeout
setters.doc: The default per-test timeout, e.g. `30s` or `2x` (`--timeout`).

setters.name: shard
setters.doc:
Run one shard of the suite: `shard(index, total)` renders
`--total-shards total --shard-index index`, with `index` from 0.

packages.name: dart
packages.summary: `@zuke/dart` — typed `DartTasks` wrappers for the [Dart](https://dart.dev) CLI, for use in Zuke builds: analyze, format, fix and test Dart code, compile it to every target, generate docs, scaffold and run programs, and manage pub dependencies.

tasks.name: DartTasks
tasks.doc: Typed task functions for the `dart` CLI.

tasks.name: analyze
tasks.doc: Analyze the project's Dart code: `dart analyze`.

tasks.name: format
tasks.doc: Format Dart code, or check it with `.setExitIfChanged()`: `dart format`.

tasks.name: fix
tasks.doc: Apply analyzer fixes: `dart fix`.

tasks.name: test
tasks.doc: Run the tests: `dart test`.

tasks.name: run
tasks.doc: Run a Dart program or package executable: `dart run`.

tasks.name: doc
tasks.doc: Generate API documentation: `dart doc`.

tasks.name: create
tasks.doc: Scaffold a project: `dart create`.

tasks.name: pubGet
tasks.doc: Resolve dependencies: `dart pub get`.

tasks.name: pubUpgrade
tasks.doc: Upgrade dependencies: `dart pub upgrade`.

tasks.name: pubDowngrade
tasks.doc: Downgrade dependencies to their lowest allowed versions: `dart pub downgrade`.

tasks.name: pubOutdated
tasks.doc: List outdated dependencies: `dart pub outdated`.

tasks.name: pubDeps
tasks.doc: Print the dependency graph: `dart pub deps`.

tasks.name: pubAdd
tasks.doc: Add dependencies to `pubspec.yaml`: `dart pub add`.

tasks.name: pubRemove
tasks.doc: Remove dependencies from `pubspec.yaml`: `dart pub remove`.

tasks.name: pubPublish
tasks.doc: Publish the package to pub.dev: `dart pub publish`.

tasks.name: info
tasks.doc: Print diagnostic details about the SDK: `dart info`.

tasks.name: version
tasks.doc: Print the Dart SDK version: `dart --version`.

settings.name: DartSettings
settings.doc: Base for all `dart` settings: the binary is `dart`, found on `PATH`.

setters.name: path
setters.doc: A file or directory to analyze (defaults to the current one); repeatable.

setters.name: fatalInfos
setters.doc: Treat info-level issues as fatal (`--fatal-infos`).

setters.name: noFatalWarnings
setters.doc: Do not fail on warnings (`--no-fatal-warnings`).

setters.name: format
setters.doc: The output format: `default`, `json` or `machine` (`--format`).

setters.name: packages
setters.doc: The package resolution file to use (`--packages`).

settings.name: DartFormatSettings
settings.doc:
Settings for `dart format`. With no `.path()` the current directory is
formatted: `dart format` itself would read stdin instead, and in CI — no
terminal, empty stdin — a `.setExitIfChanged()` check would pass vacuously.

setters.name: path
setters.doc: A file or directory to format (defaults to `.`); repeatable.

setters.name: output
setters.doc: What to do with formatted code: `write` (default), `show`, `json` or `none` (`--output`).

setters.name: setExitIfChanged
setters.doc: Exit with code 1 when any file would change — the CI check (`--set-exit-if-changed`).

setters.name: lineLength
setters.doc: Wrap lines longer than this (`--line-length`).

setters.name: show
setters.doc: Which files to list: `all`, `changed` (default) or `none` (`--show`).

setters.name: summary
setters.doc: The summary to print: `line` (default), `profile` or `none` (`--summary`).

setters.name: followLinks
setters.doc: Follow symbolic links into directories (`--follow-links`).

setters.name: languageVersion
setters.doc: The language version to parse as, e.g. `3.3` (`--language-version`).

setters.name: enableExperiment
setters.doc: Enable an experimental language feature (`--enable-experiment`); repeatable.

setters.name: dir
setters.doc: The directory to create the project in; required.

setters.name: template
setters.doc: The project template, instead of `console` (`--template`).

setters.name: noPub
setters.doc: Skip the implicit `dart pub get` (`--no-pub`).

setters.name: force
setters.doc: Create into a directory that already exists (`--force`).

setters.name: dir
setters.doc: The package directory to document (defaults to the current one).

setters.name: output
setters.doc: Where to write the generated docs, instead of `doc/api` (`--output`).

setters.name: validateLinks
setters.doc: Check the generated docs for broken links (`--validate-links`).

setters.name: dryRun
setters.doc: Report what would be documented without writing files (`--dry-run`).

setters.name: dir
setters.doc: The directory to fix (defaults to the current one).

setters.name: apply
setters.doc: Apply the proposed fixes (`--apply`). Without it or `.dryRun()`, `dart fix` only prints usage.

setters.name: dryRun
setters.doc: List the proposed fixes without applying them (`--dry-run`).

setters.name: code
setters.doc: Apply only the fix for one diagnostic code (`--code`); repeatable.

settings.name: DartInfoSettings
settings.doc: Settings for `dart info`, which prints diagnostic details about the SDK.

setters.name: noRemoveFilePaths
setters.doc: Keep file paths in the output instead of redacting them (`--no-remove-file-paths`).

setters.name: style
setters.doc: The layout: `compact`, `tree` (default) or `list` (`--style`).

setters.name: noDev
setters.doc: Leave dev dependencies out (`--no-dev`).

setters.name: executables
setters.doc: List the executables the dependencies expose instead (`--executables`).

setters.name: json
setters.doc: Print the dependency graph as JSON (`--json`).

setters.name: package
setters.doc: Downgrade only this package (defaults to all); repeatable.

setters.name: offline
setters.doc: Resolve from the local pub cache only (`--offline`).

setters.name: dryRun
setters.doc: Report what would change without changing it (`--dry-run`).

setters.name: tighten
setters.doc: Lower the constraints in `pubspec.yaml` to the resolved versions (`--tighten`).

setters.name: offline
setters.doc: Resolve from the local pub cache only (`--offline`).

setters.name: enforceLockfile
setters.doc: Fail rather than change `pubspec.lock` (`--enforce-lockfile`).

setters.name: dryRun
setters.doc: Report what would change without changing it (`--dry-run`).

setters.name: noPrecompile
setters.doc: Skip precompiling executables (`--no-precompile`).

setters.name: json
setters.doc: Print machine-readable JSON (`--json`).

setters.name: showAll
setters.doc: Include packages that are already up to date (`--show-all`).

setters.name: noDevDependencies
setters.doc: Leave dev dependencies out (`--no-dev-dependencies`).

setters.name: noTransitive
setters.doc: Leave transitive dependencies out (`--no-transitive`).

setters.name: prereleases
setters.doc: Include prereleases when looking for newer versions (`--prereleases`).

settings.name: DartPubPackagesSettings
settings.doc: Settings for `dart pub add` and `dart pub remove`.

setters.name: package
setters.doc:
A package to add or remove; repeatable, at least one is required. For
`add` it takes pub's descriptor syntax: `http`, `http:^1.2.0`, or
`dev:mocktail` for a dev dependency.

setters.name: offline
setters.doc: Resolve from the local pub cache only (`--offline`).

setters.name: dryRun
setters.doc: Report what would change without changing it (`--dry-run`).

setters.name: dryRun
setters.doc: Validate the package without uploading it (`--dry-run`).

setters.name: force
setters.doc: Publish without the confirmation prompt — what CI needs (`--force`).

setters.name: skipValidation
setters.doc: Publish even when validation reports warnings (`--skip-validation`).

setters.name: package
setters.doc: Upgrade only this package (defaults to all); repeatable.

setters.name: offline
setters.doc: Resolve from the local pub cache only (`--offline`).

setters.name: dryRun
setters.doc: Report what would change without changing it (`--dry-run`).

setters.name: majorVersions
setters.doc: Also raise constraints in `pubspec.yaml` across majors (`--major-versions`).

setters.name: tighten
setters.doc: Raise lower bounds in `pubspec.yaml` to the resolved versions (`--tighten`).

setters.name: unlockTransitive
setters.doc: Also upgrade the transitive dependencies of the named packages (`--unlock-transitive`).

settings.name: DartVmSettings
settings.doc:
Flags shared by the commands that load Dart code into the VM — `compile`
and `run`: `--define`, `--enable-asserts`, `--enable-experiment`,
`--packages` and `--verbosity`. Valued options render as `--flag=value`:
`dart compile js` hands its argv to dart2js, whose parser accepts only that
spelling, and Dart's `args` package accepts it everywhere else.

setters.name: define
setters.doc: Define an environment declaration (`--define=name=value`); repeatable.

setters.name: enableAsserts
setters.doc: Enable assert statements (`--enable-asserts`).

setters.name: enableExperiment
setters.doc: Enable an experimental language feature (`--enable-experiment`); repeatable.

setters.name: packages
setters.doc: The package resolution file to use (`--packages`).

setters.name: verbosity
setters.doc: How much to print: `error`, `warning`, `info` or `all` (`--verbosity`).

settings.name: DartRunSettings
settings.doc:
Settings for `dart run`. The entry point is the last token the settings
build, so anything passed through `.args()` lands after it and reaches the
program, not the VM — without an `.entry()`, the first `.args()` token is
what `dart run` takes as the program, exactly as on the command line.

setters.name: entry
setters.doc:
The Dart file to run, or a package executable such as `build_runner` or
`test:test`. Without one, `dart run` runs the current package's own
executable.

setters.name: observe
setters.doc:
Start the VM service with the debugging conveniences and pause on start
(`--observe=<port>[/<bind-address>]`). The value is attached with `=`
because `dart run` reads the option's value from the next token, which
would otherwise be the entry point.

setters.name: enableVmService
setters.doc: Start the VM service without pausing (`--enable-vm-service=<port>[/<bind-address>]`).

setters.name: path
setters.doc: A test file or directory to run (defaults to `test/`); repeatable.

setters.name: name
setters.doc: Run only tests whose name matches a regular expression (`--name`); repeatable.

setters.name: plainName
setters.doc: Run only tests whose name contains a string (`--plain-name`); repeatable.

setters.name: tags
setters.doc: Run only tests with a tag expression (`--tags`).

setters.name: excludeTags
setters.doc: Skip tests matching a tag expression (`--exclude-tags`).

setters.name: preset
setters.doc: Apply a preset from `dart_test.yaml` (`--preset`); repeatable.

setters.name: runSkipped
setters.doc: Run skipped tests too (`--run-skipped`).

setters.name: failFast
setters.doc: Stop after the first failure (`--fail-fast`).

setters.name: platform
setters.doc: Run on a platform, e.g. `vm`, `chrome` or `node` (`--platform`); repeatable.

setters.name: compiler
setters.doc: The compiler for a platform, e.g. `dart2js`, `dart2wasm` or `kernel` (`--compiler`); repeatable.

setters.name: concurrency
setters.doc: How many test suites to run at once (`--concurrency`).

setters.name: timeout
setters.doc: The default per-test timeout, e.g. `30s` or `2x` (`--timeout`).

setters.name: coverage
setters.doc: Collect coverage into a directory of JSON reports (`--coverage`).

setters.name: reporter
setters.doc: The console reporter: `compact`, `expanded`, `failures-only`, `github`, `json` or `silent` (`--reporter`).

setters.name: fileReporter
setters.doc: Also write a reporter's output to a file, e.g. `json:report.json` (`--file-reporter`).

setters.name: randomizeOrderingSeed
setters.doc: Shuffle test order with a seed, or `random` (`--test-randomize-ordering-seed`).

setters.name: ignoreTimeouts
setters.doc: Do not stop a test at its timeout (`--ignore-timeouts`).

setters.name: noColor
setters.doc: Print stack traces without colour codes (`--no-color`).

setters.name: shard
setters.doc:
Run one shard of the suite: `shard(index, total)` renders
`--total-shards total --shard-index index`, with `index` from 0.

packages.name: prometheus
packages.summary: A typed client for the Prometheus HTTP API, for Zuke builds.

tasks.name: PrometheusTasks
tasks.doc:
The Prometheus HTTP API as tasks
(<https://prometheus.io/docs/prometheus/latest/querying/api/>).

tasks.name: query
tasks.doc:
Evaluate an instant query (`/api/v1/query`).

```ts
const result = await PrometheusTasks.query((s) =>
  s.url("https://prometheus.internal").bearerToken(token)
    .query('sum(rate(http_requests_total{code=~"5.."}[5m]))')
);
```

tasks.name: queryRange
tasks.doc: Evaluate a range query (`/api/v1/query_range`); the answer is a matrix.

tasks.name: series
tasks.doc: Find the series matching selectors (`/api/v1/series`).

tasks.name: labels
tasks.doc: List label names (`/api/v1/labels`).

tasks.name: labelValues
tasks.doc: List one label's values (`/api/v1/label/<label_name>/values`).

tasks.name: metadata
tasks.doc: Read metric metadata (`/api/v1/metadata`), keyed by metric name.

tasks.name: targets
tasks.doc: Read target discovery state (`/api/v1/targets`).

tasks.name: rules
tasks.doc: Read the loaded alerting and recording rules (`/api/v1/rules`).

tasks.name: alerts
tasks.doc: Read the active alerts (`/api/v1/alerts`).

tasks.name: buildInfo
tasks.doc: Read the server's build information (`/api/v1/status/buildinfo`).

tasks.name: healthy
tasks.doc:
Probe `/-/healthy`: `true` on 2xx, `false` on 503, and a
`PrometheusApiError` on any other status — a 401 is a credential
problem, not an unhealthy server.

tasks.name: ready
tasks.doc:
Probe `/-/ready`: `true` once the server serves queries, `false` while it
answers 503, and a `PrometheusApiError` on any other status.

tasks.name: value
tasks.doc:
The single number an instant query returned — a scalar, or a vector of
exactly one float sample — failing clearly on an empty or multi-sample
vector, a matrix, a string or a native histogram. `NaN` is returned as
`NaN`, which compares false both ways — gate with `!(v <= max)`.

```ts
const ratio = PrometheusTasks.value(await PrometheusTasks.query((s) => …));
```

tasks.name: samples
tasks.doc:
Every float sample of an instant query, with its labels: a vector's
elements, or a scalar as one unlabelled sample. An empty vector is an
empty list; a matrix, string or native histogram fails.

setters.name: region
setters.doc:
The workspace's region, such as `us-east-1`; defaults to `AWS_REGION`,
then `AWS_DEFAULT_REGION`.

setters.name: profile
setters.doc:
Read static keys from this profile of the shared credentials and config
files (`~/.aws/credentials`, `~/.aws/config`) instead of searching the
default chain.

setters.name: accessKey
setters.doc: Sign with this access key instead of searching the default chain.

setters.name: scope
setters.doc: The scope to request, replacing `https://prometheus.monitor.azure.com/.default`.

setters.name: tenantId
setters.doc: The Microsoft Entra tenant (directory) id; defaults to `AZURE_TENANT_ID`.

setters.name: clientId
setters.doc:
The application's client id — or, for a user-assigned managed identity,
the identity's; defaults to `AZURE_CLIENT_ID`.

setters.name: authorityHost
setters.doc:
The Microsoft Entra authority, such as `https://login.microsoftonline.us`
for Azure Government; defaults to `AZURE_AUTHORITY_HOST`, then
`https://login.microsoftonline.com`.

setters.name: clientSecret
setters.doc:
Use a service principal's client secret (the client-credentials grant).
The secret defaults to `AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET`.

setters.name: workloadIdentity
setters.doc:
Use workload identity federation: the Kubernetes service-account token
in `tokenFile` (default `AZURE_FEDERATED_TOKEN_FILE`) is the client
assertion, read afresh on every token request since it is rotated.

setters.name: managedIdentity
setters.doc:
Use the managed identity of the VM, App Service or Functions app the
build runs on. Pass a user-assigned identity's client id, or leave it
out for `clientId(...)` / `AZURE_CLIENT_ID`, and failing those the
system-assigned identity.

settings.name: PrometheusConnectionSettings
settings.doc: The connection half of every Prometheus call's settings.

setters.name: url
setters.doc:
The Prometheus base URL, such as `https://prometheus.internal`. A path or
query string it carries — a proxy prefix, a tenant parameter — is kept,
and the endpoint path is appended. Userinfo in the URL
(`https://user:pass@host`) is taken off the URL and sent as basic auth.
When the call carries any credential — a configured source, or that
userinfo — the URL must be `https:` unless it is loopback, or
`ZUKE_ALLOW_INSECURE_URL` is set, since a plaintext request hands the
credential to anyone on the path. An unauthenticated URL may be plaintext,
as an in-cluster `http://prometheus.monitoring.svc:9090` usually is.

setters.name: bearerToken
setters.doc: Authenticate with `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

setters.name: basicAuth
setters.doc: Authenticate with HTTP basic auth (`Authorization: Basic …`).

setters.name: header
setters.doc:
Send a fixed header, such as a tenant id (`X-Scope-OrgID`). A plain
header does not make the call credentialed, so an in-cluster
`http://` Mimir, Cortex or Thanos with a tenant header keeps working —
except `Authorization`, `Proxy-Authorization`, `Cookie`, and a name core's
URL redactor treats as credential-bearing (`X-API-Key`, `X-Auth-Token`:
names containing `key`, `token`, `secret`, `auth`, `pass` and the like),
which count as credentials. For an API key under any other name use
secretHeader. The value is masked in errors either way (when eight
or more characters long).

setters.name: secretHeader
setters.doc:
Send a fixed header that carries a credential — an API key such as
`X-API-Key`. Like `bearerToken`, it makes the call credentialed, so the
URL must be `https:` unless it is loopback, and its value is masked in
errors.

setters.name: google
setters.doc:
Authenticate to Google Cloud Managed Service for Prometheus with an
OAuth access token from Application Default Credentials — no `gcloud`
needed. The search order is `credentialsFile(...)`, else the file
`GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` names; then gcloud's
`application_default_credentials.json`; then the GCE / GKE metadata
server. A file may be a `service_account` key, an `authorized_user`
gcloud login, or an `external_account` workload identity federation
configuration with a `file` or `url` subject-token source. The scope
defaults to `monitoring.read`; the token is cached until shortly before
it expires.

```ts
s.url("https://monitoring.googleapis.com/v1/projects/my-project/location/global/prometheus")
  .google()
```

setters.name: azure
setters.doc:
Authenticate to Azure Monitor managed service for Prometheus with a
Microsoft Entra ID token for
`https://prometheus.monitor.azure.com/.default` — no `az` needed. Unless
a credential is chosen, the first the environment configures is used:
client secret (`AZURE_TENANT_ID`, `AZURE_CLIENT_ID`,
`AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET`), then workload identity (`AZURE_TENANT_ID`,
`AZURE_CLIENT_ID`, `AZURE_FEDERATED_TOKEN_FILE`), then managed identity
(App Service's `IDENTITY_ENDPOINT`, else the VM's IMDS). The token is
cached until shortly before it expires.

```ts
s.url("https://my-amw.eastus.prometheus.monitor.azure.com")
  .azure((a) => a.managedIdentity(clientId))
```

setters.name: sigv4
setters.doc:
Sign every request with AWS Signature Version 4 for Amazon Managed
Service for Prometheus (service `aps`) — no `aws` CLI needed. The region
is `region(...)`, else `AWS_REGION` / `AWS_DEFAULT_REGION`. Credentials
come from `accessKey(...)` or `profile(...)` when set, else the chain:
the `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID` environment, the shared files' profile, web
identity (`AWS_WEB_IDENTITY_TOKEN_FILE` + `AWS_ROLE_ARN`), the ECS / EKS
Pod Identity container endpoint, then EC2 IMDSv2. Configure it after any
other source, so it signs the headers they add.

```ts
s.url("https://aps-workspaces.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/workspaces/ws-1234")
  .sigv4((a) => a.region("us-east-1"))
```

setters.name: requestTimeout
setters.doc:
How long the call may take, end to end (`"10s"`, or ms; default 30 s).
Client-side: the query's own `timeout` parameter is separate.

setters.name: maxResponseBytes
setters.doc:
The largest response body to read, in bytes (default 64 MiB). A larger
one fails the call rather than being buffered whole.

setters.name: scopes
setters.doc:
The OAuth scopes to request, replacing the default
`https://www.googleapis.com/auth/monitoring.read`. A gcloud user
credential (`authorized_user`) carries the scopes it was granted at
`gcloud auth application-default login` and ignores these.

setters.name: credentialsFile
setters.doc:
Read this credentials file — a service-account key, a gcloud user
credential, or a workload identity federation configuration — instead of
searching Application Default Credentials.

setters.name: quotaProject
setters.doc:
The project charged for the request's quota, sent as
`x-goog-user-project`. Defaults to the credentials file's
`quota_project_id`, which `gcloud auth application-default
set-quota-project` writes.

settings.name: PrometheusSelectionSettings
settings.doc: What the series, label-name and label-value endpoints share.

setters.name: match
setters.doc: Add series selectors (`match[]`), such as `up` or `{job="api"}`.

setters.name: start
setters.doc: The start time (`start`): a `Date`, Unix seconds, or RFC 3339 text.

setters.name: end
setters.doc: The end time (`end`): a `Date`, Unix seconds, or RFC 3339 text.

setters.name: limit
setters.doc: The most results to return (`limit`); `0` means no limit.

setters.name: httpMethod
setters.doc: Send the parameters as a `POST` form (the default) or in a `GET` URL.

setters.name: labelName
setters.doc:
The label whose values to list. Any name is accepted: one outside the
classic `[a-zA-Z_:][a-zA-Z0-9_:]*` form (a UTF-8 name such as
`http.status_code`) is sent in the API's `U__` value-encoding escape, so
nothing in the name can reach the URL path as a separator.

setters.name: limit
setters.doc: The most metrics to return (`limit`).

setters.name: limitPerMetric
setters.doc: The most metadata entries per metric (`limit_per_metric`).

setters.name: metric
setters.doc: Only this metric's metadata (`metric`).

settings.name: PrometheusSeriesSettings
settings.doc: Settings for finding series by matchers (`/api/v1/series`).

setters.name: httpMethod
setters.doc: Send the parameters as a `POST` form (the default) or in a `GET` URL.

settings.name: PrometheusExpressionSettings
settings.doc: What an instant and a range query share: the expression and its limits.

setters.name: query
setters.doc: The PromQL expression (`query`).

setters.name: timeout
setters.doc:
The evaluation timeout (`timeout`), such as `"30s"` — capped by the
server's `-query.timeout`. The client-side limit is `requestTimeout`.

setters.name: limit
setters.doc: The most series to return (`limit`); `0` means no limit.

setters.name: lookbackDelta
setters.doc: Override the lookback period for this query (`lookback_delta`).

setters.name: httpMethod
setters.doc: Send the parameters as a `POST` form (the default) or in a `GET` URL.

setters.name: start
setters.doc: The inclusive start (`start`): a `Date`, Unix seconds, or RFC 3339 text.

setters.name: end
setters.doc: The inclusive end (`end`): a `Date`, Unix seconds, or RFC 3339 text.

setters.name: step
setters.doc: The resolution step (`step`): `"15s"`, or a number of seconds.

setters.name: time
setters.doc: The evaluation time (`time`): a `Date`, Unix seconds, or RFC 3339 text.

setters.name: type
setters.doc: Only alerting (`"alert"`) or only recording (`"record"`) rules (`type`).

setters.name: ruleName
setters.doc: Only rules with these names (`rule_name[]`).

setters.name: ruleGroup
setters.doc: Only rules in these groups (`rule_group[]`).

setters.name: file
setters.doc: Only rules from these files (`file[]`).

setters.name: match
setters.doc: Only rules whose configured labels match these selectors (`match[]`).

setters.name: excludeAlerts
setters.doc: Leave out each rule's active alerts (`exclude_alerts=true`).

setters.name: groupLimit
setters.doc: At most this many rule groups per page (`group_limit`).

setters.name: groupNextToken
setters.doc: Continue from a previous page's `groupNextToken` (`group_next_token`).

setters.name: state
setters.doc: Only active or only dropped targets (`state`); both by default.
